Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "AirAsia delays staff salary payments to end of month, internal email shows"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. The planned workforce adjustment will not affect passenger flights, bookings, or other services, AirAsia Philippines General Manager and President...
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. articles.title: 200-year-old Taj Mahal marble slab to be auctioned in U.K.
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The rectangular slab is estimated to fetch between 20,000 and 30,000 pounds (₹24-36 lakh approximately)

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: An intricate floral-bordered marble slab taken from the Taj Mahal in Agra by an officer of the East India Company is set to be auctioned in the U.K. next month. The rectangular slab, one of two that Colonel Pownoll Phipps collected in 1816 at the end of his tenure as superintendent of the repairs of the buildings in and around Agra, is estimated to fetch between 20,000 and 30,000 pounds (₹24-36 lakh approximately). It is being offered as part of the Islamic and Indian Art sale by Lyon and Turnbull auctioneers on December 9. “The marble slab is accompanied by a vintage black and white photograph of the Taj Mahal and two letters — one printed by the grandson of Colonel Pownoll and one handwritten by the Marquess of Bath,” the auction notes state. The colonel’s son's memoirs quote that his father found them in a ‘souterrain’, or underground area, at the Taj Mahal and that he thought they were intended for the repairs to the iconic Mughal-era monument. Colonel Pownoll Phipps was born in Devon, England, in 1780. Hailing from a line of soldiers since the early 17th century, he joined the East India Company as a cadet in the Bengal Army in 1799. After battling troops in Egypt, Phipps returned to India, where he quickly rose through the ranks, becoming Fort-Adjutant and Barrack-Master at Agra in 1809, where he remained for the next seven years. articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: The rectangular slab is estimated to fetch between 20,000 and 30,000 pounds (₹24-36 lakh approximately)
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: An intricate floral-bordered marble slab taken from the Taj Mahal in Agra by an officer of the East India Company is set to be auctioned in the U.K. next month. The rectangular slab, one of two that Colonel Pownoll Phipps collected in 1816 at the end of his tenure as superintendent of the repairs of the buildings in and around Agra, is estimated to fetch between 20,000 and 30,000 pounds (₹24-36 lakh approximately). It is being offered as part of the Islamic and Indian Art sale by Lyon and Turnbull auctioneers on December 9. “The marble slab is accompanied by a vintage black and white photograph of the Taj Mahal and two letters — one printed by the grandson of Colonel Pownoll and one handwritten by the Marquess of Bath,” the auction notes state. The colonel’s son's memoirs quote that his father found them in a ‘souterrain’, or underground area, at the Taj Mahal and that he thought they were intended for the repairs to the iconic Mughal-era monument. Colonel Pownoll Phipps was born in Devon, England, in 1780. Hailing from a line of soldiers since the early 17th century, he joined the East India Company as a cadet in the Bengal Army in 1799. After battling troops in Egypt, Phipps returned to India, where he quickly rose through the ranks, becoming Fort-Adjutant and Barrack-Master at Agra in 1809, where he remained for the next seven years. During the colonial era, he was responsible among other things for the care of the Taj Mahal and other historic buildings. “He took this job most seriously and was at times called upon to prevent damage by Europeans looking for keepsakes. As his son wrote, ‘he was once sent for to the Taj, where, in spite of the remonstrances of the sentry, an English lady was insisting on picking agates out of the marble with a steel fork’,” the auctioneers note.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: In 1816, the colonel was chosen by the Governor General of India to become Superintendent of Building in the Lower Provinces, which meant leaving Agra for Kolkata.

articles.title: Donald Trump urges Vladimir Putin to end ‘military aggression’ in Europe
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Donald Trump said he had requested Vladimir Putin when they met in China last week, adding that he thought it would help lead to a deal to end Moscow's grinding war in Ukraine

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: U.S. President Donald Trump said on Thursday (November 26, 2026) he had asked Vladimir Putin to "pull back all military aggression" against Europe, in a fresh shift in tone towards the Russian leader he called his friend just last week. Mr. Trump said he had requested Mr. Putin when they met in China last week, adding that he thought it would help lead to a deal to end Moscow's grinding war in Ukraine. "During my conversations in China with President Vladimir Putin, of Russia, I spent a lot of time talking about the fact that I would like to see President Putin pull back all Military aggression against territories throughout Europe," Mr. Trump said on his Truth Social network. Mr. Trump said he had done so "in the hopes that a Deal can be made between Russia and Ukraine, and made quickly." "I really believe this is a strong possibility," he added. The statement did not specify which territories Mr. Trump meant -- and did not specifically include Ukraine, which Russia invaded in February 2022, kicking off the largest war in Europe since World War II. European nations have been increasingly concerned by what they regard as Russian provocations, including three Russian cruise missiles landing in NATO-member Poland last week. In their joint statement on Wednesday (November 25), Mr. Trump and Mr. Rutte said they "discussed the importance of Russia avoiding any actions that intentionally, or unintentionally, expand the war." In a notable contrast with Mr. Trump's recent criticisms of Ukraine for striking targets deep inside Russia, the U.S. leader made no call for Kyiv to show similar restraint.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Speaking to reporters at his Mar-a-Lago estate in Florida on Thursday (November 26), Mr. Trump said he was unsure if Mr. Putin would be coming to the G20 summit next month in Miami, but "but if he wanted to come, he certainly can."

📰 Donald Trump urges Vladimir Putin to end ‘military aggression’ in Europe

📌 Published: 27 Nov 2026, 01:21:27 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Donald Trump said he had requested Vladimir Putin when they met in China last week, adding that he thought it would help lead to a deal to end Moscow's grinding war in Ukraine

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: U.S. President Donald Trump said on Thursday (November 26, 2026) he had asked Vladimir Putin to "pull back all military aggression" against Europe, in a fresh shift in tone towards the Russian leader he called his friend just last week. Mr. Trump said he had requested Mr. Putin when they met in China last week, adding that he thought it would help lead to a deal to end Moscow's grinding war in Ukraine. "During my conversations in China with President Vladimir Putin, of Russia, I spent a lot of time talking about the fact that I would like to see President Putin pull back all Military aggression against territories throughout Europe," Mr. Trump said on his Truth Social network. Mr. Trump said he had done so "in the hopes that a Deal can be made between Russia and Ukraine, and made quickly." "I really believe this is a strong possibility," he added. The statement did not specify which territories Mr. Trump meant -- and did not specifically include Ukraine, which Russia invaded in February 2022, kicking off the largest war in Europe since World War II. European nations have been increasingly concerned by what they regard as Russian provocations, including three Russian cruise missiles landing in NATO-member Poland last week. In their joint statement on Wednesday (November 25), Mr. Trump and Mr. Rutte said they "discussed the importance of Russia avoiding any actions that intentionally, or unintentionally, expand the war." In a notable contrast with Mr. Trump's recent criticisms of Ukraine for striking targets deep inside Russia, the U.S. leader made no call for Kyiv to show similar restraint.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Speaking to reporters at his Mar-a-Lago estate in Florida on Thursday (November 26), Mr. Trump said he was unsure if Mr. Putin would be coming to the G20 summit next month in Miami, but "but if he wanted to come, he certainly can."

articles.title: Elevated blood sugar during adulthood linked with worse cognition in midlife: study
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The findings suggest that changes in glucose metabolism may affect brain health earlier in adulthood than previously thought

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Young adults with progressively increasing fasting blood sugar may be more likely to have a poor cognitive functioning by midlife, according to a new study that tracked young adults for over three decades. The findings suggest that changes in glucose metabolism may affect brain health earlier in adulthood than previously thought. Participants who developed type 2 diabetes during the study also showed signs of structural brain changes, according to findings published in the Journal of the American Heart Association . "Diabetes is known to affect cognitive function, but cognitive impairment due to diabetes was once believed to happen mostly during childhood among people with Type 1 diabetes or after age 65 in people with Type 2 diabetes," lead author Regina Paradela, a post-doctoral researcher at the University of São Paulo Medical School in São Paulo, Brazil, said. "However, prediabetes and sustained elevated fasting blood sugar levels in adults without type 1 or type 2 diabetes may also have an increased risk of late-life cognitive decline and dementia," Paradela said. The researchers suggested early monitoring and management of blood sugar levels in young adulthood -- 18 to 30 years old -- might be a strategy to preserve brain health. Normal fasting blood glucose is generally below 100 milligrams per decilitre, 100-125 milligrams per decilitre indicates prediabetes and a value over 126 milligrams per decilitre is consistent with Type 2 diabetes. "The fact that increasing glucose levels were associated with poorer cognitive performance, even among people who had not developed Type 2 diabetes during the 30-year study, is very important," Paradela said. "This suggests that changes in glucose metabolism may be relevant to brain health earlier in adulthood than we typically think about," Paradela said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The study is among the first to investigate and compare the association between changes in fasting blood sugar levels from early adulthood to changes in cognition and brain structure in middle age, over approximately 30 years, the researchers said.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #25 of 30 (27 NOV)

📰 Elevated blood sugar during adulthood linked with worse cognition in midlife: study

📌 Published: 27 Nov 2026, 03:25:54 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The findings suggest that changes in glucose metabolism may affect brain health earlier in adulthood than previously thought

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Young adults with progressively increasing fasting blood sugar may be more likely to have a poor cognitive functioning by midlife, according to a new study that tracked young adults for over three decades. The findings suggest that changes in glucose metabolism may affect brain health earlier in adulthood than previously thought. Participants who developed type 2 diabetes during the study also showed signs of structural brain changes, according to findings published in the Journal of the American Heart Association . "Diabetes is known to affect cognitive function, but cognitive impairment due to diabetes was once believed to happen mostly during childhood among people with Type 1 diabetes or after age 65 in people with Type 2 diabetes," lead author Regina Paradela, a post-doctoral researcher at the University of São Paulo Medical School in São Paulo, Brazil, said. "However, prediabetes and sustained elevated fasting blood sugar levels in adults without type 1 or type 2 diabetes may also have an increased risk of late-life cognitive decline and dementia," Paradela said. The researchers suggested early monitoring and management of blood sugar levels in young adulthood -- 18 to 30 years old -- might be a strategy to preserve brain health. Normal fasting blood glucose is generally below 100 milligrams per decilitre, 100-125 milligrams per decilitre indicates prediabetes and a value over 126 milligrams per decilitre is consistent with Type 2 diabetes. "The fact that increasing glucose levels were associated with poorer cognitive performance, even among people who had not developed Type 2 diabetes during the 30-year study, is very important," Paradela said. "This suggests that changes in glucose metabolism may be relevant to brain health earlier in adulthood than we typically think about," Paradela said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The study is among the first to investigate and compare the association between changes in fasting blood sugar levels from early adulthood to changes in cognition and brain structure in middle age, over approximately 30 years, the researchers said.

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: In a time of global tension, digital overload and endless advice about raising children, experts say 2027 calls for a radical rethink: less perfection, more presence

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Prem Kishore occasionally turns to Artificial Intelligence (AI) for help when it comes to raising his six-year-old son. “It’s the big feelings that can be difficult to talk about, because we don’t always have the right words. I usually seek advice from my friends or psychologists, but if they’re not available, I turn to AI,” says the creative professional, 43, who splits his time between Bengaluru and Dubai. Kishore recalls how he visited an AI video generator to create an avatar of a doctor, who chatted with his son about healthy boundaries and consent. As AI becomes more enmeshed in our day-to-day lives, families are turning to it for advice, research and assistance in managing the mental load of modern-day parenting. A 2026 consumer trends report by GIPSI, the research arm of agency Tonic Worldwide, combined search and social media data with a survey of 50,000 people, and found that 52% of Indian Gen Z parents now use AI instead of their usual search engines, and 48% use it as an adviser. In India, Google Gemini recently launched a series of commercials featuring Shah Rukh Khan in which he directs two fathers at very different stages of their parenting journeys towards the chatbot for advice. Apps such as Fambot and AVA seek to help families with administrative tasks by syncing to their calendars, email and online shopping orders. Eighteen years ago, when I first became a parent, Dr. Spock’s Baby and Child Care was the de facto gift to all new parents along with a Johnson & Johnson baby care set. I kept the book for a number of years after I had my second child and referred to it frequently. But today, new parents can seek advice from podcasts, influencers, online communities and yes, AI chatbots. There is a lot of advice out there, available in seconds. But how much of it is actually helping parents? Author-editor Sanjana Kapur, 40, who’s raising a nine-year-old in Bengaluru, admits that parenting feels a little nerve-racking today. “There’s so much information out there, that you’re constantly worrying if you’re making the right decision, or how even your smallest reaction will affect your child. The world has become such a complicated place, and parents are nervous even when kids are at school now,” she admits.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The Hindu Sunday Magazine / children / parent and child / technology (general) / OpenAI / Artificial Intelligence / human interest

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #26 of 30 (27 NOV)

📰 Parenting in an anxious age: What does ‘good enough’ look like?

📌 Published: 27 Nov 2026, 02:37:18 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: In a time of global tension, digital overload and endless advice about raising children, experts say 2027 calls for a radical rethink: less perfection, more presence

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Prem Kishore occasionally turns to Artificial Intelligence (AI) for help when it comes to raising his six-year-old son. “It’s the big feelings that can be difficult to talk about, because we don’t always have the right words. I usually seek advice from my friends or psychologists, but if they’re not available, I turn to AI,” says the creative professional, 43, who splits his time between Bengaluru and Dubai. Kishore recalls how he visited an AI video generator to create an avatar of a doctor, who chatted with his son about healthy boundaries and consent. As AI becomes more enmeshed in our day-to-day lives, families are turning to it for advice, research and assistance in managing the mental load of modern-day parenting. A 2026 consumer trends report by GIPSI, the research arm of agency Tonic Worldwide, combined search and social media data with a survey of 50,000 people, and found that 52% of Indian Gen Z parents now use AI instead of their usual search engines, and 48% use it as an adviser. In India, Google Gemini recently launched a series of commercials featuring Shah Rukh Khan in which he directs two fathers at very different stages of their parenting journeys towards the chatbot for advice. Apps such as Fambot and AVA seek to help families with administrative tasks by syncing to their calendars, email and online shopping orders. Eighteen years ago, when I first became a parent, Dr. Spock’s Baby and Child Care was the de facto gift to all new parents along with a Johnson & Johnson baby care set. I kept the book for a number of years after I had my second child and referred to it frequently. But today, new parents can seek advice from podcasts, influencers, online communities and yes, AI chatbots. There is a lot of advice out there, available in seconds. But how much of it is actually helping parents? Author-editor Sanjana Kapur, 40, who’s raising a nine-year-old in Bengaluru, admits that parenting feels a little nerve-racking today. “There’s so much information out there, that you’re constantly worrying if you’re making the right decision, or how even your smallest reaction will affect your child. The world has become such a complicated place, and parents are nervous even when kids are at school now,” she admits.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The Hindu Sunday Magazine / children / parent and child / technology (general) / OpenAI / Artificial Intelligence / human interest

• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Prem Kishore occasionally turns to Artificial Intelligence (AI) for help when it comes to raising his six-year-old son. “It’s the big feelings that can be difficult to talk about, because we don’t always have the right words. I usually seek advice from my friends or psychologists, but if they’re not available, I turn to AI,” says the creative professional, 43, who splits his time between Bengaluru and Dubai. Kishore recalls how he visited an AI video generator to create an avatar of a doctor, who chatted with his son about healthy boundaries and consent. As AI becomes more enmeshed in our day-to-day lives, families are turning to it for advice, research and assistance in managing the mental load of modern-day parenting. A 2026 consumer trends report by GIPSI, the research arm of agency Tonic Worldwide, combined search and social media data with a survey of 50,000 people, and found that 52% of Indian Gen Z parents now use AI instead of their usual search engines, and 48% use it as an adviser. In India, Google Gemini recently launched a series of commercials featuring Shah Rukh Khan in which he directs two fathers at very different stages of their parenting journeys towards the chatbot for advice. Apps such as Fambot and AVA seek to help families with administrative tasks by syncing to their calendars, email and online shopping orders. Eighteen years ago, when I first became a parent, Dr. Spock’s Baby and Child Care was the de facto gift to all new parents along with a Johnson & Johnson baby care set. I kept the book for a number of years after I had my second child and referred to it frequently. But today, new parents can seek advice from podcasts, influencers, online communities and yes, AI chatbots. There is a lot of advice out there, available in seconds. But how much of it is actually helping parents? Author-editor Sanjana Kapur, 40, who’s raising a nine-year-old in Bengaluru, admits that parenting feels a little nerve-racking today. “There’s so much information out there, that you’re constantly worrying if you’re making the right decision, or how even your smallest reaction will affect your child. The world has become such a complicated place, and parents are nervous even when kids are at school now,” she admits.

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: According to the latest IDC report, Motorola has already climbed to become the fifth-largest smartphone brand in India, capturing an 8.8% market share during the third quarter of this year

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Motorola is aiming for the third spot in India’s competitive smartphone market as the Lenovo-owned brand aggressively pivots to premiumisation and seamless connected experiences. The company’s executives outlined their strategic vision during a media visit at their contract partner Dixon (Padget Electronics) facility in Noida, Uttar Pradesh. India’s smartphone market is currently being dominated by Samsung followed by two Chinese players (Vivo and Oppo). If Motorola continues its aggressive push and mix of products, it would be able to replace Oppo to become the third largest smartphone brand in the country. According to the latest IDC report, Motorola has already climbed to become the fifth-largest smartphone brand in India, capturing an 8.8% market share during the third quarter of this year. This growth is heavily anchored in its premium portfolio, which includes the Edge, Razr, and Signature series. Motorola reports that its revenue has surged 20-fold since FY19-20, with nearly 60% now driven entirely by these high-end devices. Fueling this momentum is robust local manufacturing. Motorola’s upcoming premium flagship smartphone, the Motorola Signature 27, will be made at the Noida facility. Alongside Dixon, the brand maintains a strategic manufacturing partnership with Neolync in Tirupati, Andhra Pradesh. Together, these facilities not only fulfill domestic demand but also handle exports to Latin and North American markets. Motorola’s manufacturing expansion has generated a substantial economic footprint, providing direct employment to nearly 8,000 people and creating over 56,000 indirect opportunities spanning manufacturing, sales, and servicing. To support its expanding market presence, Motorola has established an extensive service network across the country. The brand currently covers 716 PIN codes across 620 cities in India, supported by over 846 touch points and 685 dedicated repair centres. Looking ahead, Motorola is doubling down on artificial intelligence, prioritising practical, day-to-day use cases. The company has partnered with Google to integrate Gemini Intelligence into its upcoming Signature 27.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Motorola continues to evolve its proprietary AI assistant, Qira, which is designed to enhance cross-device connectivity and deliver advanced productivity tools for users.

📰 Motorola pivots to premiumisation, aims for third spot in India

📌 Published: 27 Nov 2026, 11:57:52 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: According to the latest IDC report, Motorola has already climbed to become the fifth-largest smartphone brand in India, capturing an 8.8% market share during the third quarter of this year

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Motorola is aiming for the third spot in India’s competitive smartphone market as the Lenovo-owned brand aggressively pivots to premiumisation and seamless connected experiences. The company’s executives outlined their strategic vision during a media visit at their contract partner Dixon (Padget Electronics) facility in Noida, Uttar Pradesh. India’s smartphone market is currently being dominated by Samsung followed by two Chinese players (Vivo and Oppo). If Motorola continues its aggressive push and mix of products, it would be able to replace Oppo to become the third largest smartphone brand in the country. According to the latest IDC report, Motorola has already climbed to become the fifth-largest smartphone brand in India, capturing an 8.8% market share during the third quarter of this year. This growth is heavily anchored in its premium portfolio, which includes the Edge, Razr, and Signature series. Motorola reports that its revenue has surged 20-fold since FY19-20, with nearly 60% now driven entirely by these high-end devices. Fueling this momentum is robust local manufacturing. Motorola’s upcoming premium flagship smartphone, the Motorola Signature 27, will be made at the Noida facility. Alongside Dixon, the brand maintains a strategic manufacturing partnership with Neolync in Tirupati, Andhra Pradesh. Together, these facilities not only fulfill domestic demand but also handle exports to Latin and North American markets. Motorola’s manufacturing expansion has generated a substantial economic footprint, providing direct employment to nearly 8,000 people and creating over 56,000 indirect opportunities spanning manufacturing, sales, and servicing. To support its expanding market presence, Motorola has established an extensive service network across the country. The brand currently covers 716 PIN codes across 620 cities in India, supported by over 846 touch points and 685 dedicated repair centres. Looking ahead, Motorola is doubling down on artificial intelligence, prioritising practical, day-to-day use cases. The company has partnered with Google to integrate Gemini Intelligence into its upcoming Signature 27.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Motorola continues to evolve its proprietary AI assistant, Qira, which is designed to enhance cross-device connectivity and deliver advanced productivity tools for users.

articles.title: Pressure tactics: On the new U.S. tariffs on India
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The new U.S. tariffs must not erode India’s stand on a trade deal

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The latest U.S. tariffs on India are nothing more than a pressure tactic to push for the signing of a trade deal. The U.S. Trade Representative (USTR) has proposed to levy a tariff of 25% for India’s apparent use of strategic excess manufacturing capacity to the detriment of American industry. This is the second-highest tariff rate the USTR has applied across the 14 countries that it has taken action against. The pressure on India does not come from the 25% rate but from the 17% this could be reduced to if it signs a trade deal with the U.S. This latest action is yet another example of how, despite the frothiness of India-U.S. trade relations over the past year and a half, the actual substance has not changed. The 25% rate now proposed, which is net of existing tariffs, is nearly the same as the 26% rate that U.S. President Donald Trump had first announced when he unveiled his ‘Liberation Day’ reciprocal tariffs in April 2025. Indeed, it is exactly the same as the 25% tariff he finally imposed in July 2025, before he imposed an additional 25% for India’s Russian oil imports. The 17% rate is also only marginally lower than the 18% that the two countries had agreed on in their joint statement in February 2026. It is also just one percentage point lower than the tariffs on competitors such as Indonesia and Malaysia. The allegation of India having excess capacity does not hold water. Indeed, were India to have excess manufacturing capacity in any sector, it would be the Government of India that would be the first to announce it with great fanfare, instead of denying it as it did. After all, that has been its aim since 2014. Yet, even a basic assessment of India’s import dependence and the fact that manufacturing’s share in GDP is lower now than a decade ago shows that India is far from having excess manufacturing capacity in any sector. Further, higher tariffs are unlikely to reduce America’s imports of the goods from India that it does depend on. The USTR mentioned generic pharmaceuticals, telecommunication equipment, and renewable energy goods. The first two are items that India has developed expertise in, which is distinct from strategic excess capacity. A relatively small tariff disadvantage will not substantially erode the attractiveness of these Indian products. Renewable energy imports from India have swelled because the U.S. is reducing its purchases from China. Hanging over all of this are the 100% tariffs related to the purchase of Russian oil, which have only temporarily been paused. India has so far held off on signing a deal, and must go ahead with one only if it is convinced that the benefits at least equal the costs.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: USA / India / taxes and duties / manufacturing and engineering / industrial production / trade policy / Russia / oil and gas - upstream activities / Indonesia / Malaysia / imports / pharmaceutical / telecommunication equipment / renewable energy / China

✍️ Editorial & Opinion Paragraph #1 of 30 (27 NOV)

📰 Pressure tactics: On the new U.S. tariffs on India

📌 Published: 27 Nov 2026, 07:59:47 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The new U.S. tariffs must not erode India’s stand on a trade deal

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The latest U.S. tariffs on India are nothing more than a pressure tactic to push for the signing of a trade deal. The U.S. Trade Representative (USTR) has proposed to levy a tariff of 25% for India’s apparent use of strategic excess manufacturing capacity to the detriment of American industry. This is the second-highest tariff rate the USTR has applied across the 14 countries that it has taken action against. The pressure on India does not come from the 25% rate but from the 17% this could be reduced to if it signs a trade deal with the U.S. This latest action is yet another example of how, despite the frothiness of India-U.S. trade relations over the past year and a half, the actual substance has not changed. The 25% rate now proposed, which is net of existing tariffs, is nearly the same as the 26% rate that U.S. President Donald Trump had first announced when he unveiled his ‘Liberation Day’ reciprocal tariffs in April 2025. Indeed, it is exactly the same as the 25% tariff he finally imposed in July 2025, before he imposed an additional 25% for India’s Russian oil imports. The 17% rate is also only marginally lower than the 18% that the two countries had agreed on in their joint statement in February 2026. It is also just one percentage point lower than the tariffs on competitors such as Indonesia and Malaysia. The allegation of India having excess capacity does not hold water. Indeed, were India to have excess manufacturing capacity in any sector, it would be the Government of India that would be the first to announce it with great fanfare, instead of denying it as it did. After all, that has been its aim since 2014. Yet, even a basic assessment of India’s import dependence and the fact that manufacturing’s share in GDP is lower now than a decade ago shows that India is far from having excess manufacturing capacity in any sector. Further, higher tariffs are unlikely to reduce America’s imports of the goods from India that it does depend on. The USTR mentioned generic pharmaceuticals, telecommunication equipment, and renewable energy goods. The first two are items that India has developed expertise in, which is distinct from strategic excess capacity. A relatively small tariff disadvantage will not substantially erode the attractiveness of these Indian products. Renewable energy imports from India have swelled because the U.S. is reducing its purchases from China. Hanging over all of this are the 100% tariffs related to the purchase of Russian oil, which have only temporarily been paused. India has so far held off on signing a deal, and must go ahead with one only if it is convinced that the benefits at least equal the costs.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: USA / India / taxes and duties / manufacturing and engineering / industrial production / trade policy / Russia / oil and gas - upstream activities / Indonesia / Malaysia / imports / pharmaceutical / telecommunication equipment / renewable energy / China

मुक्ति — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Liberation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।

This is the second-highest tariff rate the USTR has applied across the 14 countries that it has taken action against. The pressure on India does not come from the 25% rate but from the 17% this could be reduced to if it signs a trade deal with the U.S. This latest action is yet another example of how, despite the frothiness of India-U.S. trade relations over the past year and a half, the actual substance has not changed. The 25% rate now proposed, which is net of existing tariffs, is nearly the same as the 26% rate that U.S. President Donald Trump had first announced when he unveiled his ‘Liberation Day’ reciprocal tariffs in April 2025. Indeed, it is exactly the same as the 25% tariff he finally imposed in July 2025, before he imposed an additional 25% for India’s Russian oil imports. The 17% rate is also only marginally lower than the 18% that the two countries had agreed on in their joint statement in February 2026. It is also just one percentage point lower than the tariffs on competitors such as Indonesia and Malaysia. The allegation of India having excess capacity does not hold water. Indeed, were India to have excess manufacturing capacity in any sector, it would be the Government of India that would be the first to announce it with great fanfare, instead of denying it as it did. After all, that has been its aim since 2014. Yet, even a basic assessment of India’s import dependence and the fact that manufacturing’s share in GDP is lower now than a decade ago shows that India is far from having excess manufacturing capacity in any sector. Further, higher tariffs are unlikely to reduce America’s imports of the goods from India that it does depend on. The USTR mentioned generic pharmaceuticals, telecommunication equipment, and renewable energy goods. The first two are items that India has developed expertise in, which is distinct from strategic excess capacity. A relatively small tariff disadvantage will not substantially erode the attractiveness of these Indian products. Renewable energy imports from India have swelled because the U.S. is reducing its purchases from China. Hanging over all of this are the 100% tariffs related to the purchase of Russian oil, which have only temporarily been paused. India has so far held off on signing a deal, and must go ahead with one only if it is convinced that the benefits at least equal the costs.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: USA / India / taxes and duties / manufacturing and engineering / industrial production / trade policy / Russia / oil and gas - upstream activities / Indonesia / Malaysia / imports / pharmaceutical / telecommunication equipment / renewable energy / China

articles.title: Indefensible defiance: On Tamil Nadu and Court’s Thirupparankundram order
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Tamil Nadu should have followed Court order without backing Deepathoon claim

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: By defying the Supreme Court’s one-time direction to also light the ceremonial Karthigai Deepam at a stone pillar , claimed by Hindu groups to be a Deepathoon, atop the Thirupparankundram hills, the Tamil Nadu government has disregarded a constitutional body’s authority. Believed to be Lord Murugan’s first abode, the hills have, for centuries , witnessed an intersection of religious faiths, with occasional skirmishes leading to tense flare-ups and legal battles. They house the Arulmigu Subramaniya Swamy, Uchchi Pillaiyar and Kashi Viswanathar temples; Sultan Sikkandar Avulia Dargah; and also Jain beds. Historically, the lamp is lit near the Pillaiyar temple. In 1994-95, the Hindu Munnani precipitated matters, claiming that the moksha deepam (for departed souls) and Karthigai Deepam were being lit at the same place. It demanded the lamp be lit at a pillar, 50 metres from the Dargah. In multiple legal battles, successive governments, backed by hereditary priests (Sthaneeka Bhattars) , opposed the demand. Even in 1862 and 1912, courts had disallowed lamp lighting near the Dargah. The BJP and its affiliates have, since, aggressively weaponised the demand in the name of Hindu religious rights. Against this backdrop, last year, the Madras High Cour t’s Madurai Bench, relying on the 1931 Privy Council ruling on ownership of the hills, held that “for the sake of protecting its property, the [Subramania Swamy] temple management is obliged to light the festival lamp at the Deepathoon” . The DMK government defied the order. Later, a Division Bench upheld the verdict. While staying this order recently, the Supreme Court cited the festival’s proximity to permit the lamp to be lit at the Deepathoon this year alone , clarifying that this did not constitute “essential religious practice”. The State filed a review petition , arguing when no right is recognised prima facie, a direction altering the existing position lacks judicial foundation. On Karthigai Deepam day, November 24, with the review pending, the government walked a tightrope. The Collector assured the High Court of compliance. Yet, the lamp was lit only at the traditional spot . The Collector has now apologised to the Court, blaming the temple’s Board of Trustees for not authorising the proposed lighting team at the Deepathoon. The administration has thus attempted to distinguish its proclaimed intent to comply with judicial directions from customs governed by the trustees. But it remains exposed to the charge of colluding with the temple authorities to breach a judicial mandate. The Deepathoon may be a mischievous prop deployed by self-serving Hindu groups, but the pillar stands on temple property. The State could have permitted the limited lighting, leaving the onus on the Court, without endorsing the Deepathoon claim or compromising religious amity. A democracy can remain healthy only when its constitutional pillars do not collide with one another.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: court / Tamil Nadu / religion and belief / history / Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam / democracy / customs and tradition / constitution

✍️ Editorial & Opinion Paragraph #2 of 30 (27 NOV)

📰 Indefensible defiance: On Tamil Nadu and Court’s Thirupparankundram order

📌 Published: 27 Nov 2026, 12:14:34 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Tamil Nadu should have followed Court order without backing Deepathoon claim

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: By defying the Supreme Court’s one-time direction to also light the ceremonial Karthigai Deepam at a stone pillar , claimed by Hindu groups to be a Deepathoon, atop the Thirupparankundram hills, the Tamil Nadu government has disregarded a constitutional body’s authority. Believed to be Lord Murugan’s first abode, the hills have, for centuries , witnessed an intersection of religious faiths, with occasional skirmishes leading to tense flare-ups and legal battles. They house the Arulmigu Subramaniya Swamy, Uchchi Pillaiyar and Kashi Viswanathar temples; Sultan Sikkandar Avulia Dargah; and also Jain beds. Historically, the lamp is lit near the Pillaiyar temple. In 1994-95, the Hindu Munnani precipitated matters, claiming that the moksha deepam (for departed souls) and Karthigai Deepam were being lit at the same place. It demanded the lamp be lit at a pillar, 50 metres from the Dargah. In multiple legal battles, successive governments, backed by hereditary priests (Sthaneeka Bhattars) , opposed the demand. Even in 1862 and 1912, courts had disallowed lamp lighting near the Dargah. The BJP and its affiliates have, since, aggressively weaponised the demand in the name of Hindu religious rights. Against this backdrop, last year, the Madras High Cour t’s Madurai Bench, relying on the 1931 Privy Council ruling on ownership of the hills, held that “for the sake of protecting its property, the [Subramania Swamy] temple management is obliged to light the festival lamp at the Deepathoon” . The DMK government defied the order. Later, a Division Bench upheld the verdict. While staying this order recently, the Supreme Court cited the festival’s proximity to permit the lamp to be lit at the Deepathoon this year alone , clarifying that this did not constitute “essential religious practice”. The State filed a review petition , arguing when no right is recognised prima facie, a direction altering the existing position lacks judicial foundation. On Karthigai Deepam day, November 24, with the review pending, the government walked a tightrope. The Collector assured the High Court of compliance. Yet, the lamp was lit only at the traditional spot . The Collector has now apologised to the Court, blaming the temple’s Board of Trustees for not authorising the proposed lighting team at the Deepathoon. The administration has thus attempted to distinguish its proclaimed intent to comply with judicial directions from customs governed by the trustees. But it remains exposed to the charge of colluding with the temple authorities to breach a judicial mandate. The Deepathoon may be a mischievous prop deployed by self-serving Hindu groups, but the pillar stands on temple property. The State could have permitted the limited lighting, leaving the onus on the Court, without endorsing the Deepathoon claim or compromising religious amity. A democracy can remain healthy only when its constitutional pillars do not collide with one another.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: court / Tamil Nadu / religion and belief / history / Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam / democracy / customs and tradition / constitution

Constitutional (Adjective)
संवैधानिक — देश के संविधान (Constitution) के दायरे और मौलिक अधिकारों के अनुरूप।
✓ Syn: Statutory, Legitimate, Lawful  |  ✖ Ant: Unconstitutional, Illegal, Arbitrary
Administration (Noun)
प्रशासन — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Administration' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Intersection (Adjective / Verb)
चौराहा — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Intersection' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse  |  ✖ Ant: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable
Traditional (Adjective)
परंपरागत — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Traditional' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile

Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above ✍️ Editorial & Opinion passage on "Indefensible defiance: On Tamil Nadu and Court’s Thirupparankundram order", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Tamil Nadu should have followed Court order without backing Deepathoon claim.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Indefensible defiance: On Tamil Nadu and Court’s' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.

D. The author contends that 'Indefensible defiance: On Tamil Nadu and Cour' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.

D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "court / Tamil Nadu / religion and belief / history / Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam / democracy / customs and tradition / constitution." articles.title: Tamil Nadu govt. has acquired only 24% of land required for railway projects: Ashwini Vaishnav
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Stating that the Tamil Nadu government will have to do its duty of acquiring land if all sanctioned railway projects are to be implemented in the State, Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said that the total land acquired so far stood at only 24% of the land required.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Speaking at a Constitution Day event organised by the State BJP unit in the city on Thursday, Mr. Vaishnav said, that out of a total requirment of 4,800 hectares of land, the State has managed to acquire only 1,253 hectares. “My request to the TVK is, please take this as a challenge. Acquire the land [and] we will [carry out] each and every project without any hassle...don’t shy away from your responsibilities,” he emphasised. Projects sanctioned for development of railways in Tamil Nadu amounted to Rs. 48,000 crore, he added. Taking a dig at the State government over the Thiruparankundram deepam issue, Mr. Vaishnav said, “You can stop one deepam to be lighted, but you cannot stop the Tamil people from progress. Stopping one deepam, you have disturbed the emotions of millions of people.” Listing out some of the projects undertaken, the minister said that 77 railway stations in Tamil Nadu are being reconstructed. Construction was underway in stations like Chennai Egmore, Madurai, and Katpadi, while construction work has been completed in Chinna Salem, Morappur, Manapparai, Pollachi, Thiruvarur, Coonoor, and Udhagamandalam. Nine Vande Bharat services are being operated in Tamil Nadu, he maintained. Bullet trains, once introduced, will cut the journey from Chennai to Bengaluru to merely 73 minutes. Also, the Hyderabad-Amaravati-Chennai distance will take three hours to complete, the minister added. He added that in Gummidipoondi, the Ramkrishna Titagarh Rail Wheels Ltd’s forged wheel factory was ready and would soon roll out high strength railway wheels which will be exported to Europe as well. Earlier, BJP State President Nainar Nagendran put forth a series of requests, including installing a statue of former chief minister M.G. Ramachandran at the Chennai Central Railway Station, reopening of Kallur station near Tirunelveli, introducing sleeper coaches in Vande Bharat trains, and a stop at Thalaiyuthu station for trains running between Coimbatore and Tirunelveli. The minister immediately got on his phone passing the demands on to railway officials and setting a timeline for the same, which drew applause from the crowd.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Tamilisai Soundararajan, senior BJP leader, requested the minister to install a statue of freedom fighter Vanchinathan at the Vanchi Maniyachchi Junction in Thoothukudi district.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #8 of 30 (27 NOV)

📰 Tamil Nadu govt. has acquired only 24% of land required for railway projects: Ashwini Vaishnav

📌 Published: 27 Nov 2026, 01:04:58 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Stating that the Tamil Nadu government will have to do its duty of acquiring land if all sanctioned railway projects are to be implemented in the State, Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said that the total land acquired so far stood at only 24% of the land required.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Speaking at a Constitution Day event organised by the State BJP unit in the city on Thursday, Mr. Vaishnav said, that out of a total requirment of 4,800 hectares of land, the State has managed to acquire only 1,253 hectares. “My request to the TVK is, please take this as a challenge. Acquire the land [and] we will [carry out] each and every project without any hassle...don’t shy away from your responsibilities,” he emphasised. Projects sanctioned for development of railways in Tamil Nadu amounted to Rs. 48,000 crore, he added. Taking a dig at the State government over the Thiruparankundram deepam issue, Mr. Vaishnav said, “You can stop one deepam to be lighted, but you cannot stop the Tamil people from progress. Stopping one deepam, you have disturbed the emotions of millions of people.” Listing out some of the projects undertaken, the minister said that 77 railway stations in Tamil Nadu are being reconstructed. Construction was underway in stations like Chennai Egmore, Madurai, and Katpadi, while construction work has been completed in Chinna Salem, Morappur, Manapparai, Pollachi, Thiruvarur, Coonoor, and Udhagamandalam. Nine Vande Bharat services are being operated in Tamil Nadu, he maintained. Bullet trains, once introduced, will cut the journey from Chennai to Bengaluru to merely 73 minutes. Also, the Hyderabad-Amaravati-Chennai distance will take three hours to complete, the minister added. He added that in Gummidipoondi, the Ramkrishna Titagarh Rail Wheels Ltd’s forged wheel factory was ready and would soon roll out high strength railway wheels which will be exported to Europe as well. Earlier, BJP State President Nainar Nagendran put forth a series of requests, including installing a statue of former chief minister M.G. Ramachandran at the Chennai Central Railway Station, reopening of Kallur station near Tirunelveli, introducing sleeper coaches in Vande Bharat trains, and a stop at Thalaiyuthu station for trains running between Coimbatore and Tirunelveli. The minister immediately got on his phone passing the demands on to railway officials and setting a timeline for the same, which drew applause from the crowd.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Tamilisai Soundararajan, senior BJP leader, requested the minister to install a statue of freedom fighter Vanchinathan at the Vanchi Maniyachchi Junction in Thoothukudi district.

क्रियान्वयन / ज़मीनी स्तर पर लागू करना — किसी योजना या फैसले को असलियत में पूरा करना।
✓ Syn: Execution, Enforcement, Fulfillment  |  ✖ Ant: Abandonment, Neglect, Cancellation
Constitutional (Adjective)
संवैधानिक — देश के संविधान (Constitution) के दायरे और मौलिक अधिकारों के अनुरूप।
✓ Syn: Statutory, Legitimate, Lawful  |  ✖ Ant: Unconstitutional, Illegal, Arbitrary
Construction (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Construction' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Development (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Development' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile

C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Tamil Nadu govt. has acquired only 24% of lan' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Tamil Nadu govt. has acquired only 24% of lan' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. articles.title: Experts examine key aspects, challenges of conducting Census
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: An engaging conversation between retired IAS officer C. Chandramouli and Vinay Sitapati, Associate Dean and Professor of Law and Politics at Shiv Nadar University, over the former’s book, Counting a Nation – The Story of the Indian Census, here on Thursday evening, brought out the various aspects of conducting Census in the country.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Among the issues discussed were the need for a law to govern enumeration for caste census, the challenges faced while ensuring accuracy, training of enumerators for a standardised enumeration process, differences in the motive for carrying out the Census before and after the country’s independence, and the implication of Census for delimitation. During the book launch organised by Chennai International Centre (CIC) at the NFDC Tagore auditorium, Mr. Chandramouli, who had also served as the Registrar General and the Census Commissioner of India, recalled the challenges faced by enumerators while collecting data, specifically while enumerating the Sentinelese. Mr. Chandramouli, also the CIC Managing Director, explained why his book was not a memoir, noting that carrying out the Census was a team work of greater proportion. Mr. Sitapati said Mr. Chandramouli’s book was a current affairs work, but it looked at current issues through the lens of history. The discussion also highlighted the curiosity over the results of Census 2027. When a curious Mr. Sitapati asked what the newspapers’ headlines would be, especially that of The Hindu, the day after Census 2027 results, Mr. Chandramouli said the headlines would differ across regions depending on the results for each State. As for adopting technology for conducting Census, Mr. Chandramouli said that even in the most sophisticated of Censuses, “ground truthing of the whole exercise by visiting the field and checking the information is key to the success of an operation like this.”
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: With modern technology, the exercise could be more efficient and quicker, he added.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #9 of 30 (27 NOV)

📰 Experts examine key aspects, challenges of conducting Census

📌 Published: 27 Nov 2026, 01:01:46 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: An engaging conversation between retired IAS officer C. Chandramouli and Vinay Sitapati, Associate Dean and Professor of Law and Politics at Shiv Nadar University, over the former’s book, Counting a Nation – The Story of the Indian Census, here on Thursday evening, brought out the various aspects of conducting Census in the country.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Among the issues discussed were the need for a law to govern enumeration for caste census, the challenges faced while ensuring accuracy, training of enumerators for a standardised enumeration process, differences in the motive for carrying out the Census before and after the country’s independence, and the implication of Census for delimitation. During the book launch organised by Chennai International Centre (CIC) at the NFDC Tagore auditorium, Mr. Chandramouli, who had also served as the Registrar General and the Census Commissioner of India, recalled the challenges faced by enumerators while collecting data, specifically while enumerating the Sentinelese. Mr. Chandramouli, also the CIC Managing Director, explained why his book was not a memoir, noting that carrying out the Census was a team work of greater proportion. Mr. Sitapati said Mr. Chandramouli’s book was a current affairs work, but it looked at current issues through the lens of history. The discussion also highlighted the curiosity over the results of Census 2027. When a curious Mr. Sitapati asked what the newspapers’ headlines would be, especially that of The Hindu, the day after Census 2027 results, Mr. Chandramouli said the headlines would differ across regions depending on the results for each State. As for adopting technology for conducting Census, Mr. Chandramouli said that even in the most sophisticated of Censuses, “ground truthing of the whole exercise by visiting the field and checking the information is key to the success of an operation like this.”

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: With modern technology, the exercise could be more efficient and quicker, he added.

articles.title: Thirupparankundram ‘deepathoon’ row: Supreme Court agrees to list plea to detail Vijay’s role
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The application said the four Sthanikars had denied giving any opinion to light the lamp at the Deepa Mandapam nor were they consulted

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Supreme Court on Thursday (November 26, 2026) allowed the listing of a contempt petition on November 27 seeking a personal affidavit from the Tamil Nadu Chief Secretary detailing the government’s decision-making, including any role played by Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay in the failure to light the Karthigai Deepam at the Deepathoon on the Thirupparankundram Hill summit in compliance with the November 20 order of the court. The petition filed by Rama Ravikumar was orally mentioned before a Bench headed by Justice Arvind Kumar at 2 p.m. The petition, settled by senior advocate P. Valliappan and filed by advocate G. Balaji, also sought the immediate preservation and production of all physical and electronic records relating to the implementation of the November 20 order. It has made both Tamil Nadu authorities and the temple administration parties in the contempt case. Other documents sought to include the November 23 prohibitory order and the resolution of the Board of Trustees, including the opinions purportedly obtained from the Agama experts and Sthanikars. The plea also urged the apex court to invoke its plenary powers under Article 142 of the Constitution for lighting the ceremonial lamp at Deepathoon in Thirupparankundram Hill on a substituted date within seven days, preferably during the current Tamil month of Karthigai, subject to the safeguards prescribed in the November 20 order, and under the personal supervision of the State Chief Secretary, with the assistance of an independent Court Commissioner and the Central Reserve Police Force. Vinay, Commissioner, Hindu Religious & Charitable Endowments Department; Nishant Krishna, District Collector, Madurai; and S. Rajendiran, Madurai Commissioner of Police. 🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #10 of 30 (27 NOV)

📰 Thirupparankundram ‘deepathoon’ row: Supreme Court agrees to list plea to detail Vijay’s role

📌 Published: 27 Nov 2026, 12:58:59 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The application said the four Sthanikars had denied giving any opinion to light the lamp at the Deepa Mandapam nor were they consulted

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Supreme Court on Thursday (November 26, 2026) allowed the listing of a contempt petition on November 27 seeking a personal affidavit from the Tamil Nadu Chief Secretary detailing the government’s decision-making, including any role played by Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay in the failure to light the Karthigai Deepam at the Deepathoon on the Thirupparankundram Hill summit in compliance with the November 20 order of the court. The petition filed by Rama Ravikumar was orally mentioned before a Bench headed by Justice Arvind Kumar at 2 p.m. The petition, settled by senior advocate P. Valliappan and filed by advocate G. Balaji, also sought the immediate preservation and production of all physical and electronic records relating to the implementation of the November 20 order. It has made both Tamil Nadu authorities and the temple administration parties in the contempt case. Other documents sought to include the November 23 prohibitory order and the resolution of the Board of Trustees, including the opinions purportedly obtained from the Agama experts and Sthanikars. The petition said the court must initiate suo motu criminal contempt proceedings. The plea also urged the apex court to invoke its plenary powers under Article 142 of the Constitution for lighting the ceremonial lamp at Deepathoon in Thirupparankundram Hill on a substituted date within seven days, preferably during the current Tamil month of Karthigai, subject to the safeguards prescribed in the November 20 order, and under the personal supervision of the State Chief Secretary, with the assistance of an independent Court Commissioner and the Central Reserve Police Force. In the morning, Justice Kumar verbally conveyed that an application to shift the Karthigai Deepam flame from the Deepa Mandapam to the Deepathoon and contempt petitions filed against State authorities for failing to comply with the November 20 order to light the sacred lamp on the stone pillar would be listed on November 27. In one of these contempt petitions, Hindu Dharma Parishad has sought the initiation of action against T.G. Vinay, Commissioner, Hindu Religious & Charitable Endowments Department; Nishant Krishna, District Collector, Madurai; and S. Rajendiran, Madurai Commissioner of Police. The Hindu parties are seeking contempt action despite Mr. Krishna’s preliminary report of November 25, which stated that the district authorities had made all arrangements to facilitate the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam at the Deepathoon in compliance with the November 20 order. However, the Board of Trustees at the Arulmigu Subramaniaswamy Temple had not authorised persons for the lamp-lighting team on November 24. Another contempt plea, drawn by advocate Yashika Anand and filed through advocate Narender Kumar Verma, said the non-compliance with the apex court order of November 20 to light the lamp on November 24 at the Deepathoon as a “limited one-time arrangement” only for this year was not only contumacious but also a patent violation of Articles 14 and 16 of the Constitution. “It amounts to invasion of legitimate expectation duly sanctioned by the Supreme Court,” the petition said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Karthigai deepam lit only at traditional spot atop Thirupparankundram hills

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Implementation (Noun)
क्रियान्वयन / ज़मीनी स्तर पर लागू करना — किसी योजना या फैसले को असलियत में पूरा करना।
✓ Syn: Execution, Enforcement, Fulfillment  |  ✖ Ant: Abandonment, Neglect, Cancellation
Constitutional (Adjective)
संवैधानिक — देश के संविधान (Constitution) के दायरे और मौलिक अधिकारों के अनुरूप।
✓ Syn: Statutory, Legitimate, Lawful  |  ✖ Ant: Unconstitutional, Illegal, Arbitrary
Administration (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Administration' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Preservation (Noun)
संरक्षण — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Preservation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "Thirupparankundram ‘deepathoon’ row: Supreme Court agrees to list plea to detail Vijay’s role", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. The application said the four Sthanikars had denied giving any opinion to light the lamp at the Deepa Mandapam nor were they consulted.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Thirupparankundram ‘deepathoon’ row: Supreme Cou' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Thirupparankundram ‘deepathoon’ row: Supreme ' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Thirupparankundram ‘deepathoon’ row: Supreme ' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "The application said the four Sthanikars had denied giving any opinion to light the lamp at the Deepa Mandapam nor were they consulted." (Hinglish Arth: आवेदन में कहा गया है कि चारों स्थानिकरों ने दीपा मंडपम में दीपक जलाने के बारे में कोई राय देने से इनकार किया था और न ही उनसे कोई सलाह ली गई थी.)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Thirupparankundram ‘deepathoon’ row: Supreme Court agrees to list plea to detail Vijay’s role"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. Karthigai deepam lit only at traditional spot atop Thirupparankundram hills.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "Karthigai deepam lit only at traditional spot atop Thirupparankundram hills." (Hinglish Arth: कार्तिगई दीपम केवल थिरुप्पारनकुंड्रम पहाड़ियों के शीर्ष पर पारंपरिक स्थान पर जलाया जाता है)

articles.title: Vizag youth advocate pitches ‘Blue Steps’ beach walk at Doha wellness forum
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Young people from eight countries met in Doha from November 8 to 11 for the fourth edition of the Youth at Hostel, International Forum, which looked at how youth hostels and tourism can promote physical and mental well-being.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: India was represented by Haritha Nagaveni Naganaboina of Visakhapatnam and Mithil Manoj Joshi of Goa. Ms. Haritha spoke on the country’s experience of youth health and well-being. Organised by Qatar Youth Hostels in partnership with UNICEF, the forum focused on United Nations Sustainable Development Goal, SDG-3: Good Health and Well-being. The theme was chosen by participants through a vote at the end of the previous edition. The forum aims to develop youth-led recommendations and programmes that link health and well-being with sustainable tourism, in line with the Qatar National Youth Policy. The participating countries were Qatar, the host, Bahrain, Libya, Lebanon, Slovenia, India, Pakistan and Spain. Ms. Haritha, 28, said the two of them were the only participants from India. Mr. Joshi is 25. The programme combined interactive sessions and workshops meant to build partnerships among youth hostel representatives. UNICEF and Qatari ministry representatives opened the ceremony, and addressed the delegates, she said. Participants attended eight workshops over two days. In one, groups were asked how tourism and wellness could be combined in Qatar. Ms. Haritha led her group in pitching “Blue Steps”, a beach walk proposal that the session host liked. Each country also made a presentation, and hers was on India’s experience. Extreme heat keeps most people in Qatar indoors, Ms. Haritha said, with residents travelling largely by car or metro. She was told that parks and cycling facilities were being developed there, and felt the idea could work in Visakhapatnam, which has a coastal setting and is not as hot. Delegates from other countries, she found, shared similar concerns, among them the need for a digital detox, and drew on their own geography for activities such as mountaineering and kayaking. Ms. Haritha, who holds an LL.M. from Middlesex University, London, and an LL.B. from Andhra University, is a former junior advocate. She has been associated with the Youth Hostels Association of India for about 13 years. The Andhra Pradesh branch recommended her to the national office, and she credits its chairman, Ch. Ravi Paul, for urging her to apply.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Back home, she hopes to organise a five-day trek through forest to the Katiki waterfalls in Araku, and will propose it to the State branch.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #11 of 30 (27 NOV)

📰 Vizag youth advocate pitches ‘Blue Steps’ beach walk at Doha wellness forum

📌 Published: 27 Nov 2026, 12:48:13 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Young people from eight countries met in Doha from November 8 to 11 for the fourth edition of the Youth at Hostel, International Forum, which looked at how youth hostels and tourism can promote physical and mental well-being.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: India was represented by Haritha Nagaveni Naganaboina of Visakhapatnam and Mithil Manoj Joshi of Goa. Ms. Haritha spoke on the country’s experience of youth health and well-being. Organised by Qatar Youth Hostels in partnership with UNICEF, the forum focused on United Nations Sustainable Development Goal, SDG-3: Good Health and Well-being. The theme was chosen by participants through a vote at the end of the previous edition. The forum aims to develop youth-led recommendations and programmes that link health and well-being with sustainable tourism, in line with the Qatar National Youth Policy. The participating countries were Qatar, the host, Bahrain, Libya, Lebanon, Slovenia, India, Pakistan and Spain. Ms. Haritha, 28, said the two of them were the only participants from India. Mr. Joshi is 25. The programme combined interactive sessions and workshops meant to build partnerships among youth hostel representatives. UNICEF and Qatari ministry representatives opened the ceremony, and addressed the delegates, she said. Participants attended eight workshops over two days. In one, groups were asked how tourism and wellness could be combined in Qatar. Ms. Haritha led her group in pitching “Blue Steps”, a beach walk proposal that the session host liked. Each country also made a presentation, and hers was on India’s experience. Extreme heat keeps most people in Qatar indoors, Ms. Haritha said, with residents travelling largely by car or metro. She was told that parks and cycling facilities were being developed there, and felt the idea could work in Visakhapatnam, which has a coastal setting and is not as hot. Delegates from other countries, she found, shared similar concerns, among them the need for a digital detox, and drew on their own geography for activities such as mountaineering and kayaking. Ms. Haritha, who holds an LL.M. from Middlesex University, London, and an LL.B. from Andhra University, is a former junior advocate. She has been associated with the Youth Hostels Association of India for about 13 years. The Andhra Pradesh branch recommended her to the national office, and she credits its chairman, Ch. Ravi Paul, for urging her to apply.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Back home, she hopes to organise a five-day trek through forest to the Katiki waterfalls in Araku, and will propose it to the State branch.

articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: Young people from eight countries met in Doha from November 8 to 11 for the fourth edition of the Youth at Hostel, International Forum, which looked at how youth hostels and tourism can promote physical and mental well-being.
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: India was represented by Haritha Nagaveni Naganaboina of Visakhapatnam and Mithil Manoj Joshi of Goa. Ms. Haritha spoke on the country’s experience of youth health and well-being. Organised by Qatar Youth Hostels in partnership with UNICEF, the forum focused on United Nations Sustainable Development Goal, SDG-3: Good Health and Well-being. The theme was chosen by participants through a vote at the end of the previous edition. The forum aims to develop youth-led recommendations and programmes that link health and well-being with sustainable tourism, in line with the Qatar National Youth Policy. The participating countries were Qatar, the host, Bahrain, Libya, Lebanon, Slovenia, India, Pakistan and Spain. Ms. Haritha, 28, said the two of them were the only participants from India. Mr. Joshi is 25. The programme combined interactive sessions and workshops meant to build partnerships among youth hostel representatives. UNICEF and Qatari ministry representatives opened the ceremony, and addressed the delegates, she said. Participants attended eight workshops over two days. In one, groups were asked how tourism and wellness could be combined in Qatar. Ms. Haritha led her group in pitching “Blue Steps”, a beach walk proposal that the session host liked. Each country also made a presentation, and hers was on India’s experience. Extreme heat keeps most people in Qatar indoors, Ms. Haritha said, with residents travelling largely by car or metro. She was told that parks and cycling facilities were being developed there, and felt the idea could work in Visakhapatnam, which has a coastal setting and is not as hot. Delegates from other countries, she found, shared similar concerns, among them the need for a digital detox, and drew on their own geography for activities such as mountaineering and kayaking. Ms. Haritha, who holds an LL.M. from Middlesex University, London, and an LL.B. from Andhra University, is a former junior advocate. She has been associated with the Youth Hostels Association of India for about 13 years. The Andhra Pradesh branch recommended her to the national office, and she credits its chairman, Ch. Ravi Paul, for urging her to apply.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Back home, she hopes to organise a five-day trek through forest to the Katiki waterfalls in Araku, and will propose it to the State branch.

articles.title: Amended Delimitation Bill likely to be tabled in special Parliament sitting from November 30
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Centre announces special sitting of Parliament from November 30, 2026, over 100 days since both Houses were adjourned without prorogation; government trying to pass the Bill after ‘operation lotus’, says Congress

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The government has called for a special sitting of Parliament beginning Monday (November 30, 2026), where it is likely to table an amended Delimitation Bill. The two Houses will meet on separate dates, Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju announced on Thursday (November 26, 2026), which is the 104th day since the Monsoon Session adjourned indefinitely on August 13. Lok Sabha sittings will begin on November 30 and Rajya Sabha sittings on December 2. Both Houses will conclude on December 3. The last record of a session of Parliament continuing unprorogued was in 2008 , when it went on for 87 days. The Union Cabinet will meet on Friday (November 27, 2026) to clear the amended legislation. According to sources, three crucial changes are being introduced: a uniform 50% increase in the share of Lok Sabha seats; extending the freeze for 25 years on using the 1971 Census as the basis to determine the proportional strength of each State in the Lok Sabha; and third, using the 2011 Census for redrawing constituencies within each State. This replicates the formula brought by the Atal Bihari Vajpayee government in the Constitution (Eighty-fourth Amendment) Act, 2001. Reacting to the announcement, Congress general secretary (communication) Jairam Ramesh said the Narendra Modi government announced the session “after 105 days of operation lotus” in the hope of getting a “super-tainted” two-thirds majority to get the Bill passed. “Can there be a great insult to and assault on the Constitution,” he asked in a post on X, noting that the announcement came on Constitution Day. Congress general secretary (organisation) K.C. Venugopal took to X to describe the attempt to pass the Delimitation Bill as “ sansad chori” . “To orchestrate this murder of the Constitution on Constitution Day shows how badly they want to mock our precious democratic system. We will not allow this to pass,” Mr. Venugopal said. Since April, when the legislative package, including the Delimitation Bill, was defeated by a united Opposition in the Lok Sabha, the seat arithmetic in the House has changed. Twenty TMC MPs broke away and merged with the Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI), pledging support to the NDA. TMC challenged the split, which is currently under Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla’s review. The NCPI faction, on Tuesday (November 24, 2026), 84 days after TMC’s challenge, submitted replies to Mr. Birla, defending its decision and asserting that the move did not violate any parliamentary or constitutional provisions. Six Shiv Sena (UBT) MPs joined the Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena. Following the recent alliance between the BJP and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD), the lone SAD MP is also expected to vote with the government. It is also learnt that the YSR Congress, which has four MPs in the Lok Sabha, will extend support to the government on the Bill.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: In this evolving situation, all eyes are on the DMK, with 22 Lok Sabha MPs, and the NCP (Sharadchandra Pawar), with eight.
