articles.title: CPI(M) slams Keralam govt over ban on party newspapers in jails
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The CPI(M) on Friday strongly criticised the Congress-led government over the decision to stop the distribution of political party-affiliated newspapers in jails, questioning whether a “super Emergency” had been declared in Keralam.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Senior party leader M V Jayarajan told reporters in Kannur that a circular directing prisons to stop purchasing and distributing newspapers, including Deshabhimani , the CPI(M)’s mouthpiece, was issued by the Director General of Prisons a day ago. “Has a super Emergency been declared in Keralam? Chief Minister V D Satheesan and Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala should clarify this,” he said. Mr. Jayarajan pointed out that even during the Emergency, newspapers, including Deshabhimani , were allowed in State prisons. At that time, certain news reports were blacked out due to press censorship to prevent inmates from accessing them, he said. There was no such situation now, and the present ban was a “primitive” move, he alleged. He also said prison rules stipulated that newspapers sent to inmates by their friends or relatives through sponsorships should be provided to them. The present restriction was against these rules, Jayarajan said, alleging that the Director General of Prisons would not have issued such a circular without the knowledge of the home minister. His criticism came a day after the Kerala Prisons and Correctional Services Department directed all jails in the state to stop purchasing and distributing newspapers and publications affiliated to political parties. In a circular issued on Thursday, Director General of Prisons S Sreejith said correctional institutions, which aim at the psychological and social rehabilitation of inmates, should ensure that the news and information made available to them were objective, truthful and free from political bias.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Publications serving as mouthpieces of political parties or organisations, or reflecting political interests, were not appropriate for distribution in prisons, the circular said.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #10 of 30 (27 NOV)

📰 CPI(M) slams Keralam govt over ban on party newspapers in jails

📌 Published: 27 Nov 2026, 03:11:43 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The CPI(M) on Friday strongly criticised the Congress-led government over the decision to stop the distribution of political party-affiliated newspapers in jails, questioning whether a “super Emergency” had been declared in Keralam.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Senior party leader M V Jayarajan told reporters in Kannur that a circular directing prisons to stop purchasing and distributing newspapers, including Deshabhimani , the CPI(M)’s mouthpiece, was issued by the Director General of Prisons a day ago. “Has a super Emergency been declared in Keralam? Chief Minister V D Satheesan and Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala should clarify this,” he said. Mr. Jayarajan pointed out that even during the Emergency, newspapers, including Deshabhimani , were allowed in State prisons. At that time, certain news reports were blacked out due to press censorship to prevent inmates from accessing them, he said. There was no such situation now, and the present ban was a “primitive” move, he alleged. He also said prison rules stipulated that newspapers sent to inmates by their friends or relatives through sponsorships should be provided to them. The present restriction was against these rules, Jayarajan said, alleging that the Director General of Prisons would not have issued such a circular without the knowledge of the home minister. His criticism came a day after the Kerala Prisons and Correctional Services Department directed all jails in the state to stop purchasing and distributing newspapers and publications affiliated to political parties. In a circular issued on Thursday, Director General of Prisons S Sreejith said correctional institutions, which aim at the psychological and social rehabilitation of inmates, should ensure that the news and information made available to them were objective, truthful and free from political bias.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Publications serving as mouthpieces of political parties or organisations, or reflecting political interests, were not appropriate for distribution in prisons, the circular said.

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Institutional (Adjective)
संस्थागत — देश की संवैधानिक या सरकारी संस्थाओं के नियमों और ढांचे से जुड़ा हुआ।
✓ Syn: Systemic, Organizational, Constitutional  |  ✖ Ant: Individual, Informal, Unorganized
Rehabilitation (Noun)
पुनर्वास — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Rehabilitation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Psychological (Adjective)
मनोवैज्ञानिक — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Psychological' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Distribution (Adjective / Verb)
वितरण — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Distribution' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse  |  ✖ Ant: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "CPI(M) slams Keralam govt over ban on party newspapers in jails", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. The CPI(M) on Friday strongly criticised the Congress-led government over the decision to stop the distribution of political party-affiliated...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'CPI(M) slams Keralam govt over ban on party news' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'CPI(M) slams Keralam govt over ban on party n' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'CPI(M) slams Keralam govt over ban on party n' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "The CPI(M) on Friday strongly criticised the Congress-led government over the decision to stop the distribution of political party-affiliated..." (Hinglish Arth: सीपीआई (एम) ने शुक्रवार को जेलों में राजनीतिक दलों से जुड़े समाचार पत्रों के वितरण को रोकने के फैसले पर कांग्रेस के नेतृत्व वाली सरकार की कड़ी आलोचना की, सवाल उठाया कि क्या "सुपर आपातकाल" घोषित किया गया था।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "CPI(M) slams Keralam govt over ban on party newspapers in jails"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. Publications serving as mouthpieces of political parties or organisations, or reflecting political interests, were not appropriate for distribution...
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "Publications serving as mouthpieces of political parties or organisations, or reflecting political interests, were not appropriate for distribution..." (Hinglish Arth: सर्कुलर में कहा गया है कि राजनीतिक दलों या संगठनों के मुखपत्र के रूप में काम करने वाले या राजनीतिक हितों को प्रतिबिंबित करने वाले प्रकाशन जेलों में वितरण के लिए उपयुक्त नहीं हैं।)

articles.title: NGT-appointed amicus report flags gaps in Keralam’s solid, liquid waste management
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The report stated that about four-fifths of sanitary waste is not scientifically treated. Only 42.1 tonnes per day of the total sanitary waste of 203.66 tonnes generated daily is treated. Even when all projects are complete, the capacity will be 113.25 tonnes per day

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A report filed by an amicus curiae appointed by the National Green Tribunal (NGT) has flagged multiple gaps in the management of solid and liquid waste in Keralam. The deficiencies have been pointed out in the observation note dated November 24, 2026 submitted in the matter related to the compliance of Municipal Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016 and other environmental issues in the State. The amicus curiae made the observations based on the affidavits and compliance reports submitted by the authorities. The report stated that about four-fifths of sanitary waste is not scientifically treated. Only 42.1 tonnes per day of the total sanitary waste of 203.66 tonnes generated daily is treated. Even when all projects are complete, the capacity will be 113.25 tonnes per day, it said. The amicus curiae pointed out that inert waste is being used for land filling without safeguards. Quoting a report submitted by the Keralam government, the report said that about 404.8 tonnes per day of inert waste is used for filling up appropriate portions of hilly areas, stadiums, railway platforms, yards and road embankment formations. No register of sites, test reports or approvals is given. Given the State’s wetlands and landslide-prone slopes, this practice needs strict control, it suggested. The report said that the action on the illegal drains discharging untreated sewage into streams and water bodies has been initiated in only four districts, including Kollam, Ernakulam, Alappuzha and Kottayam as per the affidavit submitted by the government. Of the 723 illegal outlets in the four districts, 671 are in Ernakulam alone. The total quantity of processed and unprocessed legacy (old) waste has increased from 19.54 lakh metric tonnes in December 2025 to 19,6 lakh metric tonnes in July 2026. The gap in total sewage generated and treated is as high as 3901.2 million litres daily, indicative of a serious concern, it said. The amicus curiae has suggested a sample-based functional audit of composting bins and biogas plants. The four regional plants for sanitary waste treatment should be commissioned by a fixed date. For inert and land filling, a register of every site where inert are used for filling be maintained and published, with test reports and approvals.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The report suggested preparation of a GIS-mapped inventory of drains, streams and storm-water channels carrying sewage into rivers, backwaters, ponds and the sea.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #11 of 30 (27 NOV)

📰 NGT-appointed amicus report flags gaps in Keralam’s solid, liquid waste management

📌 Published: 27 Nov 2026, 03:09:26 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The report stated that about four-fifths of sanitary waste is not scientifically treated. Only 42.1 tonnes per day of the total sanitary waste of 203.66 tonnes generated daily is treated. Even when all projects are complete, the capacity will be 113.25 tonnes per day

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A report filed by an amicus curiae appointed by the National Green Tribunal (NGT) has flagged multiple gaps in the management of solid and liquid waste in Keralam. The deficiencies have been pointed out in the observation note dated November 24, 2026 submitted in the matter related to the compliance of Municipal Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016 and other environmental issues in the State. The amicus curiae made the observations based on the affidavits and compliance reports submitted by the authorities. The report stated that about four-fifths of sanitary waste is not scientifically treated. Only 42.1 tonnes per day of the total sanitary waste of 203.66 tonnes generated daily is treated. Even when all projects are complete, the capacity will be 113.25 tonnes per day, it said. The amicus curiae pointed out that inert waste is being used for land filling without safeguards. Quoting a report submitted by the Keralam government, the report said that about 404.8 tonnes per day of inert waste is used for filling up appropriate portions of hilly areas, stadiums, railway platforms, yards and road embankment formations. No register of sites, test reports or approvals is given. Given the State’s wetlands and landslide-prone slopes, this practice needs strict control, it suggested. The report said that the action on the illegal drains discharging untreated sewage into streams and water bodies has been initiated in only four districts, including Kollam, Ernakulam, Alappuzha and Kottayam as per the affidavit submitted by the government. Of the 723 illegal outlets in the four districts, 671 are in Ernakulam alone. The total quantity of processed and unprocessed legacy (old) waste has increased from 19.54 lakh metric tonnes in December 2025 to 19,6 lakh metric tonnes in July 2026. The gap in total sewage generated and treated is as high as 3901.2 million litres daily, indicative of a serious concern, it said. The amicus curiae has suggested a sample-based functional audit of composting bins and biogas plants. The four regional plants for sanitary waste treatment should be commissioned by a fixed date. For inert and land filling, a register of every site where inert are used for filling be maintained and published, with test reports and approvals.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The report suggested preparation of a GIS-mapped inventory of drains, streams and storm-water channels carrying sewage into rivers, backwaters, ponds and the sea.

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Quantitative (Adjective)
आंकड़ों और संख्या पर आधारित — जिसे ठोस नंबरों और डेटा में मापा जा सके।
✓ Syn: Measurable, Numerical, Empirical  |  ✖ Ant: Qualitative, Subjective, Unmeasurable
Environmental (Adjective)
पर्यावरण, प्रकृति और हमारे पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र (Ecosystem) से संबंधित।
✓ Syn: Ecological, Biospheric, Natural  |  ✖ Ant: Industrial, Polluting, Synthetic
Observation (Noun)
अवलोकन — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Observation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Preparation (Noun)
तैयारी — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Preparation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "NGT-appointed amicus report flags gaps in Keralam’s solid, liquid waste management", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. The report stated that about four-fifths of sanitary waste is not scientifically treated.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'NGT-appointed amicus report flags gaps in Kerala' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'NGT-appointed amicus report flags gaps in Ker' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'NGT-appointed amicus report flags gaps in Ker' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "The report stated that about four-fifths of sanitary waste is not scientifically treated." (Hinglish Arth: रिपोर्ट में कहा गया है कि लगभग चार-पाँचवें सैनिटरी कचरे का वैज्ञानिक तरीके से उपचार नहीं किया जाता है।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "NGT-appointed amicus report flags gaps in Keralam’s solid, liquid waste management"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. The report suggested preparation of a GIS-mapped inventory of drains, streams and storm-water channels carrying sewage into rivers, backwaters, ponds...
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "The report suggested preparation of a GIS-mapped inventory of drains, streams and storm-water channels carrying sewage into rivers, backwaters, ponds..." (Hinglish Arth: रिपोर्ट में नदियों, बैकवाटर, तालाबों और समुद्र में सीवेज ले जाने वाले नालों, झरनों और तूफानी जल चैनलों की जीआईएस-मैप सूची तैयार करने का सुझाव दिया गया है।)

No register of sites, test reports or approvals is given. Given the State’s wetlands and landslide-prone slopes, this practice needs strict control, it suggested. The report said that the action on the illegal drains discharging untreated sewage into streams and water bodies has been initiated in only four districts, including Kollam, Ernakulam, Alappuzha and Kottayam as per the affidavit submitted by the government. Of the 723 illegal outlets in the four districts, 671 are in Ernakulam alone. The total quantity of processed and unprocessed legacy (old) waste has increased from 19.54 lakh metric tonnes in December 2025 to 19,6 lakh metric tonnes in July 2026. The gap in total sewage generated and treated is as high as 3901.2 million litres daily, indicative of a serious concern, it said. The amicus curiae has suggested a sample-based functional audit of composting bins and biogas plants. The four regional plants for sanitary waste treatment should be commissioned by a fixed date. For inert and land filling, a register of every site where inert are used for filling be maintained and published, with test reports and approvals.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The report suggested preparation of a GIS-mapped inventory of drains, streams and storm-water channels carrying sewage into rivers, backwaters, ponds and the sea.

articles.title: Punjab CM launches Smart Ration Card Scheme to benefit 10 lakh beneficiaries
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The Chief Minister assured the beneficiaries of five kg of free wheat per family member per month after the completion of e-KYC

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann launched the Smart Ration Card Scheme on Thursday (November 27, 2026) to extend food-security benefits to 10 lakh beneficiaries, asserting that his government has ensured that only the genuinely needy would receive their rightful entitlements through a transparent selection process. Along with Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) national convenor Arvind Kejriwal , Mr. Mann distributed "Meri Rasoi" kits among beneficiaries on stage at an event in Moga. The kits contained pulses, sugar, salt, turmeric and mustard oil. The Chief Minister assured the beneficiaries of five kg of free wheat per family member per month after the completion of e-KYC. "Our government has undertaken a special drive to issue 10 lakh new ration cards to the most deserving and needy families. The entire exercise has been conducted through a digital, transparent and impartial system to ensure that genuine beneficiaries receive their rightful entitlements, without any discrimination or political interference," he said. Mr. Mann noted that 19.25 lakh online applications were received during the special campaign launched in July. "People applied through sewa kendras, common service centres (CSCs) and online platforms, while the district administration conducted door-to-door verification to identify eligible families," he said. Mr. Mann said that under the National Food Security Act (NFSA), 2013, Punjab currently has 1.36 crore beneficiaries belonging to 39.73 lakh families. "All new ration card beneficiaries will receive a special Meri Rasoi kit comprising two kg of pulses, two kg of sugar, one kg of salt, 200 of grams turmeric powder and one litre mustard oil. Besides, they will continue to receive free wheat under the National Food Security Act," he said. The AAP government in Punjab is committed to ensuring food security for every deserving family, the Chief Minister said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: These additional benefits will provide meaningful relief to ordinary households and strengthen the welfare support extended to the poorest sections of the society, he added.

articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: The Chief Minister assured the beneficiaries of five kg of free wheat per family member per month after the completion of e-KYC
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann launched the Smart Ration Card Scheme on Thursday (November 27, 2026) to extend food-security benefits to 10 lakh beneficiaries, asserting that his government has ensured that only the genuinely needy would receive their rightful entitlements through a transparent selection process. Along with Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) national convenor Arvind Kejriwal , Mr. Mann distributed "Meri Rasoi" kits among beneficiaries on stage at an event in Moga. The kits contained pulses, sugar, salt, turmeric and mustard oil. The Chief Minister assured the beneficiaries of five kg of free wheat per family member per month after the completion of e-KYC. "Our government has undertaken a special drive to issue 10 lakh new ration cards to the most deserving and needy families. The entire exercise has been conducted through a digital, transparent and impartial system to ensure that genuine beneficiaries receive their rightful entitlements, without any discrimination or political interference," he said. Mr. Mann noted that 19.25 lakh online applications were received during the special campaign launched in July. "People applied through sewa kendras, common service centres (CSCs) and online platforms, while the district administration conducted door-to-door verification to identify eligible families," he said. Mr. Mann said that under the National Food Security Act (NFSA), 2013, Punjab currently has 1.36 crore beneficiaries belonging to 39.73 lakh families. "All new ration card beneficiaries will receive a special Meri Rasoi kit comprising two kg of pulses, two kg of sugar, one kg of salt, 200 of grams turmeric powder and one litre mustard oil. Besides, they will continue to receive free wheat under the National Food Security Act," he said. The AAP government in Punjab is committed to ensuring food security for every deserving family, the Chief Minister said.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: These additional benefits will provide meaningful relief to ordinary households and strengthen the welfare support extended to the poorest sections of the society, he added.

articles.title: Pakistan set to host talks with Saudi Arabia, Turkey under trilateral defence pact
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The talks in Islamabad will focus on West Asia and the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, two security officials said, with Pakistan’s Defence and Foreign Ministers and army chief attending

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Pakistan is set to host talks with Saudi Arabia and Turkiye on Friday (November 27, 2026) under a trilateral defence pact that treats an attack on any member as an attack on all three, two security officials said. The talks in Islamabad will focus on developments in West Asia, including ongoing attacks on Saudi Arabia by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebels, the officials said. They spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorised to discuss the meeting publicly. Pakistan has said that the agreement is purely defensive in nature and not against anyone, including Iran, and that the trilateral alliance reflects a shared desire to strengthen strategic security cooperation. Senior diplomats as well as defence and military officials from the three countries are expected to discuss ways to deter threats, expand military cooperation, share intelligence and strengthen defence industry ties, the officials said. Pakistan’s Defence Minister Khawaja Muhammad Asif, Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar and army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir will attend the meeting. Mr. Asif has said that Pakistan will use “whatever means are available” to defend Saudi Arabia against attacks from the Houthis. However, Pakistan is still making efforts, with help from countries in West Asia, including Qatar, to urge the United States and Iran to return to the negotiating table to end the conflict in the region and beyond through talks. Pakistan had brokered an interim deal between the two sides in June 2026. Friday’s meeting of the Strategic, Political and Defense Committee falls under the Joint Mecca Defense Agreement, which was signed in August 2026 in the Saudi holy city of Mecca by Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Pakistan’s Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif. Pakistan’s government has not released details ahead of the meeting, but the authorities have declared a local holiday in Islamabad to limit public movement as part of security measures for the gathering. Islamabad traffic police have announced road diversions and advised motorists to use alternative routes to accommodate the movement of foreign delegations. During a previous meeting in Riyadh, the three sides had vowed to immediately implement what they said were their collective defence commitments, including arrangements for the rapid deployment of agreed-upon military forces and capabilities to Saudi Arabia.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: According to the agreement, the group’s secretariat has been established in Saudi Arabia, and retired Pakistani General Nauman Mahmood has been selected as its first secretary-general. He will also attend Friday’s meeting. The pact binds the parties for 10 years, after which they would need to give three months’ notice before leaving.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #19 of 30 (27 NOV)

📰 Pakistan set to host talks with Saudi Arabia, Turkey under trilateral defence pact

📌 Published: 27 Nov 2026, 02:51:36 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The talks in Islamabad will focus on West Asia and the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, two security officials said, with Pakistan’s Defence and Foreign Ministers and army chief attending

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Pakistan is set to host talks with Saudi Arabia and Turkiye on Friday (November 27, 2026) under a trilateral defence pact that treats an attack on any member as an attack on all three, two security officials said. The talks in Islamabad will focus on developments in West Asia, including ongoing attacks on Saudi Arabia by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebels, the officials said. They spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorised to discuss the meeting publicly. Pakistan has said that the agreement is purely defensive in nature and not against anyone, including Iran, and that the trilateral alliance reflects a shared desire to strengthen strategic security cooperation. Senior diplomats as well as defence and military officials from the three countries are expected to discuss ways to deter threats, expand military cooperation, share intelligence and strengthen defence industry ties, the officials said. Pakistan’s Defence Minister Khawaja Muhammad Asif, Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar and army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir will attend the meeting. Mr. Asif has said that Pakistan will use “whatever means are available” to defend Saudi Arabia against attacks from the Houthis. However, Pakistan is still making efforts, with help from countries in West Asia, including Qatar, to urge the United States and Iran to return to the negotiating table to end the conflict in the region and beyond through talks. Pakistan had brokered an interim deal between the two sides in June 2026. Friday’s meeting of the Strategic, Political and Defense Committee falls under the Joint Mecca Defense Agreement, which was signed in August 2026 in the Saudi holy city of Mecca by Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Pakistan’s Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif. Pakistan’s government has not released details ahead of the meeting, but the authorities have declared a local holiday in Islamabad to limit public movement as part of security measures for the gathering. Islamabad traffic police have announced road diversions and advised motorists to use alternative routes to accommodate the movement of foreign delegations. During a previous meeting in Riyadh, the three sides had vowed to immediately implement what they said were their collective defence commitments, including arrangements for the rapid deployment of agreed-upon military forces and capabilities to Saudi Arabia.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: According to the agreement, the group’s secretariat has been established in Saudi Arabia, and retired Pakistani General Nauman Mahmood has been selected as its first secretary-general. He will also attend Friday’s meeting. The pact binds the parties for 10 years, after which they would need to give three months’ notice before leaving.

Cooperation (Noun)
सहयोग — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Cooperation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Alternative (Adjective)
विकल्प — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Alternative' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।

articles.title: Donald Trump urges Vladimir Putin to end ‘military aggression’ in Europe
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Donald Trump said he had requested Vladimir Putin when they met in China last week, adding that he thought it would help lead to a deal to end Moscow's grinding war in Ukraine

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: U.S. President Donald Trump said on Thursday (November 26, 2026) he had asked Vladimir Putin to "pull back all military aggression" against Europe, in a fresh shift in tone towards the Russian leader he called his friend just last week. Mr. Trump said he had requested Mr. Putin when they met in China last week, adding that he thought it would help lead to a deal to end Moscow's grinding war in Ukraine. "During my conversations in China with President Vladimir Putin, of Russia, I spent a lot of time talking about the fact that I would like to see President Putin pull back all Military aggression against territories throughout Europe," Mr. Trump said on his Truth Social network. Mr. Trump said he had done so "in the hopes that a Deal can be made between Russia and Ukraine, and made quickly." "I really believe this is a strong possibility," he added. The statement did not specify which territories Mr. Trump meant -- and did not specifically include Ukraine, which Russia invaded in February 2022, kicking off the largest war in Europe since World War II. European nations have been increasingly concerned by what they regard as Russian provocations, including three Russian cruise missiles landing in NATO-member Poland last week. In their joint statement on Wednesday (November 25), Mr. Trump and Mr. Rutte said they "discussed the importance of Russia avoiding any actions that intentionally, or unintentionally, expand the war." In a notable contrast with Mr. Trump's recent criticisms of Ukraine for striking targets deep inside Russia, the U.S. leader made no call for Kyiv to show similar restraint.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Speaking to reporters at his Mar-a-Lago estate in Florida on Thursday (November 26), Mr. Trump said he was unsure if Mr. Putin would be coming to the G20 summit next month in Miami, but "but if he wanted to come, he certainly can."

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #24 of 30 (27 NOV)

📰 Donald Trump urges Vladimir Putin to end ‘military aggression’ in Europe

📌 Published: 27 Nov 2026, 01:21:27 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Donald Trump said he had requested Vladimir Putin when they met in China last week, adding that he thought it would help lead to a deal to end Moscow's grinding war in Ukraine

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: U.S. President Donald Trump said on Thursday (November 26, 2026) he had asked Vladimir Putin to "pull back all military aggression" against Europe, in a fresh shift in tone towards the Russian leader he called his friend just last week. Mr. Trump said he had requested Mr. Putin when they met in China last week, adding that he thought it would help lead to a deal to end Moscow's grinding war in Ukraine. "During my conversations in China with President Vladimir Putin, of Russia, I spent a lot of time talking about the fact that I would like to see President Putin pull back all Military aggression against territories throughout Europe," Mr. Trump said on his Truth Social network. Mr. Trump said he had done so "in the hopes that a Deal can be made between Russia and Ukraine, and made quickly." "I really believe this is a strong possibility," he added. The statement did not specify which territories Mr. Trump meant -- and did not specifically include Ukraine, which Russia invaded in February 2022, kicking off the largest war in Europe since World War II. European nations have been increasingly concerned by what they regard as Russian provocations, including three Russian cruise missiles landing in NATO-member Poland last week. In their joint statement on Wednesday (November 25), Mr. Trump and Mr. Rutte said they "discussed the importance of Russia avoiding any actions that intentionally, or unintentionally, expand the war." In a notable contrast with Mr. Trump's recent criticisms of Ukraine for striking targets deep inside Russia, the U.S. leader made no call for Kyiv to show similar restraint.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Speaking to reporters at his Mar-a-Lago estate in Florida on Thursday (November 26), Mr. Trump said he was unsure if Mr. Putin would be coming to the G20 summit next month in Miami, but "but if he wanted to come, he certainly can."

Possibility (Noun)
संभावना — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Possibility' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।

Aggression (Noun)

✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Importance (Adjective / Verb)
महत्त्व — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Importance' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse  |  ✖ Ant: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable
Statement (Adjective)
कथन — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Statement' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile

A. Donald Trump said he had requested Vladimir Putin when they met in China last week, adding that he thought it would help lead to a deal to end...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Donald Trump urges Vladimir Putin to end ‘milita' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.

✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The findings suggest that changes in glucose metabolism may affect brain health earlier in adulthood than previously thought

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Young adults with progressively increasing fasting blood sugar may be more likely to have a poor cognitive functioning by midlife, according to a new study that tracked young adults for over three decades. The findings suggest that changes in glucose metabolism may affect brain health earlier in adulthood than previously thought. Participants who developed type 2 diabetes during the study also showed signs of structural brain changes, according to findings published in the Journal of the American Heart Association . "Diabetes is known to affect cognitive function, but cognitive impairment due to diabetes was once believed to happen mostly during childhood among people with Type 1 diabetes or after age 65 in people with Type 2 diabetes," lead author Regina Paradela, a post-doctoral researcher at the University of São Paulo Medical School in São Paulo, Brazil, said. "However, prediabetes and sustained elevated fasting blood sugar levels in adults without type 1 or type 2 diabetes may also have an increased risk of late-life cognitive decline and dementia," Paradela said. The researchers suggested early monitoring and management of blood sugar levels in young adulthood -- 18 to 30 years old -- might be a strategy to preserve brain health. Normal fasting blood glucose is generally below 100 milligrams per decilitre, 100-125 milligrams per decilitre indicates prediabetes and a value over 126 milligrams per decilitre is consistent with Type 2 diabetes. "The fact that increasing glucose levels were associated with poorer cognitive performance, even among people who had not developed Type 2 diabetes during the 30-year study, is very important," Paradela said. "This suggests that changes in glucose metabolism may be relevant to brain health earlier in adulthood than we typically think about," Paradela said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The study is among the first to investigate and compare the association between changes in fasting blood sugar levels from early adulthood to changes in cognition and brain structure in middle age, over approximately 30 years, the researchers said.

articles.summary: 1. Core Context & Background: The findings suggest that changes in glucose metabolism may affect brain health earlier in adulthood than previously thought
articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: The findings suggest that changes in glucose metabolism may affect brain health earlier in adulthood than previously thought
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Young adults with progressively increasing fasting blood sugar may be more likely to have a poor cognitive functioning by midlife, according to a new study that tracked young adults for over three decades. The findings suggest that changes in glucose metabolism may affect brain health earlier in adulthood than previously thought. Participants who developed type 2 diabetes during the study also showed signs of structural brain changes, according to findings published in the Journal of the American Heart Association . "Diabetes is known to affect cognitive function, but cognitive impairment due to diabetes was once believed to happen mostly during childhood among people with Type 1 diabetes or after age 65 in people with Type 2 diabetes," lead author Regina Paradela, a post-doctoral researcher at the University of São Paulo Medical School in São Paulo, Brazil, said. "However, prediabetes and sustained elevated fasting blood sugar levels in adults without type 1 or type 2 diabetes may also have an increased risk of late-life cognitive decline and dementia," Paradela said. The researchers suggested early monitoring and management of blood sugar levels in young adulthood -- 18 to 30 years old -- might be a strategy to preserve brain health. Normal fasting blood glucose is generally below 100 milligrams per decilitre, 100-125 milligrams per decilitre indicates prediabetes and a value over 126 milligrams per decilitre is consistent with Type 2 diabetes. "The fact that increasing glucose levels were associated with poorer cognitive performance, even among people who had not developed Type 2 diabetes during the 30-year study, is very important," Paradela said. "This suggests that changes in glucose metabolism may be relevant to brain health earlier in adulthood than we typically think about," Paradela said.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The study is among the first to investigate and compare the association between changes in fasting blood sugar levels from early adulthood to changes in cognition and brain structure in middle age, over approximately 30 years, the researchers said.

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: In a time of global tension, digital overload and endless advice about raising children, experts say 2027 calls for a radical rethink: less perfection, more presence

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Prem Kishore occasionally turns to Artificial Intelligence (AI) for help when it comes to raising his six-year-old son. “It’s the big feelings that can be difficult to talk about, because we don’t always have the right words. I usually seek advice from my friends or psychologists, but if they’re not available, I turn to AI,” says the creative professional, 43, who splits his time between Bengaluru and Dubai. Kishore recalls how he visited an AI video generator to create an avatar of a doctor, who chatted with his son about healthy boundaries and consent. As AI becomes more enmeshed in our day-to-day lives, families are turning to it for advice, research and assistance in managing the mental load of modern-day parenting. A 2026 consumer trends report by GIPSI, the research arm of agency Tonic Worldwide, combined search and social media data with a survey of 50,000 people, and found that 52% of Indian Gen Z parents now use AI instead of their usual search engines, and 48% use it as an adviser. In India, Google Gemini recently launched a series of commercials featuring Shah Rukh Khan in which he directs two fathers at very different stages of their parenting journeys towards the chatbot for advice. Apps such as Fambot and AVA seek to help families with administrative tasks by syncing to their calendars, email and online shopping orders. Eighteen years ago, when I first became a parent, Dr. Spock’s Baby and Child Care was the de facto gift to all new parents along with a Johnson & Johnson baby care set. I kept the book for a number of years after I had my second child and referred to it frequently. But today, new parents can seek advice from podcasts, influencers, online communities and yes, AI chatbots. There is a lot of advice out there, available in seconds. But how much of it is actually helping parents? Author-editor Sanjana Kapur, 40, who’s raising a nine-year-old in Bengaluru, admits that parenting feels a little nerve-racking today. “There’s so much information out there, that you’re constantly worrying if you’re making the right decision, or how even your smallest reaction will affect your child. The world has become such a complicated place, and parents are nervous even when kids are at school now,” she admits.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The Hindu Sunday Magazine / children / parent and child / technology (general) / OpenAI / Artificial Intelligence / human interest

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #26 of 30 (27 NOV)

📰 Parenting in an anxious age: What does ‘good enough’ look like?

📌 Published: 27 Nov 2026, 02:37:18 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: In a time of global tension, digital overload and endless advice about raising children, experts say 2027 calls for a radical rethink: less perfection, more presence

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Prem Kishore occasionally turns to Artificial Intelligence (AI) for help when it comes to raising his six-year-old son. “It’s the big feelings that can be difficult to talk about, because we don’t always have the right words. I usually seek advice from my friends or psychologists, but if they’re not available, I turn to AI,” says the creative professional, 43, who splits his time between Bengaluru and Dubai. Kishore recalls how he visited an AI video generator to create an avatar of a doctor, who chatted with his son about healthy boundaries and consent. As AI becomes more enmeshed in our day-to-day lives, families are turning to it for advice, research and assistance in managing the mental load of modern-day parenting. A 2026 consumer trends report by GIPSI, the research arm of agency Tonic Worldwide, combined search and social media data with a survey of 50,000 people, and found that 52% of Indian Gen Z parents now use AI instead of their usual search engines, and 48% use it as an adviser. In India, Google Gemini recently launched a series of commercials featuring Shah Rukh Khan in which he directs two fathers at very different stages of their parenting journeys towards the chatbot for advice. Apps such as Fambot and AVA seek to help families with administrative tasks by syncing to their calendars, email and online shopping orders. Eighteen years ago, when I first became a parent, Dr. Spock’s Baby and Child Care was the de facto gift to all new parents along with a Johnson & Johnson baby care set. I kept the book for a number of years after I had my second child and referred to it frequently. But today, new parents can seek advice from podcasts, influencers, online communities and yes, AI chatbots. There is a lot of advice out there, available in seconds. But how much of it is actually helping parents? Author-editor Sanjana Kapur, 40, who’s raising a nine-year-old in Bengaluru, admits that parenting feels a little nerve-racking today. “There’s so much information out there, that you’re constantly worrying if you’re making the right decision, or how even your smallest reaction will affect your child. The world has become such a complicated place, and parents are nervous even when kids are at school now,” she admits.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The Hindu Sunday Magazine / children / parent and child / technology (general) / OpenAI / Artificial Intelligence / human interest

articles.title: All to play for: On the World chess championship in Geneva
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Chess is one sport where both the young and the old can excel

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The World chess championship opened in Geneva with a game worthy of the occasion. Both the defending champion, D. Gukesh, and his challenger, Javokhir Sindarov, produced chess of top quality, and the draw was a just result . Given that the Indian was playing with black pieces and that he had gone into the match as the less favoured of the two, Gukesh could be a little happier with the game than his Uzbek rival. The Chennai Grandmaster was in considerable time trouble on multiple occasions, but managed to solve his problems and found proper answers to the questions posed to him on the board by the confident Sindarov. The match has only begun, and there is plenty of chess left. It is a long match of 14 games, played in the classical time control, and the man who reaches 7.5 points will be the champion. The well-contested opening game would have given Gukesh, and his team comprising his coach and ‘seconds’, enough confidence, after several disappointing performances since he became the youngest World champion in history , at 18, by defeating China’s Ding Liren in Singapore two years ago. That match too had gone down the wire, with Gukesh winning the last of the 14 games, thanks to a terrible mistake towards the end by his rival. Sindarov is just six months older than Gukesh, making the Geneva match the youngest in the 140-year-old history of the World championship: both players are 20. It is remarkable that Gukesh has already seen the highs and lows of life at such a young age. For his opponent, the last one year has been better than a dream: from World No. 26 he has risen to No. 4. Chess is getting younger. The next World championship could also very well have two young contenders. Grandmasters are usually said to peak when they are around 30 and chess is one game that even older players have continued to excel in. Viswanathan Anand was 48 when he won the World rapid chess championship . The match between Gukesh and Sindarov has attracted considerable interest from across the sporting world. After the 1972 match between Boris Spassky and Bobby Fischer — the defining moment of world chess — the World championship has earned a reputation as one of the planet’s most important sporting events. No battle between two of the world’s most talented men in chess has ever disappointed.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: chess / World Chess Championship 2026 / India / Singapore / history

✍️ Editorial & Opinion Paragraph #3 of 30 (26 NOV)

📰 All to play for: On the World chess championship in Geneva

📌 Published: 26 Nov 2026, 12:12:32 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Chess is one sport where both the young and the old can excel

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The World chess championship opened in Geneva with a game worthy of the occasion. Both the defending champion, D. Gukesh, and his challenger, Javokhir Sindarov, produced chess of top quality, and the draw was a just result . Given that the Indian was playing with black pieces and that he had gone into the match as the less favoured of the two, Gukesh could be a little happier with the game than his Uzbek rival. The Chennai Grandmaster was in considerable time trouble on multiple occasions, but managed to solve his problems and found proper answers to the questions posed to him on the board by the confident Sindarov. The match has only begun, and there is plenty of chess left. It is a long match of 14 games, played in the classical time control, and the man who reaches 7.5 points will be the champion. The well-contested opening game would have given Gukesh, and his team comprising his coach and ‘seconds’, enough confidence, after several disappointing performances since he became the youngest World champion in history , at 18, by defeating China’s Ding Liren in Singapore two years ago. That match too had gone down the wire, with Gukesh winning the last of the 14 games, thanks to a terrible mistake towards the end by his rival. Sindarov is just six months older than Gukesh, making the Geneva match the youngest in the 140-year-old history of the World championship: both players are 20. It is remarkable that Gukesh has already seen the highs and lows of life at such a young age. For his opponent, the last one year has been better than a dream: from World No. 26 he has risen to No. 4. Chess is getting younger. The next World championship could also very well have two young contenders. Grandmasters are usually said to peak when they are around 30 and chess is one game that even older players have continued to excel in. Viswanathan Anand was 48 when he won the World rapid chess championship . The match between Gukesh and Sindarov has attracted considerable interest from across the sporting world. After the 1972 match between Boris Spassky and Bobby Fischer — the defining moment of world chess — the World championship has earned a reputation as one of the planet’s most important sporting events. No battle between two of the world’s most talented men in chess has ever disappointed.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: chess / World Chess Championship 2026 / India / Singapore / history

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The eligibility criteria and procedures to be followed for CAS will be implemented ‘in strict adherence’ to guidelines issued through a G.O. of January 11, 2021.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Keeping up with its announcement made during the demand for grant on August 24, the Tamil Nadu Higher Education Department issued a Government Order (G.O.) on Tuesday, awarding Career Advancement Scheme (CAS) monetary benefits to teachers of government-aided Arts and Science colleges. According to the G.O., the government has sanctioned ₹11.75 crore as recurring monthly expenditure for awarding CAS to eligible teachers, with effect from September 1. A total of 6,116 teachers will benefit from the scheme. According to the G.O., the eligibility criteria and procedures to be followed for CAS will be implemented “in strict adherence” to guidelines issued through a G.O. of January 11, 2021. The scheme would be implemented only after proper verification of the eligibility of each teacher. A screening and selection committee will scrutinise promotion requests and applications, and the Regional Joint Director will forward the minutes and recommendations to the Director of Collegiate Education. After being vetted, the files would be sent back to the Regional Joint Director who would forward the same, along with service records, to audit teams nominated by the Director-General of Audit. After receiving the observations from the audit teams, the Regional Joint Director would issue relevant CAS orders.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The G.O. warns that the responsibility of any miscalculation or error would fall squarely on the officer who issues the CAS order. The excess amount paid will be recovered from the teacher, while action will be initiated against erring officials.

• 1. Core Context & Background: The eligibility criteria and procedures to be followed for CAS will be implemented ‘in strict adherence’ to guidelines issued through a G.O. of January 11, 2021.
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Keeping up with its announcement made during the demand for grant on August 24, the Tamil Nadu Higher Education Department issued a Government Order (G.O.) on Tuesday, awarding Career Advancement Scheme (CAS) monetary benefits to teachers of government-aided Arts and Science colleges. According to the G.O., the government has sanctioned ₹11.75 crore as recurring monthly expenditure for awarding CAS to eligible teachers, with effect from September 1. A total of 6,116 teachers will benefit from the scheme. According to the G.O., the eligibility criteria and procedures to be followed for CAS will be implemented “in strict adherence” to guidelines issued through a G.O. of January 11, 2021. The scheme would be implemented only after proper verification of the eligibility of each teacher. A screening and selection committee will scrutinise promotion requests and applications, and the Regional Joint Director will forward the minutes and recommendations to the Director of Collegiate Education. After being vetted, the files would be sent back to the Regional Joint Director who would forward the same, along with service records, to audit teams nominated by the Director-General of Audit. After receiving the observations from the audit teams, the Regional Joint Director would issue relevant CAS orders.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The G.O. warns that the responsibility of any miscalculation or error would fall squarely on the officer who issues the CAS order. The excess amount paid will be recovered from the teacher, while action will be initiated against erring officials.

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: A 31-year-old man was arrested by the Sathuvachari police in Vellore on Wednesday for killing his wife over a family dispute.

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Most of the collected wastes would be dumped at the 15 acre-landfill site near the Girivalam path

Officials of Tiruvannamalai Corporation said that apart from the civic body, sanitary workers of District Rural Development Agency (DRDA) were also roped in for the mammoth exercise, which was started on Monday, a day before Maha Deepam as the town witnessed steady flow of pilgrims. “Rain also delayed removal of garbage on streets and the Girivalam Path. Nonetheless, sanitary workers worked round-the-clock, in shifts, to keep the town clean of wastes,” K. Balasubramanian, Corporation Commissioner, told The Hindu. Around 45 lakh devotees visited the town on Maha Deepam day. Disposable food plates formed the majority of waste, followed by those of sugarcane and sweet corn. District administration has allowed 250 individuals and organisations for annadhanam (free food). Many volunteers and groups were also provided free food on the day.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Most of the collected wastes would be dumped at the 15 acre-landfill site of the civic body near the Girivalam path. Food and other organic wastes would be recycled to make manure for farming and terrace gardens in Tiruvannamalai.

articles.title: Large-sized pancreatic stones removed via keyhole surgery
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: A 41-year-old male patient got relief from debilitating pain after large-sized pancreatic stones measuring up to 3 cm were removed through laparoscopic surgery at a city hospital. The patient, who was diagnosed with acute-on-chronic calcific pancreatitis accompanied by pancreatic diabetes, had severely atrophic pancreas.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A team of surgeons led by surgical gastroenterologist and director at GEM Hospital P. Senthilnathan extracted the calculi with zero abdominal scars or stitches. The patient was discharged just four days after the surgery. Speaking to presspersons on Wednesday, he said that in chronic calcific pancreatitis, stones accumulate in the central duct and cause severe blockages, excruciating pain, and secondary diabetes. “If left untreated, chronic inflammation can even increase the risk of pancreatic cancer. While smaller stones can be managed medically or endoscopically, large stones require surgery.“ The pancreas was choked with dozens of stones, including giant calculi measuring 3 cm x 1 cm lodged across the head, neck, and tail of the main pancreatic duct, and stones up to 2 cm x 2 cm trapped inside the minor duct, he added.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: As these stones sit dangerously close to major blood vessels, they must be extracted without fracturing or damaging the surrounding tissue, which is why such cases are almost universally managed through traditional open surgery, Dr. Senthilnathan added.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #12 of 30 (26 NOV)

📰 Large-sized pancreatic stones removed via keyhole surgery

📌 Published: 26 Nov 2026, 12:27:37 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: A 41-year-old male patient got relief from debilitating pain after large-sized pancreatic stones measuring up to 3 cm were removed through laparoscopic surgery at a city hospital. The patient, who was diagnosed with acute-on-chronic calcific pancreatitis accompanied by pancreatic diabetes, had severely atrophic pancreas.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A team of surgeons led by surgical gastroenterologist and director at GEM Hospital P. Senthilnathan extracted the calculi with zero abdominal scars or stitches. The patient was discharged just four days after the surgery. Speaking to presspersons on Wednesday, he said that in chronic calcific pancreatitis, stones accumulate in the central duct and cause severe blockages, excruciating pain, and secondary diabetes. “If left untreated, chronic inflammation can even increase the risk of pancreatic cancer. While smaller stones can be managed medically or endoscopically, large stones require surgery.“ The pancreas was choked with dozens of stones, including giant calculi measuring 3 cm x 1 cm lodged across the head, neck, and tail of the main pancreatic duct, and stones up to 2 cm x 2 cm trapped inside the minor duct, he added.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: As these stones sit dangerously close to major blood vessels, they must be extracted without fracturing or damaging the surrounding tissue, which is why such cases are almost universally managed through traditional open surgery, Dr. Senthilnathan added.

articles.title: IAPEN summit adopts national declaration on muscle loss and sarcopenia
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The Indian Association of Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition (IAPEN), Chennai Chapter, adopted the Sarcopenia Declaration at Beyond Calories 2026, its national gastrointestinal nutrition summit organised in association with SIMS Hospitals in Chennai on November 25.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The declaration calls for early screening for sarcopenia, setting protein intake targets, regular strength exercise and early mobilisation and rehabilitation after illness, including post-intensive care follow-up. It also emphasises professional education, India-specific research and the development of diagnostic cut-offs suited to Indian populations. It urges policymakers to include sarcopenia in national healthy-ageing and non-communicable disease programmes, particularly focusing on rural and low-income communities. Sarcopenia is the progressive loss of muscle mass, strength and function. It can occur with ageing and is accelerated by inadequate nutrition, physical inactivity and chronic diseases. It increases the risk of falls, fractures, disability, delayed recovery from illness or surgery and loss of independence. Doctors at the summit cited data showing that 43.6% of Indians aged 60 and above have sarcopenia, with 19.4% having its severe form. They noted that the condition also affects younger people, particularly those with chronic illnesses, poor nutrition and sedentary lifestyles.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The summit featured talks by specialists in surgical gastroenterology, critical care and nutrition.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #26 of 30 (26 NOV)

📰 IAPEN summit adopts national declaration on muscle loss and sarcopenia

📌 Published: 26 Nov 2026, 12:09:46 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The Indian Association of Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition (IAPEN), Chennai Chapter, adopted the Sarcopenia Declaration at Beyond Calories 2026, its national gastrointestinal nutrition summit organised in association with SIMS Hospitals in Chennai on November 25.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The declaration calls for early screening for sarcopenia, setting protein intake targets, regular strength exercise and early mobilisation and rehabilitation after illness, including post-intensive care follow-up. It also emphasises professional education, India-specific research and the development of diagnostic cut-offs suited to Indian populations. It urges policymakers to include sarcopenia in national healthy-ageing and non-communicable disease programmes, particularly focusing on rural and low-income communities. Sarcopenia is the progressive loss of muscle mass, strength and function. It can occur with ageing and is accelerated by inadequate nutrition, physical inactivity and chronic diseases. It increases the risk of falls, fractures, disability, delayed recovery from illness or surgery and loss of independence. Doctors at the summit cited data showing that 43.6% of Indians aged 60 and above have sarcopenia, with 19.4% having its severe form. They noted that the condition also affects younger people, particularly those with chronic illnesses, poor nutrition and sedentary lifestyles.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The summit featured talks by specialists in surgical gastroenterology, critical care and nutrition.

articles.title: Right to choose a partner is an aspect of constitutional freedom, not a privilege granted by a family, caste or community: Thirumavalavan
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: In his memorandum to Chairperson of Tamil Nadu Commission for the Prevention of Honour Killings, Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi founder and Chidambaram MP, Thol. Thirumavalavan said, “the right to choose one’s partner is not a privilege granted by a family, caste or community” but “an aspect of the constitutional freedom and dignity of every individual”.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: In his request to the Commission headed by Justice K.N. Basha, Mr. Thirumavalavan said that the Commission should “recommend the enactment of a comprehensive Tamil Nadu law against honour killings and honour-based crimes, with a broad definition rooted in the right to choose a partner and individual autonomy”. He further urged the Commission to provide a framework to address “collective and mob-based honour violence”, which would ensure that “every person who intentionally participates in, instigates, facilitates or enables the crime can be held accountable under clearly defined standards of criminal responsibility”. The VCK leader further said that enforceable duties and penalties should be imposed on police and public officials who fail to protect couples despite credible threats, including wilful refusal to register complaints, disclosure of confidential information and dereliction of preventive duties.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Mr. Thirumavalavan also demanded that there exist comprehensive protection for couples, survivors, witnesses and their families, including safehouses, relocation, legal aid, counselling, medical care, compensation and rehabilitation. He also appealed to the Commission to submit “a draft Bill and a time-bound implementation framework to the Government of Tamil Nadu, with budgetary allocations, monitoring arrangements and annual reporting to the Legislature”.

hinglishTracks.en: He also appealed to the Commission to submit “a draft Bill and a time-bound implementation framework to the Government of Tamil Nadu, with budgetary allocations, monitoring arrangements and annual reporting to the Legislature”.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — उन्होंने आयोग से "बजटीय आवंटन, निगरानी व्यवस्था और विधानमंडल को वार्षिक रिपोर्टिंग के साथ तमिलनाडु सरकार को एक मसौदा विधेयक और एक समयबद्ध कार्यान्वयन ढांचा" प्रस्तुत करने की भी अपील की।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Implementation' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: क्रियान्वयन / ज़मीनी स्तर पर लागू करना — किसी योजना या फैसले को असलियत में पूरा करना। इसके Synonyms हैं: Execution, Enforcement, Fulfillment और Antonyms हैं: Abandonment, Neglect, Cancellation।

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #10 of 30 (26 NOV)

📰 Right to choose a partner is an aspect of constitutional freedom, not a privilege granted by a family, caste or community: Thirumavalavan

📌 Published: 26 Nov 2026, 01:45:56 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: In his memorandum to Chairperson of Tamil Nadu Commission for the Prevention of Honour Killings, Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi founder and Chidambaram MP, Thol. Thirumavalavan said, “the right to choose one’s partner is not a privilege granted by a family, caste or community” but “an aspect of the constitutional freedom and dignity of every individual”.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: In his request to the Commission headed by Justice K.N. Basha, Mr. Thirumavalavan said that the Commission should “recommend the enactment of a comprehensive Tamil Nadu law against honour killings and honour-based crimes, with a broad definition rooted in the right to choose a partner and individual autonomy”. He further urged the Commission to provide a framework to address “collective and mob-based honour violence”, which would ensure that “every person who intentionally participates in, instigates, facilitates or enables the crime can be held accountable under clearly defined standards of criminal responsibility”. The VCK leader further said that enforceable duties and penalties should be imposed on police and public officials who fail to protect couples despite credible threats, including wilful refusal to register complaints, disclosure of confidential information and dereliction of preventive duties.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Mr. Thirumavalavan also demanded that there exist comprehensive protection for couples, survivors, witnesses and their families, including safehouses, relocation, legal aid, counselling, medical care, compensation and rehabilitation. He also appealed to the Commission to submit “a draft Bill and a time-bound implementation framework to the Government of Tamil Nadu, with budgetary allocations, monitoring arrangements and annual reporting to the Legislature”.

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Enforcement (Noun)
सख्ती से कानून लागू करना — किसी नियम या आदेश का ज़मीनी स्तर पर पालन करवाना।
✓ Syn: Implementation, Execution, Administration  |  ✖ Ant: Neglect, Abandonment, Waiver
Implementation (Noun)
क्रियान्वयन / ज़मीनी स्तर पर लागू करना — किसी योजना या फैसले को असलियत में पूरा करना।
✓ Syn: Execution, Enforcement, Fulfillment  |  ✖ Ant: Abandonment, Neglect, Cancellation
Constitutional (Adjective)
संवैधानिक — देश के संविधान (Constitution) के दायरे और मौलिक अधिकारों के अनुरूप।
✓ Syn: Statutory, Legitimate, Lawful  |  ✖ Ant: Unconstitutional, Illegal, Arbitrary
Accountability (Noun)
जवाबदेही — अपने फैसलों और काम का जनता तथा संविधान को हिसाब देने की बाध्यता।
✓ Syn: Responsibility, Answerability, Liability  |  ✖ Ant: Immunity, Exemption, Irresponsibility

articles.title: Kallakurichi TVK MLA Arul Vignesh summoned for questioning in harassment case
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Police personnel have been deployed in strength at the MLA’s office in Kallakurichi

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Kallakurichi All Women Police on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) served summons on Kallakurichi TVK MLA C. Arul Vignesh directing him to appear for questioning in connection with a harassment case registered against him on a complaint lodged by a woman IAS officer. Inspector Bhuvaneshwari attached to the All Women Police station visited the MLA’s house in Kallakurichi and handed the summons to him in person. The police also questioned Arul Vignesh at the house. The woman IAS officer had submitted a formal complaint to the Kallakurichi district Superintendent of Police on Monday (November 23), accusing the MLA of making inappropriate advances and sending unwarranted messages. The police have booked a case against the MLA invoking provisions of the Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Harassment of Women Act and Sections 75, 78 and 79 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. Police sources said that Tiruppur Superintendent of Police Shristi Singh, who has been appointed as the Investigating Officer in the criminal case, began preliminary investigation into the incident on Wednesday after receiving the inquiry report from Kallakurichi Superintendent of Police I. Shahnaz at the All Women Police Station. Inspector General of Police (Administration) N. Kamini has been appointed to supervise the investigation. The National Commission for Women had earlier taken suo moto cognisance of the allegations and asked the Tamil Nadu Director General of Police to conduct an impartial inquiry. In the morning, more than 30 Democratic Youth Federation of India (DYFI) activists were arrested when they attempted to lay siege to the office of Kallakurichi TVK MLA, demanding his resignation over the allegations against him. The protesters raised slogans alleging lack of safety for women. The DMK’s women wing also staged a demonstration at the Four Roads junction in Kallakurichi demanding the arrest of the MLA. They burnt the effigy of the MLA and raised slogans against him.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Meanwhile, police personnel have been deployed in strength at the MLA’s office in Kallakurichi.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #11 of 30 (26 NOV)

📰 Kallakurichi TVK MLA Arul Vignesh summoned for questioning in harassment case

📌 Published: 26 Nov 2026, 01:42:18 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Police personnel have been deployed in strength at the MLA’s office in Kallakurichi

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Kallakurichi All Women Police on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) served summons on Kallakurichi TVK MLA C. Arul Vignesh directing him to appear for questioning in connection with a harassment case registered against him on a complaint lodged by a woman IAS officer. Inspector Bhuvaneshwari attached to the All Women Police station visited the MLA’s house in Kallakurichi and handed the summons to him in person. The police also questioned Arul Vignesh at the house. The woman IAS officer had submitted a formal complaint to the Kallakurichi district Superintendent of Police on Monday (November 23), accusing the MLA of making inappropriate advances and sending unwarranted messages. The police have booked a case against the MLA invoking provisions of the Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Harassment of Women Act and Sections 75, 78 and 79 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. Police sources said that Tiruppur Superintendent of Police Shristi Singh, who has been appointed as the Investigating Officer in the criminal case, began preliminary investigation into the incident on Wednesday after receiving the inquiry report from Kallakurichi Superintendent of Police I. Shahnaz at the All Women Police Station. Inspector General of Police (Administration) N. Kamini has been appointed to supervise the investigation. The National Commission for Women had earlier taken suo moto cognisance of the allegations and asked the Tamil Nadu Director General of Police to conduct an impartial inquiry. In the morning, more than 30 Democratic Youth Federation of India (DYFI) activists were arrested when they attempted to lay siege to the office of Kallakurichi TVK MLA, demanding his resignation over the allegations against him. The protesters raised slogans alleging lack of safety for women. The DMK’s women wing also staged a demonstration at the Four Roads junction in Kallakurichi demanding the arrest of the MLA. They burnt the effigy of the MLA and raised slogans against him.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Meanwhile, police personnel have been deployed in strength at the MLA’s office in Kallakurichi.

articles.title: No permission sought for November 26 anti-SIR march, Delhi Police say; organisers say ‘intimation’ sent
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: People Against SIR emailed the police details of the proposed Constitution Day march from Valmiki Sadan to Jantar Mantar; the police, however, say they have received no such communication and warn that Section 163 of BNSS remains in force in the area

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: No permission has been sought from the Delhi Police for a protest march against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls , scheduled for November 26 , senior New Delhi police officials said. The organisers, however, maintained that they had intimated the police about the proposed demonstration. The Delhi wing of the People Against SIR platform has called for a march on Constitution Day from Valmiki Sadan on Mandir Marg towards Jantar Mantar. The protesters are demanding the scrapping of SIR and the restoration of Jantar Mantar as a designated site for peaceful protests, among other demands. An email dated November 23, 2026, seen by The Hindu , was sent to the Delhi Police to inform them about the proposed programme. It stated: “This is to inform you that we, the Delhi People Against SIR, are going to observe Constitution Day as per the details given.” The email further stated that participants would assemble outside Valmiki Sadan on Mandir Marg at 12.30 p.m. on November 26 and march towards Jantar Mantar via Kali Bari Marg. “This is for your information and any follow-up/arrangements,” it added. “We make sure not to ask for permission but only inform the police about the march,” Maimoona Mollah, a representative of the platform, told The Hindu . Ms. Mollah claimed that the police had acknowledged the intimation and subsequently sought further details, including the proposed route and the expected number of participants expected. These details, she said, were shared with the police over a telephone conversation. The organisers have also announced plans to burn copies of the SIR notification during the demonstration. Public notice 🔶Information has been received that Samyukta Kisan Morcha and other activists are planning a protest march from Kali Bari to Jantar Mantar on 26.11.2026. No application for permission has been received and no permission has been granted for the said march. 🔶Section 163 BNSS, 2023, is in force in New Delhi District. Unauthorised gatherings, processions, demonstrations, speeches, sloganeering and dharnas are prohibited. 🔶All are requested to comply with the order u/s 163 BNSS and cooperate with Police. Violations will invite legal action. However, New Delhi police officers denied receiving the intimation and stressed that prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) remain in force in the area and warned that action would be taken against gatherings in violation of the restrictions. The police said “preventive” security measures would be put in place to prevent any unauthorised gathering in the area. These would include multi-layer barricading, deployment of additional personnel and preventive detentions, if required, to disperse crowds and prevent protesters from assembling in violation of the prohibitory orders.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: People Against SIR was formed on October 14 following an emergency consultation in Delhi attended by representatives of more than 200 organisations. The national platform brings together 145 civil society groups, farmers’ unions, workers’ organisations, and women’s and youth groups across 18 States to campaign against the SIR exercise.
