hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — भारतीय चिकित्सा अनुसंधान परिषद (आईसीएमआर) के एक नए राष्ट्रीय सर्वेक्षण के अनुसार, लगभग दो-तिहाई भारतीय किशोरों में विटामिन बी12 की कमी है, जो मस्तिष्क के विकास, स्वस्थ तंत्रिका कार्य और लाल रक्त कोशिकाओं के निर्माण के लिए आवश्यक सूक्ष्म पोषक तत्व है।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Developmental' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: विकास संबंधी — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Developmental' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive और Antonyms हैं: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile।

hinglishTracks.en: The findings raise concerns about the long-term consequences of nutritional deficiencies across generations, particularly among children, adolescents, and pregnant women.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — निष्कर्ष पीढ़ियों, विशेषकर बच्चों, किशोरों और गर्भवती महिलाओं में पोषण संबंधी कमी के दीर्घकालिक परिणामों के बारे में चिंता जताते हैं।।

hinglishTracks.en: The Survey for Assessment of Markers of Population Health, Activity, Diet and Anthropometry (SAMPADA), conducted by ICMR’s National Institute of Nutrition during 2023–25, found vitamin B12 deficiency in 66.1% of adolescent boys and 65.4% of adolescent girls.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — 2023-25 ​​के दौरान आईसीएमआर के राष्ट्रीय पोषण संस्थान द्वारा आयोजित जनसंख्या स्वास्थ्य, गतिविधि, आहार और मानवमिति (SAMPADA) के मार्करों के आकलन के लिए सर्वेक्षण में 66.1% किशोर लड़कों और 65.4% किशोर लड़कियों में विटामिन बी 12 की कमी पाई गई।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Institutional' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: संस्थागत — देश की संवैधानिक या सरकारी संस्थाओं के नियमों और ढांचे से जुड़ा हुआ। इसके Synonyms हैं: Systemic, Organizational, Constitutional और Antonyms हैं: Individual, Informal, Unorganized।

hinglishTracks.en: The prevalence was 63.1% among pregnant women, 60.4% among adult men aged 20–59, and 57.4% among women aged 15–49.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — गर्भवती महिलाओं में इसका प्रसार 63.1%, 20-59 आयु वर्ग के वयस्क पुरुषों में 60.4% और 15-49 आयु वर्ग की महिलाओं में 57.4% था।।

hinglishTracks.en: Even among children aged five to nine, 46.5% were deficient.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — यहां तक ​​कि पांच से नौ साल के बच्चों में भी 46.5% में कमी थी।।

hinglishTracks.en: The survey, which analysed over 1.7 lakh blood samples from a population of more than two lakh people across 183 districts and 35 States and Union Territories, defined deficiency as serum vitamin B12 levels below 203 pg/mL.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — सर्वेक्षण, जिसमें 183 जिलों और 35 राज्यों और केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों में दो लाख से अधिक लोगों की आबादी से 1.7 लाख से अधिक रक्त नमूनों का विश्लेषण किया गया, ने 203 पीजी / एमएल से नीचे सीरम विटामिन बी 12 के स्तर की कमी को परिभाषित किया।।

hinglishTracks.en: Vitamin B12 plays a critical role in DNA synthesis, red blood cell formation, and maintenance of the protective covering around nerves.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — विटामिन बी12 डीएनए संश्लेषण, लाल रक्त कोशिका निर्माण और तंत्रिकाओं के चारों ओर सुरक्षात्मक आवरण के रखरखाव में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाता है।।

hinglishTracks.en: Prolonged deficiency can cause peripheral neuropathy, impaired balance, memory problems, and, in severe cases, irreversible neurological damage.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — लंबे समय तक कमी से परिधीय न्यूरोपैथी, बिगड़ा हुआ संतुलन, स्मृति समस्याएं और, गंभीर मामलों में, अपरिवर्तनीय न्यूरोलॉजिकल क्षति हो सकती है।।

hinglishTracks.en: In infants, severe deficiency can result in developmental delays and neurological impairment.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — शिशुओं में, गंभीर कमी के परिणामस्वरूप विकासात्मक देरी और तंत्रिका संबंधी हानि हो सकती है।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Developmental' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: विकास संबंधी — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Developmental' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive और Antonyms हैं: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile।

hinglishTracks.en: “Research conducted in Pune over the past three decades has shown that vitamin B12 deficiency is common among adolescents and women of reproductive age, with important implications for the health of future generations.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — “पिछले तीन दशकों में पुणे में किए गए शोध से पता चला है कि किशोरों और प्रजनन आयु की महिलाओं में विटामिन बी 12 की कमी आम है, जिसका भविष्य की पीढ़ियों के स्वास्थ्य पर महत्वपूर्ण प्रभाव पड़ता है।।

hinglishTracks.en: Low maternal B12 status, particularly when accompanied by high folate levels, has been associated with increased fat accumulation and insulin resistance in children, potentially predisposing them to diabetes and other non-communicable diseases later in life.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — कम मातृ बी12 स्थिति, विशेष रूप से उच्च फोलेट स्तर के साथ, बच्चों में वसा संचय और इंसुलिन प्रतिरोध में वृद्धि से जुड़ी हुई है, जो संभावित रूप से बाद में जीवन में मधुमेह और अन्य गैर-संचारी रोगों का कारण बनती है।।

hinglishTracks.en: These effects are believed to be linked to epigenetic programming arising from nutritional imbalances before conception and during pregnancy,’’ said Chittaranjan Yajnik, director, Diabetes Unit, KEM Hospital, Pune.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — ऐसा माना जाता है कि ये प्रभाव गर्भधारण से पहले और गर्भावस्था के दौरान पोषण संबंधी असंतुलन से उत्पन्न होने वाले एपिजेनेटिक प्रोग्रामिंग से जुड़े होते हैं,'' पुणे के केईएम अस्पताल की मधुमेह इकाई के निदेशक चित्तरंजन याज्ञिक ने कहा।।

hinglishTracks.en: He added that India must move beyond an exclusive focus on iron and folic acid and consider including physiological doses of B12 in supplementation programmes for women, alongside carefully planned food fortification, improved nutrition literacy among adolescents, particularly girls, and the generation of robust, India-specific evidence to establish appropriate nutritional requirements and interventions.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — उन्होंने कहा कि भारत को आयरन और फोलिक एसिड पर विशेष ध्यान देने से आगे बढ़ना चाहिए और महिलाओं के लिए पूरक कार्यक्रमों में बी 12 की शारीरिक खुराक को शामिल करने पर विचार करना चाहिए, साथ ही सावधानीपूर्वक योजनाबद्ध खाद्य सुदृढ़ीकरण, किशोरों, विशेष रूप से लड़कियों के बीच बेहतर पोषण साक्षरता और उचित पोषण संबंधी आवश्यकताओं और हस्तक्षेपों को स्थापित करने के लिए मजबूत, भारत-विशिष्ट साक्ष्य तैयार करना चाहिए।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Supplementation' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: अनुपूरण — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Supplementation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Significant, Substantial, Strategic और Antonyms हैं: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial।

hinglishTracks.en: The findings are particularly significant for maternal and child health, with nearly two-thirds of pregnant women showing a deficiency.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — ये निष्कर्ष मातृ एवं शिशु स्वास्थ्य के लिए विशेष रूप से महत्वपूर्ण हैं, लगभग दो-तिहाई गर्भवती महिलाओं में कमी देखी गई है।।

hinglishTracks.en: Low maternal B12 levels have been associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes, including neural tube defects and low birth weight, as well as poorer offspring developmental outcomes.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — मातृ बी12 का निम्न स्तर गर्भावस्था के प्रतिकूल परिणामों से जुड़ा हुआ है, जिसमें न्यूरल ट्यूब दोष और जन्म के समय कम वजन के साथ-साथ संतान के खराब विकासात्मक परिणाम भी शामिल हैं।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Developmental' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: विकास संबंधी — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Developmental' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive और Antonyms हैं: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile।

hinglishTracks.en: Vitamin B12 is found naturally in foods such as meat, fish, eggs, and dairy products.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — विटामिन बी12 प्राकृतिक रूप से मांस, मछली, अंडे और डेयरी उत्पादों जैसे खाद्य पदार्थों में पाया जाता है।।

hinglishTracks.en: Inadequate dietary intake, particularly among people consuming predominantly plant-based diets, and impaired absorption can contribute to deficiency.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — अपर्याप्त आहार का सेवन, विशेष रूप से मुख्य रूप से पौधे-आधारित आहार का सेवन करने वाले लोगों में, और बिगड़ा हुआ अवशोषण कमी में योगदान कर सकता है।।

hinglishTracks.en: The findings also raise questions about whether India’s nutrition programmes are adequately addressing deficiencies beyond iron and folic acid.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — निष्कर्ष यह भी सवाल उठाते हैं कि क्या भारत के पोषण कार्यक्रम आयरन और फोलिक एसिड से परे कमियों को पर्याप्त रूप से संबोधित कर रहे हैं।।

hinglishTracks.en: The Anemia Mukt Bharat strategy focuses substantially on iron and folic acid supplementation, testing and treatment of anaemia, deworming, and food fortification.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — एनीमिया मुक्त भारत रणनीति आयरन और फोलिक एसिड अनुपूरण, एनीमिया के परीक्षण और उपचार, कृमि मुक्ति और खाद्य सुदृढ़ीकरण पर काफी हद तक केंद्रित है।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Supplementation' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: अनुपूरण — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Supplementation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Significant, Substantial, Strategic और Antonyms हैं: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial।

hinglishTracks.en: Although fortified rice includes vitamin B12, routine B12 screening and supplementation are not central components of the programme.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — हालाँकि फोर्टिफाइड चावल में विटामिन बी12 शामिल है, नियमित बी12 स्क्रीनिंग और अनुपूरण कार्यक्रम के केंद्रीय घटक नहीं हैं।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Supplementation' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: अनुपूरण — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Supplementation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Significant, Substantial, Strategic और Antonyms हैं: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial।

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #29 of 30 (26 NOV)

📰 Two-thirds of adolescents in India are deficient in vitamin B12: ICMR survey

📌 Published: 26 Nov 2026, 08:05:44 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Findings raise concerns about the long-term consequences of nutritional deficiencies across generations, particularly among children, adolescents, and pregnant women

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Nearly two-thirds of Indian adolescents are deficient in vitamin B12, a micronutrient essential for brain development, healthy nerve function, and the formation of red blood cells, according to a new national survey by the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR). The findings raise concerns about the long-term consequences of nutritional deficiencies across generations, particularly among children, adolescents, and pregnant women. The Survey for Assessment of Markers of Population Health, Activity, Diet and Anthropometry (SAMPADA), conducted by ICMR’s National Institute of Nutrition during 2023–25, found vitamin B12 deficiency in 66.1% of adolescent boys and 65.4% of adolescent girls. The prevalence was 63.1% among pregnant women, 60.4% among adult men aged 20–59, and 57.4% among women aged 15–49. Even among children aged five to nine, 46.5% were deficient. The survey, which analysed over 1.7 lakh blood samples from a population of more than two lakh people across 183 districts and 35 States and Union Territories, defined deficiency as serum vitamin B12 levels below 203 pg/mL. Vitamin B12 plays a critical role in DNA synthesis, red blood cell formation, and maintenance of the protective covering around nerves. Prolonged deficiency can cause peripheral neuropathy, impaired balance, memory problems, and, in severe cases, irreversible neurological damage. In infants, severe deficiency can result in developmental delays and neurological impairment. “Research conducted in Pune over the past three decades has shown that vitamin B12 deficiency is common among adolescents and women of reproductive age, with important implications for the health of future generations. Low maternal B12 status, particularly when accompanied by high folate levels, has been associated with increased fat accumulation and insulin resistance in children, potentially predisposing them to diabetes and other non-communicable diseases later in life. These effects are believed to be linked to epigenetic programming arising from nutritional imbalances before conception and during pregnancy,’’ said Chittaranjan Yajnik, director, Diabetes Unit, KEM Hospital, Pune. He added that India must move beyond an exclusive focus on iron and folic acid and consider including physiological doses of B12 in supplementation programmes for women, alongside carefully planned food fortification, improved nutrition literacy among adolescents, particularly girls, and the generation of robust, India-specific evidence to establish appropriate nutritional requirements and interventions. The findings are particularly significant for maternal and child health, with nearly two-thirds of pregnant women showing a deficiency. Low maternal B12 levels have been associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes, including neural tube defects and low birth weight, as well as poorer offspring developmental outcomes. Vitamin B12 is found naturally in foods such as meat, fish, eggs, and dairy products. Inadequate dietary intake, particularly among people consuming predominantly plant-based diets, and impaired absorption can contribute to deficiency.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The findings also raise questions about whether India’s nutrition programmes are adequately addressing deficiencies beyond iron and folic acid. The Anemia Mukt Bharat strategy focuses substantially on iron and folic acid supplementation, testing and treatment of anaemia, deworming, and food fortification. articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: Findings raise concerns about the long-term consequences of nutritional deficiencies across generations, particularly among children, adolescents, and pregnant women
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Nearly two-thirds of Indian adolescents are deficient in vitamin B12, a micronutrient essential for brain development, healthy nerve function, and the formation of red blood cells, according to a new national survey by the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR). The findings raise concerns about the long-term consequences of nutritional deficiencies across generations, particularly among children, adolescents, and pregnant women. The Survey for Assessment of Markers of Population Health, Activity, Diet and Anthropometry (SAMPADA), conducted by ICMR’s National Institute of Nutrition during 2023–25, found vitamin B12 deficiency in 66.1% of adolescent boys and 65.4% of adolescent girls. The prevalence was 63.1% among pregnant women, 60.4% among adult men aged 20–59, and 57.4% among women aged 15–49. Even among children aged five to nine, 46.5% were deficient. The survey, which analysed over 1.7 lakh blood samples from a population of more than two lakh people across 183 districts and 35 States and Union Territories, defined deficiency as serum vitamin B12 levels below 203 pg/mL. Vitamin B12 plays a critical role in DNA synthesis, red blood cell formation, and maintenance of the protective covering around nerves. Prolonged deficiency can cause peripheral neuropathy, impaired balance, memory problems, and, in severe cases, irreversible neurological damage. In infants, severe deficiency can result in developmental delays and neurological impairment. “Research conducted in Pune over the past three decades has shown that vitamin B12 deficiency is common among adolescents and women of reproductive age, with important implications for the health of future generations. Low maternal B12 status, particularly when accompanied by high folate levels, has been associated with increased fat accumulation and insulin resistance in children, potentially predisposing them to diabetes and other non-communicable diseases later in life. These effects are believed to be linked to epigenetic programming arising from nutritional imbalances before conception and during pregnancy,’’ said Chittaranjan Yajnik, director, Diabetes Unit, KEM Hospital, Pune. He added that India must move beyond an exclusive focus on iron and folic acid and consider including physiological doses of B12 in supplementation programmes for women, alongside carefully planned food fortification, improved nutrition literacy among adolescents, particularly girls, and the generation of robust, India-specific evidence to establish appropriate nutritional requirements and interventions. The findings are particularly significant for maternal and child health, with nearly two-thirds of pregnant women showing a deficiency. Low maternal B12 levels have been associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes, including neural tube defects and low birth weight, as well as poorer offspring developmental outcomes. Vitamin B12 is found naturally in foods such as meat, fish, eggs, and dairy products. Inadequate dietary intake, particularly among people consuming predominantly plant-based diets, and impaired absorption can contribute to deficiency.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The findings also raise questions about whether India’s nutrition programmes are adequately addressing deficiencies beyond iron and folic acid. The Anemia Mukt Bharat strategy focuses substantially on iron and folic acid supplementation, testing and treatment of anaemia, deworming, and food fortification. Although fortified rice includes vitamin B12, routine B12 screening and supplementation are not central components of the programme.

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The first phase of the Gram Panchaya elections were conduced peacefully across Markapuram, Prakasam and SPSR Nellore districts on Thursday.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Nearly 1.20 lakh voters out of the total 1.47 lakh exercised their right to vote during elections across 90 Gram Panchayats in six mandals of Markapuram district with a turnout of 81.70%. About 80.27% voter turnout was recorded with 1.55 lakh people among the total 1.93 lakh voters exercised their franchise during the elections across 81 Gram Panchayats in eight mandals of Prakasam district. While the notification has been issued for conducting elections in 139 panchayats, candidates were elected unanimously in 62 panchayats. Similarly, 782 ward members have been elected unopposed. In Kandukuru Municipality, 76.07% voter turnout was recorded during the polling for its 40 wards. Out of the 47,473 voters, 36,114 people exercise their franchise in the elections. In Kavali division of SPSR Nellore district, the first phase elections were scheduled for 134 Gram Panchayats. Of these, 17 Panchayats were elected unanimous, while polling took place in 117 Panchayats. Among these 117 in eight mandals of the district, Sarpanches were elected unanimously in three Panchayats. Over 1.93 lakh out of total 2.39 lakh voters across 114 Panchayats with a turnout of 80.60%. Gudur and Kavali Municipalities have witnessed voter turnout of 56.40% and 68.92% respectively. Out of total 80,492 voters in Gudur, 45,400 polled, while 58,884 polled among the overall 85,433 voters in Kavali. Nellore Collector Himanshu Shukla said that the polling concluded peacefully. “The public showed great interest in the Sarpanch elections, with a higher participation rate compared to general elections,” he said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: He personally visited Sunnambatti in Dagadarthi mandal, as well as Viswanatharaopeta and KK Gunta villages in Bogolu mandal, to inspect the polling process. He inquired about the poll management process.

Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Nearly 1.20 lakh voters out of the total 1.47 lakh exercised their right to vote during elections across 90 Gram Panchayats in six mandals of Markapuram district with a turnout of 81.70%. While the notification has been issued for conducting elections in 139 panchayats, candidates were elected unanimously in 62 panchayats. Similarly, 782 ward members have been elected unopposed. In Kandukuru Municipality, 76.07% voter turnout was recorded during the polling for its 40 wards. Out of the 47,473 voters, 36,114 people exercise their franchise in the elections. In Kavali division of SPSR Nellore district, the first phase elections were scheduled for 134 Gram Panchayats. Of these, 17 Panchayats were elected unanimous, while polling took place in 117 Panchayats. Among these 117 in eight mandals of the district, Sarpanches were elected unanimously in three Panchayats. Over 1.93 lakh out of total 2.39 lakh voters across 114 Panchayats with a turnout of 80.60%. Gudur and Kavali Municipalities have witnessed voter turnout of 56.40% and 68.92% respectively. Out of total 80,492 voters in Gudur, 45,400 polled, while 58,884 polled among the overall 85,433 voters in Kavali. Nellore Collector Himanshu Shukla said that the polling concluded peacefully. “The public showed great interest in the Sarpanch elections, with a higher participation rate compared to general elections,” he said.

While the notification has been issued for conducting elections in 139 panchayats, candidates were elected unanimously in 62 panchayats. Similarly, 782 ward members have been elected unopposed. In Kandukuru Municipality, 76.07% voter turnout was recorded during the polling for its 40 wards. Out of the 47,473 voters, 36,114 people exercise their franchise in the elections. In Kavali division of SPSR Nellore district, the first phase elections were scheduled for 134 Gram Panchayats. Of these, 17 Panchayats were elected unanimous, while polling took place in 117 Panchayats. Among these 117 in eight mandals of the district, Sarpanches were elected unanimously in three Panchayats. Over 1.93 lakh out of total 2.39 lakh voters across 114 Panchayats with a turnout of 80.60%. Gudur and Kavali Municipalities have witnessed voter turnout of 56.40% and 68.92% respectively. Out of total 80,492 voters in Gudur, 45,400 polled, while 58,884 polled among the overall 85,433 voters in Kavali. articles.title: Special Parliament sitting from November 30 likely to take up amended Delimitation Bill
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The Union Cabinet will meet on November 27 to clear the amended legislation

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The government has called for a special sitting of Parliament beginning Monday (November 30, 2026), where it is likely to table an amended Delimitation Bill. The two Houses will meet on separate dates, Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju announced on Thursday (November 26, 2026), which is the 104th day since the Monsoon Session adjourned indefinitely on August 13. Lok Sabha sittings will begin on November 30 and Rajya Sabha sittings on December 2. Both Houses will conclude on December 3. The last record of a session of Parliament continuing unprorogued was in 2008 , when it went on for 87 days. The Union Cabinet will meet on Friday (November 27, 2026) to clear the amended legislation. According to sources, three crucial changes are being introduced: a uniform 50% increase in the share of Lok Sabha seats; extending the freeze for 25 years on using the 1971 Census as the basis to determine the proportional strength of each State in the Lok Sabha; and third, using the 2011 Census for redrawing constituencies within each State. This replicates the formula brought by the Atal Bihari Vajpayee government in the Constitution (Eighty-fourth Amendment) Act, 2001. Since April, when the legislative package, including the Delimitation Bill, was defeated by a united Opposition in the Lok Sabha, the seat arithmetic in the House has changed. Twenty TMC MPs broke away and merged with the Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI), pledging support to the NDA. TMC challenged the split, which is currently under Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla’s review. The NCPI faction, on Tuesday (November 24, 2026), 84 days after TMC’s challenge, submitted replies to Mr. Birla, defending its decision and asserting that the move did not violate any parliamentary or constitutional provisions. Six Shiv Sena (UBT) MPs joined the Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena. Following the recent alliance between the BJP and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD), the lone SAD MP is also expected to vote with the government. It is also learnt that the YSR Congress, which has four MPs in the Lok Sabha, will extend support to the government on the Bill. In this evolving situation, all eyes are on the DMK, with 22 Lok Sabha MPs, and the NCP (Sharadchandra Pawar), with eight. Senior NCP (SP) leader Supriya Sule, on Thursday (November 26, 2026), told reporters that pre-emptively opposing the law before its draft was made public was not a good move. “First let the bill come. Let the entire bill come into our hands. When the bill is in our hands, then we will all talk about it, and if the bill is good for the nation, we might support it,” she said. She further added that there have been instances in the past when the Opposition has supported the government on matters of national importance and key reforms. The DMK, meanwhile, has not made any public remarks on the issue. Though, as per sources, the government has reached out to the party informally. A dominant section of the DMK is leaning towards the argument that not supporting the present constitutional amendment could mean further reduced representation for Tamil Nadu. “The freeze under Articles 81 and 82, which prevents the readjustment of seats allotted to each State in the Lok Sabha, has an inbuilt sunset clause. It provides that the freeze shall cease to operate once the relevant figures of the first Census undertaken after 2026 are published. If a constitutional amendment is not brought, the freeze will automatically lapse,” Swapnil Tripathi, who leads Charkha, Centre for Constitutional Law at the Vidhi Centre for Legal Policy, explained.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: If the post-2026 Census figures are taken into consideration, a top DMK leader argued, the State could end up losing as many as 12 seats in the Lok Sabha. “We are for a fair delimitation,” a top DMK leader said.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #9 of 30 (26 NOV)

📰 Special Parliament sitting from November 30 likely to take up amended Delimitation Bill

📌 Published: 26 Nov 2026, 09:24:22 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The Union Cabinet will meet on November 27 to clear the amended legislation

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The government has called for a special sitting of Parliament beginning Monday (November 30, 2026), where it is likely to table an amended Delimitation Bill. The two Houses will meet on separate dates, Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju announced on Thursday (November 26, 2026), which is the 104th day since the Monsoon Session adjourned indefinitely on August 13. Lok Sabha sittings will begin on November 30 and Rajya Sabha sittings on December 2. Both Houses will conclude on December 3. The last record of a session of Parliament continuing unprorogued was in 2008 , when it went on for 87 days. The Union Cabinet will meet on Friday (November 27, 2026) to clear the amended legislation. According to sources, three crucial changes are being introduced: a uniform 50% increase in the share of Lok Sabha seats; extending the freeze for 25 years on using the 1971 Census as the basis to determine the proportional strength of each State in the Lok Sabha; and third, using the 2011 Census for redrawing constituencies within each State. This replicates the formula brought by the Atal Bihari Vajpayee government in the Constitution (Eighty-fourth Amendment) Act, 2001. Since April, when the legislative package, including the Delimitation Bill, was defeated by a united Opposition in the Lok Sabha, the seat arithmetic in the House has changed. Twenty TMC MPs broke away and merged with the Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI), pledging support to the NDA. TMC challenged the split, which is currently under Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla’s review. The NCPI faction, on Tuesday (November 24, 2026), 84 days after TMC’s challenge, submitted replies to Mr. Birla, defending its decision and asserting that the move did not violate any parliamentary or constitutional provisions. Six Shiv Sena (UBT) MPs joined the Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena. Following the recent alliance between the BJP and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD), the lone SAD MP is also expected to vote with the government. It is also learnt that the YSR Congress, which has four MPs in the Lok Sabha, will extend support to the government on the Bill. In this evolving situation, all eyes are on the DMK, with 22 Lok Sabha MPs, and the NCP (Sharadchandra Pawar), with eight. Senior NCP (SP) leader Supriya Sule, on Thursday (November 26, 2026), told reporters that pre-emptively opposing the law before its draft was made public was not a good move. “First let the bill come. Let the entire bill come into our hands. When the bill is in our hands, then we will all talk about it, and if the bill is good for the nation, we might support it,” she said. She further added that there have been instances in the past when the Opposition has supported the government on matters of national importance and key reforms. The DMK, meanwhile, has not made any public remarks on the issue. Though, as per sources, the government has reached out to the party informally. A dominant section of the DMK is leaning towards the argument that not supporting the present constitutional amendment could mean further reduced representation for Tamil Nadu. “The freeze under Articles 81 and 82, which prevents the readjustment of seats allotted to each State in the Lok Sabha, has an inbuilt sunset clause. It provides that the freeze shall cease to operate once the relevant figures of the first Census undertaken after 2026 are published. If a constitutional amendment is not brought, the freeze will automatically lapse,” Swapnil Tripathi, who leads Charkha, Centre for Constitutional Law at the Vidhi Centre for Legal Policy, explained.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: If the post-2026 Census figures are taken into consideration, a top DMK leader argued, the State could end up losing as many as 12 seats in the Lok Sabha. “We are for a fair delimitation,” a top DMK leader said.

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Constitutional (Adjective)
संवैधानिक — देश के संविधान (Constitution) के दायरे और मौलिक अधिकारों के अनुरूप।
✓ Syn: Statutory, Legitimate, Lawful  |  ✖ Ant: Unconstitutional, Illegal, Arbitrary
Representation (Noun)
प्रतिनिधित्व — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Representation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Consideration (Noun)
सोच-विचार — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Consideration' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Delimitation (Adjective / Verb)
हदबंदी — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Delimitation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse  |  ✖ Ant: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "Special Parliament sitting from November 30 likely to take up amended Delimitation Bill", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. The Union Cabinet will meet on November 27 to clear the amended legislation.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Special Parliament sitting from November 30 like' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Special Parliament sitting from November 30 l' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Special Parliament sitting from November 30 l' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "The Union Cabinet will meet on November 27 to clear the amended legislation." (Hinglish Arth: संशोधित कानून को मंजूरी देने के लिए केंद्रीय मंत्रिमंडल 27 नवंबर को बैठक करेगा)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Special Parliament sitting from November 30 likely to take up amended Delimitation Bill"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. “We are for a fair delimitation,” a top DMK leader said.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "“We are for a fair delimitation,” a top DMK leader said." (Hinglish Arth: द्रमुक के एक शीर्ष नेता ने कहा, ''हम निष्पक्ष परिसीमन के पक्ष में हैं।'')

A dominant section of the DMK is leaning towards the argument that not supporting the present constitutional amendment could mean further reduced representation for Tamil Nadu. “The freeze under Articles 81 and 82, which prevents the readjustment of seats allotted to each State in the Lok Sabha, has an inbuilt sunset clause. It provides that the freeze shall cease to operate once the relevant figures of the first Census undertaken after 2026 are published. If a constitutional amendment is not brought, the freeze will automatically lapse,” Swapnil Tripathi, who leads Charkha, Centre for Constitutional Law at the Vidhi Centre for Legal Policy, explained.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: If the post-2026 Census figures are taken into consideration, a top DMK leader argued, the State could end up losing as many as 12 seats in the Lok Sabha. “We are for a fair delimitation,” a top DMK leader said.

articles.title: Infectious diseases from free-ranging domestic animals threaten Nilgiris wildlife
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Five of the 12 reported instances of wildlife deaths since 2005 likely due to infections contracted from feral animals were recorded in the Nilgiris district, shows report by Forest Department

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Frequent interactions between wildlife and free-ranging domestic animals raise concerns about disease transmission to wildlife in the Nilgiris. According to a report submitted by the Forest Department to the Madras High Court, five of the 12 reported instances of infections that caused wildlife deaths, likely due to interactions with feral animals, since 2005 were recorded in the Nilgiris district. Necropsy on wildlife carcasses had found canine distemper and rabies as the cause of deaths, which had been reported in the Nilgiris, Gudalur and Mudumalai Tiger Reserve (MTR) forest divisions. S. Muralidharan, who is appearing as the party-in-person before the High Court, has sought judicial intervention to address the threat to wildlife. He told The Hindu that there have been instances of diseases such as canine distemper and rabies spreading to wildlife from free-ranging domestic animals, particularly dogs. He pointed out that such diseases had threatened the survival of vulnerable wildlife populations, citing outbreaks of canine distemper among Asiatic lions in Gujarat as an example of the potential consequences. “This is a very serious concern, especially in areas where there is a very high interface between wildlife and human communities, which feed and maintain free-ranging dog populations, like in the Nilgiris” he said. Mr. Muralidharan called on the government to take measures to manage free-ranging dogs and cats in areas bordering tiger reserves and reserve forests across the State, including their removal from these areas to protect wildlife. “These animals also hunt small game such as birds and even deer and can be extremely aggressive,” he said. According to the report filed by the Forest Department, the deaths of the 12 animals reported due to transmission of disease from domestic animals include those of leopards (canine distemper), Nilgiri langur (rabies), Indian gaur (rabies), sloth bear (rabies and ehrlichiosis) and golden jackals (canine distemper and parvovirus infection). Conservationists said that the number of animals dying from diseases transmitted to wildlife from feral animals could be much higher as not all wildlife deaths are reported or are noticed if they occur inside reserve forests.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The deaths had been reported in Kodaikanal, Kalakkad Mundanthurai Tiger Reserve (KMTR), Sivaganga, Theni, Kanniyakumari and Tirunelveli, but the Nilgiris had the highest number of the reported deaths.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #27 of 30 (26 NOV)

📰 Infectious diseases from free-ranging domestic animals threaten Nilgiris wildlife

📌 Published: 26 Nov 2026, 09:24:03 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Five of the 12 reported instances of wildlife deaths since 2005 likely due to infections contracted from feral animals were recorded in the Nilgiris district, shows report by Forest Department

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Frequent interactions between wildlife and free-ranging domestic animals raise concerns about disease transmission to wildlife in the Nilgiris. According to a report submitted by the Forest Department to the Madras High Court, five of the 12 reported instances of infections that caused wildlife deaths, likely due to interactions with feral animals, since 2005 were recorded in the Nilgiris district. Necropsy on wildlife carcasses had found canine distemper and rabies as the cause of deaths, which had been reported in the Nilgiris, Gudalur and Mudumalai Tiger Reserve (MTR) forest divisions. S. Muralidharan, who is appearing as the party-in-person before the High Court, has sought judicial intervention to address the threat to wildlife. He told The Hindu that there have been instances of diseases such as canine distemper and rabies spreading to wildlife from free-ranging domestic animals, particularly dogs. He pointed out that such diseases had threatened the survival of vulnerable wildlife populations, citing outbreaks of canine distemper among Asiatic lions in Gujarat as an example of the potential consequences. “This is a very serious concern, especially in areas where there is a very high interface between wildlife and human communities, which feed and maintain free-ranging dog populations, like in the Nilgiris” he said. Mr. Muralidharan called on the government to take measures to manage free-ranging dogs and cats in areas bordering tiger reserves and reserve forests across the State, including their removal from these areas to protect wildlife. “These animals also hunt small game such as birds and even deer and can be extremely aggressive,” he said. According to the report filed by the Forest Department, the deaths of the 12 animals reported due to transmission of disease from domestic animals include those of leopards (canine distemper), Nilgiri langur (rabies), Indian gaur (rabies), sloth bear (rabies and ehrlichiosis) and golden jackals (canine distemper and parvovirus infection). Conservationists said that the number of animals dying from diseases transmitted to wildlife from feral animals could be much higher as not all wildlife deaths are reported or are noticed if they occur inside reserve forests.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The deaths had been reported in Kodaikanal, Kalakkad Mundanthurai Tiger Reserve (KMTR), Sivaganga, Theni, Kanniyakumari and Tirunelveli, but the Nilgiris had the highest number of the reported deaths.

✓ Syn: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse  |  ✖ Ant: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable
Department (Adjective)
विभाग — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Department' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Aggressive (Adjective)
आक्रामक — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Aggressive' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।

articles.title: HC reserves orders over e-auction of truck parking land at Kukatpally
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The Telangana High Court will pronounce orders today (Friday) in a couple of PIL petitions challenging the e-auction of 3.15 acres of government land at Kukatpally. The e-auction was slated to be held today.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The bench of Acting Chief Justice P. Sam Koshy and Justice Suddala Chlapathi Rao reserved the orders on Thursday after hearing contentions of the Additional Advocate General and the senior counsels for the petitioners B. Mayur Reddy and Gandra Mohan Rao in the two petitions. While one plea was filed by Madhavaram Kantha Rao, the other was by Madhavaram Sivaiah Gari Krishna Rao. Kantha Rao contested from Kukatpally as BJP nominee in 2018 Assembly polls while Krishna Rao of BRS party is MLA from Kukatpally. The Additional AG informed the bench that the State government acquired 33.22 acres of government land in 1981 to create parking lots for truckers. The original land owners were paid compensation by the government. The truck terminals were established to ensure heavy vehicles did not enter city during peak traffic hours. Out of the acquired land, the government decided to sell 3.15 acres of land and spend the revenue accrued for public purpose, he contended. As the arguments progressed, the Acting CJ sought to know from the petitioners’ counsels as to why the truck owners did not approach the court since they would be the aggrieved parties due to sale of land meant for parking lots.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The bench also wanted to know why the original land owners from whom the land acquired did not also seem to be having any grievance over the government move. The Additional AG argued that there was no public interest involved in the matter going by the fact that the two petitioners were in active politics. The senior counsels contended that the government’s decision was in violation of the Supreme Court verdicts. The apex court earlier held that lands acquired for public purpose cannot be sold except being used for the specific purpose, they said.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #11 of 30 (26 NOV)

📰 HC reserves orders over e-auction of truck parking land at Kukatpally

📌 Published: 26 Nov 2026, 09:23:44 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The Telangana High Court will pronounce orders today (Friday) in a couple of PIL petitions challenging the e-auction of 3.15 acres of government land at Kukatpally. The e-auction was slated to be held today.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The bench of Acting Chief Justice P. Sam Koshy and Justice Suddala Chlapathi Rao reserved the orders on Thursday after hearing contentions of the Additional Advocate General and the senior counsels for the petitioners B. Mayur Reddy and Gandra Mohan Rao in the two petitions. While one plea was filed by Madhavaram Kantha Rao, the other was by Madhavaram Sivaiah Gari Krishna Rao. Kantha Rao contested from Kukatpally as BJP nominee in 2018 Assembly polls while Krishna Rao of BRS party is MLA from Kukatpally. The Additional AG informed the bench that the State government acquired 33.22 acres of government land in 1981 to create parking lots for truckers. The original land owners were paid compensation by the government. The truck terminals were established to ensure heavy vehicles did not enter city during peak traffic hours. Out of the acquired land, the government decided to sell 3.15 acres of land and spend the revenue accrued for public purpose, he contended. As the arguments progressed, the Acting CJ sought to know from the petitioners’ counsels as to why the truck owners did not approach the court since they would be the aggrieved parties due to sale of land meant for parking lots.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The bench also wanted to know why the original land owners from whom the land acquired did not also seem to be having any grievance over the government move. The Additional AG argued that there was no public interest involved in the matter going by the fact that the two petitioners were in active politics. The senior counsels contended that the government’s decision was in violation of the Supreme Court verdicts. The apex court earlier held that lands acquired for public purpose cannot be sold except being used for the specific purpose, they said.

✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Grievance (Noun)
शिकायत — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Grievance' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।

Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "HC reserves orders over e-auction of truck parking land at Kukatpally", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. The Telangana High Court will pronounce orders today (Friday) in a couple of PIL petitions challenging the e-auction of 3.15 acres of government land...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'HC reserves orders over e-auction of truck parki' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'HC reserves orders over e-auction of truck pa' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'HC reserves orders over e-auction of truck pa' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "The Telangana High Court will pronounce orders today (Friday) in a couple of PIL petitions challenging the e-auction of 3.15 acres of government land..." (Hinglish Arth: तेलंगाना उच्च न्यायालय कुकटपल्ली में 3.15 एकड़ सरकारी भूमि की ई-नीलामी को चुनौती देने वाली कुछ जनहित याचिकाओं पर आज (शुक्रवार) आदेश सुनाएगा।)

D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. (Hinglish Arth: उन्होंने कहा, शीर्ष अदालत ने पहले कहा था कि सार्वजनिक उद्देश्य के लिए अधिग्रहीत भूमि को विशिष्ट उद्देश्य के लिए इस्तेमाल किए जाने के अलावा बेचा नहीं जा सकता है।)

articles.title: Enumerate Telangana tenant farmers in crop loss survey; support financially distressed farmers: Committee
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Telangana Tenant Farmers Recognition Struggle Committee has demanded the State government to include tenant farmers — who make up around 36% of farmers community — too to be enumerated in the ongoing Agriculture Department’s survey of farmers who suffered crop loss due to El Nino induced drought.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Highlighting the financial distress they are undergoing due to land lease payments and loss of crops due to the drought, they sought government to issue clear written guidelines to Agriculture Extension Officers (AEO) on enumerating tenant farmers and process to be followed for this. On a larger note, the Committee demanded recognition cards for the tenant farmers which would help them to get compensation in such distressing weather situations, avail welfare scheme and sell farm produce at Minimum Support Price (MSP). At a press conference held in Hyderabad on Thursday, the Committee members along with farmers, released findings of a field study on the ongoing crop loss survey, explained how they are strained financially and need for support from the government. The members said that distress among farmers would increase narrowing their options if the support is not provided. A team from Rythu Swarajya Vedika conducted field study on the government’s crop loss survey by speaking to 145 farmers in 10 villages of Adilabad and Vikarabad. Out of these, 89 were tenant farmers who were not recorded in the enumeration though all of them suffered more than 33% crop damage, as per a claim in a press release. Many farmers were unaware of the survey. Maize, soybean, green gram and black gram harvested before the survey were left out of the survey, despite farmers reporting crop losses averaging 65%. Besides, farmers were unaware on whether their names were included or excluded in the enumeration, the Committee stated. K. Yadamma, a woman farmer from Kodur mandal in Vikarabad, said that she has returned to her village after her brother cleared around ₹28 lakh loan - which was ₹6 lakh ten years ago when her husband was alive - and returned to farming this monsoon. “I took four acres on lease paying ₹15,000 per acre per annum and sowed kandi (red gram) and makka (corn). I invested some more money on ploughing, labour and fertilizers. The crop is yet to be harvested but it has suffered damage,” said Ms. Yadamma. Kanneganti Ravi of the Committee said that the issue pertains to 22 lakh tenant farmers and clear guidelines have to be given to the Agriculture department officers on how they have to be enumerated. He also demanded a published list of farmers included in the survey to be displayed at gram panchayat offices, so that those left out can flag and request their details to be added. The members have also demanded Cabinet sub-committee formed for the tenant farmers recognition to soon hold a meeting with representatives of farmer organisations, tenant farmers and the Committee.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: On the sidelines of the press conference, Kiran Vissa, a member of the committee, cited provisions under Telangana Land Licensed Cultivators Act, 2011, and said that providing recognition cards for tenant farmers will help them get bank loans rather than rely on money lenders who give loans at high interest, access government welfare schemes for farmers, sell farm produce at procurement centres for MSP and stand eligible for compensation during similar government surveys.

Out of these, 89 were tenant farmers who were not recorded in the enumeration though all of them suffered more than 33% crop damage, as per a claim in a press release. Many farmers were unaware of the survey. Maize, soybean, green gram and black gram harvested before the survey were left out of the survey, despite farmers reporting crop losses averaging 65%. Besides, farmers were unaware on whether their names were included or excluded in the enumeration, the Committee stated. K. Yadamma, a woman farmer from Kodur mandal in Vikarabad, said that she has returned to her village after her brother cleared around ₹28 lakh loan - which was ₹6 lakh ten years ago when her husband was alive - and returned to farming this monsoon. “I took four acres on lease paying ₹15,000 per acre per annum and sowed kandi (red gram) and makka (corn). I invested some more money on ploughing, labour and fertilizers. The crop is yet to be harvested but it has suffered damage,” said Ms. Yadamma. Kanneganti Ravi of the Committee said that the issue pertains to 22 lakh tenant farmers and clear guidelines have to be given to the Agriculture department officers on how they have to be enumerated. He also demanded a published list of farmers included in the survey to be displayed at gram panchayat offices, so that those left out can flag and request their details to be added. The members have also demanded Cabinet sub-committee formed for the tenant farmers recognition to soon hold a meeting with representatives of farmer organisations, tenant farmers and the Committee.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: On the sidelines of the press conference, Kiran Vissa, a member of the committee, cited provisions under Telangana Land Licensed Cultivators Act, 2011, and said that providing recognition cards for tenant farmers will help them get bank loans rather than rely on money lenders who give loans at high interest, access government welfare schemes for farmers, sell farm produce at procurement centres for MSP and stand eligible for compensation during similar government surveys.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #12 of 30 (26 NOV)

📰 Enumerate Telangana tenant farmers in crop loss survey; support financially distressed farmers: Committee

📌 Published: 26 Nov 2026, 09:22:47 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Telangana Tenant Farmers Recognition Struggle Committee has demanded the State government to include tenant farmers — who make up around 36% of farmers community — too to be enumerated in the ongoing Agriculture Department’s survey of farmers who suffered crop loss due to El Nino induced drought.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Highlighting the financial distress they are undergoing due to land lease payments and loss of crops due to the drought, they sought government to issue clear written guidelines to Agriculture Extension Officers (AEO) on enumerating tenant farmers and process to be followed for this. On a larger note, the Committee demanded recognition cards for the tenant farmers which would help them to get compensation in such distressing weather situations, avail welfare scheme and sell farm produce at Minimum Support Price (MSP). At a press conference held in Hyderabad on Thursday, the Committee members along with farmers, released findings of a field study on the ongoing crop loss survey, explained how they are strained financially and need for support from the government. The members said that distress among farmers would increase narrowing their options if the support is not provided. A team from Rythu Swarajya Vedika conducted field study on the government’s crop loss survey by speaking to 145 farmers in 10 villages of Adilabad and Vikarabad. Out of these, 89 were tenant farmers who were not recorded in the enumeration though all of them suffered more than 33% crop damage, as per a claim in a press release. Many farmers were unaware of the survey. Maize, soybean, green gram and black gram harvested before the survey were left out of the survey, despite farmers reporting crop losses averaging 65%. Besides, farmers were unaware on whether their names were included or excluded in the enumeration, the Committee stated. K. Yadamma, a woman farmer from Kodur mandal in Vikarabad, said that she has returned to her village after her brother cleared around ₹28 lakh loan - which was ₹6 lakh ten years ago when her husband was alive - and returned to farming this monsoon. “I took four acres on lease paying ₹15,000 per acre per annum and sowed kandi (red gram) and makka (corn). I invested some more money on ploughing, labour and fertilizers. The crop is yet to be harvested but it has suffered damage,” said Ms. Yadamma. Kanneganti Ravi of the Committee said that the issue pertains to 22 lakh tenant farmers and clear guidelines have to be given to the Agriculture department officers on how they have to be enumerated. He also demanded a published list of farmers included in the survey to be displayed at gram panchayat offices, so that those left out can flag and request their details to be added. The members have also demanded Cabinet sub-committee formed for the tenant farmers recognition to soon hold a meeting with representatives of farmer organisations, tenant farmers and the Committee.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: On the sidelines of the press conference, Kiran Vissa, a member of the committee, cited provisions under Telangana Land Licensed Cultivators Act, 2011, and said that providing recognition cards for tenant farmers will help them get bank loans rather than rely on money lenders who give loans at high interest, access government welfare schemes for farmers, sell farm produce at procurement centres for MSP and stand eligible for compensation during similar government surveys.

✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Enumeration (Noun)
गणना — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Enumeration' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Procurement (Adjective)
खरीद — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Procurement' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।

articles.title: China's Defence Ministry urges Japan to stop 'stirring up' South China Sea disputes
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The comments were in response to an ⁠announcement earlier this month that Japan will provide the Philippines with radars and drones to boost its coastal surveillance capabilities

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: China's Defence Ministry urged Japan on Thursday (November 26, 2026) to stop "stirring up ​trouble" over the South China Sea after a spokesperson was asked about ‌deepening cooperation between Tokyo and the Philippines, both formal ​U.S. military allies. Chinese and Philippine coastguard vessels ‌frequently clash near disputed shoals and reefs as part of long-simmering tensions over the vital trade waterway. Defence Ministry ‌spokesperson Chen Xi told a regular press briefing in Beijing ‌that ⁠Japan was not party to the disputes and had ⁠no right to comment on them. "We demand that Japan stop stirring up trouble over the South China Sea issue," Mr. Chen Xi said. Japan had used "so-called external threats" ​to deepen regional anxieties, form military ‌cliques and attempt to strengthen its military presence in the South China Sea, he added. The U.S. and its allies and partners have repeatedly expressed concern over the situation in the South ‌China Sea as China asserts its sovereignty through growing deployments ​of naval, coastguard and militia vessels. China claims nearly all of the South China Sea, overlapping maritime claims of ⁠the Philippines, Vietnam, Malaysia, Brunei and Taiwan. In 2016, a Hague-based tribunal said China's claims had no legal basis, a decision Beijing ‌has rejected. China's Military is also operating further out into the Pacific and is present on a daily basis around Taiwan, which Beijing views as its own territory. China carried out a large, unannounced military exercise across the western Pacific and around Taiwan in early November, in what officials in Taipei have previously described ‌as a campaign of "silent intimidation".

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Mr. Chen Xi, asked about those drills, said the Military's stepped-up training ​and combat readiness, and its continuous improvement of practical capabilities to defend China's sovereignty and territorial integrity, are "entirely legitimate and ⁠reasonable".

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #24 of 30 (26 NOV)

📰 China's Defence Ministry urges Japan to stop 'stirring up' South China Sea disputes

📌 Published: 26 Nov 2026, 10:26:27 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The comments were in response to an ⁠announcement earlier this month that Japan will provide the Philippines with radars and drones to boost its coastal surveillance capabilities

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: China's Defence Ministry urged Japan on Thursday (November 26, 2026) to stop "stirring up ​trouble" over the South China Sea after a spokesperson was asked about ‌deepening cooperation between Tokyo and the Philippines, both formal ​U.S. military allies. Chinese and Philippine coastguard vessels ‌frequently clash near disputed shoals and reefs as part of long-simmering tensions over the vital trade waterway. Defence Ministry ‌spokesperson Chen Xi told a regular press briefing in Beijing ‌that ⁠Japan was not party to the disputes and had ⁠no right to comment on them. "We demand that Japan stop stirring up trouble over the South China Sea issue," Mr. Chen Xi said. Japan had used "so-called external threats" ​to deepen regional anxieties, form military ‌cliques and attempt to strengthen its military presence in the South China Sea, he added. The U.S. and its allies and partners have repeatedly expressed concern over the situation in the South ‌China Sea as China asserts its sovereignty through growing deployments ​of naval, coastguard and militia vessels. China claims nearly all of the South China Sea, overlapping maritime claims of ⁠the Philippines, Vietnam, Malaysia, Brunei and Taiwan. In 2016, a Hague-based tribunal said China's claims had no legal basis, a decision Beijing ‌has rejected. China's Military is also operating further out into the Pacific and is present on a daily basis around Taiwan, which Beijing views as its own territory. China carried out a large, unannounced military exercise across the western Pacific and around Taiwan in early November, in what officials in Taipei have previously described ‌as a campaign of "silent intimidation".

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Mr. Chen Xi, asked about those drills, said the Military's stepped-up training ​and combat readiness, and its continuous improvement of practical capabilities to defend China's sovereignty and territorial integrity, are "entirely legitimate and ⁠reasonable".

Intimidation (Adjective / Verb)
डराना — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Intimidation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।

articles.title: Delhi tops list of most polluted NCR cities for PM2.5, PM10 despite no severe AQI days
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The city's air quality remained in the poor or very poor categories for 30 days

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Delhi topped the list of the 10 most polluted cities in the National Capital Region for both PM2.5 and PM10 during the October 1-November 25 period this year, moving up from third and fourth positions in the corresponding period last year. According to an analysis of India Air Quality Portal by EnviroCatalysts, Delhi recorded an average PM2.5 concentration of 113 micrograms per cubic metre during the period, followed by Gurugram at 109, Noida at 105, Ghaziabad at 103, Meerut at 96, Baghpat and Greater Noida at 95, Panipat at 90, Bulandshahr at 82, and Faridabad at 69. For PM10, Delhi again topped the list with an average concentration of 221 micrograms per cubic metre. Gurugram recorded 207, followed by Bulandshahr at 201, Noida at 200, Ghaziabad at 197, Baghpat at 193, Greater Noida at 192, Meerut at 178, and Panipat and Faridabad at 173 each. In the corresponding period last year, Delhi recorded an average PM2.5 concentration of 158 micrograms per cubic metre, ranking third behind Ghaziabad and Noida. Its average PM10 concentration stood at 287 micrograms per cubic metre, placing it fourth behind Ghaziabad, Noida and Greater Noida. Ghaziabad topped both lists in 2025. A comparison of the same period over the last six years, from 2021 to 2026, shows that Delhi topped the PM2.5 list three times, in 2022, 2024 and 2026, while it recorded the highest average PM10 concentration twice, in 2024 and 2026. Despite topping both pollution charts, Delhi did not record a single day in the severe air quality category during the 56 days. It recorded three days in the satisfactory category, 23 in moderate, 18 in poor and 12 in very poor. "Air across the NCR has been clearly better this season, helped by good October rain and less pollution reaching Delhi from spread-out and fewer farm fires. The next step is to cut year-round sources such as vehicles, dust and waste burning across the whole region, so this improvement becomes the new normal," Sunil Dahiya, founder and lead analyst at EnviroCatalyst, told PTI. The city's air quality remained in the poor or very poor categories for 30 days.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: In 2025, Delhi recorded four satisfactory days, nine moderate days, 13 poor days, 27 very poor days and three severe days. The previous year, air quality remained in the moderate category for 13 days, poor for 10 days, very poor for 25 days and severe for eight days.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #25 of 30 (26 NOV)

📰 Delhi tops list of most polluted NCR cities for PM2.5, PM10 despite no severe AQI days

📌 Published: 26 Nov 2026, 10:07:48 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The city's air quality remained in the poor or very poor categories for 30 days

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Delhi topped the list of the 10 most polluted cities in the National Capital Region for both PM2.5 and PM10 during the October 1-November 25 period this year, moving up from third and fourth positions in the corresponding period last year. According to an analysis of India Air Quality Portal by EnviroCatalysts, Delhi recorded an average PM2.5 concentration of 113 micrograms per cubic metre during the period, followed by Gurugram at 109, Noida at 105, Ghaziabad at 103, Meerut at 96, Baghpat and Greater Noida at 95, Panipat at 90, Bulandshahr at 82, and Faridabad at 69. For PM10, Delhi again topped the list with an average concentration of 221 micrograms per cubic metre. Gurugram recorded 207, followed by Bulandshahr at 201, Noida at 200, Ghaziabad at 197, Baghpat at 193, Greater Noida at 192, Meerut at 178, and Panipat and Faridabad at 173 each. In the corresponding period last year, Delhi recorded an average PM2.5 concentration of 158 micrograms per cubic metre, ranking third behind Ghaziabad and Noida. Its average PM10 concentration stood at 287 micrograms per cubic metre, placing it fourth behind Ghaziabad, Noida and Greater Noida. Ghaziabad topped both lists in 2025. articles.title: Mindfulness linked to healthier social media use, better mental health: study
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The findings showed that higher levels of mindfulness were associated with lower levels of depression, anxiety, stress, loneliness and fear of missing out (FoMO)

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: People with higher levels of mindfulness are more likely to have healthier social media habits and better mental health outcomes, according to a review of 43 studies involving more than 28,000 participants. Mindfulness involves observing one’s thoughts and feelings without judgement. Researchers led by University College London analysed the studies and found that people who reported being more mindful in their daily lives were more likely to report healthier patterns of social media use. The findings, published in the journal PLOS One , also showed that higher levels of mindfulness were associated with lower levels of depression, anxiety, stress, loneliness and fear of missing out (FoMO). Previous studies have shown that cultivating mindfulness through practices such as meditation or mindfulness-based therapy can help reduce symptoms of stress, anxiety and depression. The review contributes to the debate over whether social media use poses a risk to mental health or aggravates existing mental health problems, the researchers said. Lead author Dr Marc S Tibber from University College London’s Division of Psychology and Language Sciences said the findings supported a shift away from simplistic questions about whether social media was inherently good or bad. “Our findings support a move away from reductive questions about whether social media is inherently good or bad, towards an exploration of how complex interactions between individuals, technologies, and the broader social contexts in which they are embedded shape both the potential benefits and harms of social media for mental health,” Tibber said. The review suggested that mindfulness may play a protective role, he said, adding that it could be a potential target for interventions aimed at promoting healthier digital engagement, although further research was needed.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The studies included participants aged 10 to 92, with university students accounting for the largest group at 46.5 %.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #26 of 30 (26 NOV)

📰 Mindfulness linked to healthier social media use, better mental health: study

📌 Published: 26 Nov 2026, 10:05:38 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The findings showed that higher levels of mindfulness were associated with lower levels of depression, anxiety, stress, loneliness and fear of missing out (FoMO)

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: People with higher levels of mindfulness are more likely to have healthier social media habits and better mental health outcomes, according to a review of 43 studies involving more than 28,000 participants. Mindfulness involves observing one’s thoughts and feelings without judgement. Researchers led by University College London analysed the studies and found that people who reported being more mindful in their daily lives were more likely to report healthier patterns of social media use. The findings, published in the journal PLOS One , also showed that higher levels of mindfulness were associated with lower levels of depression, anxiety, stress, loneliness and fear of missing out (FoMO). Previous studies have shown that cultivating mindfulness through practices such as meditation or mindfulness-based therapy can help reduce symptoms of stress, anxiety and depression. The review contributes to the debate over whether social media use poses a risk to mental health or aggravates existing mental health problems, the researchers said. Lead author Dr Marc S Tibber from University College London’s Division of Psychology and Language Sciences said the findings supported a shift away from simplistic questions about whether social media was inherently good or bad. “Our findings support a move away from reductive questions about whether social media is inherently good or bad, towards an exploration of how complex interactions between individuals, technologies, and the broader social contexts in which they are embedded shape both the potential benefits and harms of social media for mental health,” Tibber said. The review suggested that mindfulness may play a protective role, he said, adding that it could be a potential target for interventions aimed at promoting healthier digital engagement, although further research was needed.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The studies included participants aged 10 to 92, with university students accounting for the largest group at 46.5 %.

articles.title: Training vs inference: What’s the distinction at the heart of the Sarvam AI-China models controversy? | Explained
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Can India build an indigenous AI ecosystem while hosting models developed in China? What is Sarvam’s Token Factory? What does it mean for India’s AI ambitions?

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The story so far: Sarvam AI has so far been known for developing its own Artificial Intelligence (AI) models with support from the government’s IndiaAI Mission . On November 16, the Bengaluru-based startup added another part to its business with the launch of Token Factory, a commercial service that gives businesses access to its own models and those developed by other companies, including Chinese firms. The launch prompted a debate over whether offering Chinese-developed models through a commercial platform aligns with India’s ambition to build indigenous AI capabilities, particularly when a company has received government support. Hemant Mohapatra, partner at Lightspeed India and an investor in Sarvam, defended the commercial rationale. In a November 18 post on X, he said global AI companies were generating substantial revenue by hosting models, including Chinese ones, on infrastructure in India and serving customers worldwide. He attributed the opportunity to a global shortage of GPUs, which has made computing capacity in India attractive to companies seeking to run their models. On November 22, Sarvam co-founder Pratyush Kumar issued a clarification on X, addressing questions about the company’s government support, its decision to host foreign-developed models and its commitment to developing its own models. He said Sarvam had used subsidised computing access under the IndiaAI Mission to train its 105B model, while maintaining that its inference business did not conflict with its objective of developing its own models. The government has also defended Sarvam’s commercial strategy. IT Secretary S Krishnan told reporters that the Centre did not see any misuse of IndiaAI Mission support in the company’s decision to offer foreign-developed models through Token Factory. “Based on what Sarvam has told us, based on the experience that people have, we do not see any misuse of the support, which the IndiaAI Mission has provided to Sarvam in the service that they are now offering,” he said. Krishnan said there was no contradiction between developing indigenous models and offering foreign-developed ones commercially, adding that AI companies also needed a revenue model. Token Factory is an inference platform that allows developers and businesses to access several AI models through a single Application Programming Interface (API). An API allows one software application to communicate with another. Instead of setting up and managing the infrastructure needed to run a model, a business can connect its software to Sarvam’s API and send requests to the model it wants to use. The platform offers Sarvam’s 105-billion-parameter model, alongside open-weight models such as GLM 5.3 and GLM 5.3 Flash from China’s Z.ai, DeepSeek V4 models from DeepSeek, Kimi models from Moonshot AI, and Google’s Gemma 4 31B. Open-weight models are those whose trained parameters, or weights, are made available for others to download and run. Businesses can use them without having to develop the models from scratch.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Sarvam says Token Factory runs the models on GPU clusters located in India. Customers pay according to the number of tokens processed.
