Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Tata Institute of Fundamental Research-Hyderabad (TIFRH) and Hyderabad-based Virupaksha Organics Limited on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to collaborate on research, technology development and technical evaluation in the field of advanced materials. The agreement aims to combine TIFRH’s expertise in fundamental scientific research with Virupaksha Organics’ industrial capabilities in process development and manufacturing. The collaboration is expected to help bridge the gap between laboratory research and industrial applications, paving the way for commercialisation of promising technologies. Under the MoU, the two organisations will jointly explore opportunities in research and development, process optimisation, product development, material characterisation, testing and technical evaluation. The initial focus areas include conducting and semiconducting materials for optoelectronic applications, development of two-dimensional (2D) materials, and quantum materials and optics. (From Left to right) Harish Krishnamoorthy, Pabitra K Nayak, T N Narayanan, Srinidhi Iyengar, M Krishnamurthy, Chandra Mouliswar Reddy, Smarajit Karmakar and Vijay K P | Photo Credit: BY ARRANGEMENT
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The agreement serves as a non-exclusive umbrella framework, with specific projects to be taken up through separate agreements that will define the scope of work, timelines and deliverables. The partnership will also facilitate knowledge exchange and capacity building between researchers and industry professionals, said a press release.

articles.title: 78 MoUs signed at second edition of VETTRI Tamil Nadu Investment and Conversion Conclave
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The MoUs involve investments worth ₹58,214 crore, with the potential to generate 65,786 jobs across various sectors.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Tamil Nadu government on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) signed 78 memoranda of understanding (MoUs) involving investments worth ₹58,214 crore, with the potential to generate 65,786 jobs across various sectors and districts of the State. The MoUs were exchanged in the presence of Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay, Industries Minister S. Keerthana and Deepak Jacob, Managing Director and CEO of Guidance at the second edition of the VETTRI Tamil Nadu Investment and Conversion Conclave held in Chennai. The Chief Minister laid the foundation stone for 15 projects involving investments worth ₹7,925 crore, which are expected to generate 19,965 jobs. He also inaugurated six projects involving investments to the tune of ₹1,430 crore, creating employment opportunities for 1,710 people. Mr. Vijay handed over appointment letters to 18 candidates selected for various positions for companies including UPS, Autoliv, Stylcove, Mahindra & Mahindra, and Omron. With this, the total number of MoUs signed by the TVK government has risen to 190, involving investments worth over ₹1.73 lakh crore within 200 days of assuming office. The conversion rate is 74.1% (the MoUs signed on August 13, 2026). Industries Minister S. Keerthana said: “There has been considerable discussion about which State is attracting the most investment. Tamil Nadu welcomes competition. But for us, investment must translate into productive employment, better incomes and opportunities for our people. We are not chasing jobless growth.” She went on to add, “Our real competition is not another State. It is the world’s leading manufacturing economies.” The Minister also said that two out of every five women working in India’s factories are employed in Tamil Nadu. “That is why we launched the ‘Vetri Magalir Thozhilmunaivor Membattu Thittam’, which offers loans of up to ₹5 crore to women entrepreneurs. We have received thousands of applications, and 19 women entrepreneurs have already been sanctioned loans totalling ₹13.26 crore,” she said. On Global Capability Centres (GCCs), the Minister said the government would work with the Greater Chennai Corporation to strengthen social infrastructure. S. Vijayakumar, Additional Chief Secretary to the Government for the Industries, Investment Promotion and Commerce Department said that Tamil Nadu Single Window Portal 3.0 is under development and is expected to be ready by January 2027. The New Industrial Policy is also being prepared and is expected to be ready by January 2027, he added. Mr. Vijayakumar also said that the Tamil Nadu Investment Promotion Commission has approved that industries may self execute their HT/EHT power connections by procuring the equipment, accessories and installations on their own. The Energy Department will share the specifications for self execution. Our Budget Estimates for the incentives to the industries for this current year is ₹2000 crore. We have distributed this amount in 200 days and have requested the government of Tamil Nadu for another ₹1600 crore,” he pointed out. Royal Enfield is set to establish an electric motorcycle manufacturing facility with an investment of ₹1,000 crore, creating 500 jobs. The company also unveiled its C6 model at the conclave.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Sweden-based PMC Hydraulics is shifting a part of its manufacturing operations from Bengaluru to Tamil Nadu and will establish its first manufacturing facility in Krishnagiri, with an investment to the tune of ₹300 crore. The project is expected to generate 300 jobs.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #11 of 30 (25 NOV)

📰 78 MoUs signed at second edition of VETTRI Tamil Nadu Investment and Conversion Conclave

📌 Published: 25 Nov 2026, 05:16:49 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The MoUs involve investments worth ₹58,214 crore, with the potential to generate 65,786 jobs across various sectors.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Tamil Nadu government on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) signed 78 memoranda of understanding (MoUs) involving investments worth ₹58,214 crore, with the potential to generate 65,786 jobs across various sectors and districts of the State. The MoUs were exchanged in the presence of Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay, Industries Minister S. Keerthana and Deepak Jacob, Managing Director and CEO of Guidance at the second edition of the VETTRI Tamil Nadu Investment and Conversion Conclave held in Chennai. The Chief Minister laid the foundation stone for 15 projects involving investments worth ₹7,925 crore, which are expected to generate 19,965 jobs. He also inaugurated six projects involving investments to the tune of ₹1,430 crore, creating employment opportunities for 1,710 people. Mr. Vijay handed over appointment letters to 18 candidates selected for various positions for companies including UPS, Autoliv, Stylcove, Mahindra & Mahindra, and Omron. With this, the total number of MoUs signed by the TVK government has risen to 190, involving investments worth over ₹1.73 lakh crore within 200 days of assuming office. The conversion rate is 74.1% (the MoUs signed on August 13, 2026). Industries Minister S. Keerthana said: “There has been considerable discussion about which State is attracting the most investment. Tamil Nadu welcomes competition. But for us, investment must translate into productive employment, better incomes and opportunities for our people. We are not chasing jobless growth.” She went on to add, “Our real competition is not another State. It is the world’s leading manufacturing economies.” The Minister also said that two out of every five women working in India’s factories are employed in Tamil Nadu. “That is why we launched the ‘Vetri Magalir Thozhilmunaivor Membattu Thittam’, which offers loans of up to ₹5 crore to women entrepreneurs. We have received thousands of applications, and 19 women entrepreneurs have already been sanctioned loans totalling ₹13.26 crore,” she said. On Global Capability Centres (GCCs), the Minister said the government would work with the Greater Chennai Corporation to strengthen social infrastructure. S. Vijayakumar, Additional Chief Secretary to the Government for the Industries, Investment Promotion and Commerce Department said that Tamil Nadu Single Window Portal 3.0 is under development and is expected to be ready by January 2027. The New Industrial Policy is also being prepared and is expected to be ready by January 2027, he added. Mr. Vijayakumar also said that the Tamil Nadu Investment Promotion Commission has approved that industries may self execute their HT/EHT power connections by procuring the equipment, accessories and installations on their own. The Energy Department will share the specifications for self execution. Our Budget Estimates for the incentives to the industries for this current year is ₹2000 crore. We have distributed this amount in 200 days and have requested the government of Tamil Nadu for another ₹1600 crore,” he pointed out. Royal Enfield is set to establish an electric motorcycle manufacturing facility with an investment of ₹1,000 crore, creating 500 jobs. The company also unveiled its C6 model at the conclave.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Sweden-based PMC Hydraulics is shifting a part of its manufacturing operations from Bengaluru to Tamil Nadu and will establish its first manufacturing facility in Krishnagiri, with an investment to the tune of ₹300 crore. The project is expected to generate 300 jobs.

Appointment (Adjective)
नियुक्ति — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Appointment' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।

प्रतियोगिता — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Competition' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Corporation (Noun)
निगम — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Corporation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Development (Adjective)
विकास — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Development' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "78 MoUs signed at second edition of VETTRI Tamil Nadu Investment and Conversion Conclave", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. The MoUs involve investments worth ₹58,214 crore, with the potential to generate 65,786 jobs across various sectors.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of '78 MoUs signed at second edition of VETTRI Tamil' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to '78 MoUs signed at second edition of VETTRI Ta' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that '78 MoUs signed at second edition of VETTRI Ta' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "The MoUs involve investments worth ₹58,214 crore, with the potential to generate 65,786 jobs across various sectors." (Hinglish Arth: एमओयू में ₹58,214 करोड़ का निवेश शामिल है, जिसमें विभिन्न क्षेत्रों में 65,786 नौकरियां पैदा करने की क्षमता है।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "78 MoUs signed at second edition of VETTRI Tamil Nadu Investment and Conversion Conclave"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. The project is expected to generate 300 jobs.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "The project is expected to generate 300 jobs." (Hinglish Arth: इस परियोजना से 300 नौकरियाँ पैदा होने की उम्मीद है।)

articles.title: SC defers Umar Khalid, Sharjeel Imam’s interim bail pleas pending larger Bench ruling on UAPA bail curbs

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The two activists have challenged a September 30 ruling of the Delhi High Court rejecting their fresh bail pleas, contending that the case remains at the stage of framing of charges and that the trial is yet to commence

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Supreme Court on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) declined to entertain pleas for interim bail filed by former JNU scholar Umar Khalid and activist Sharjeel Imam , accused in the larger conspiracy case linked to the 2020 Delhi riots. The court indicated that any consideration of interim relief would have to await an authoritative ruling by a larger Bench of three judges on whether prolonged incarceration and delay in trial can override the stringent bail curbs under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 (UAPA). At the outset of the hearing, senior advocates Kapil Sibal and Siddharth Dave, appearing for Mr. Khalid and Mr. Imam, respectively, pressed for interim bail pending adjudication of the larger Bench reference, pointing out that both had been in custody for over six years. A Bench comprising Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana, however, declined the request. “We will not hear it today… We will have to constitute a larger Bench in light of the observations made in the order dated May 22, 2026 passed in Tasleem Ahmed v. State of NCT of Delhi,” the Bench said. In its January 5 verdict, a Division Bench headed by Justice Aravind Kumar had granted bail to five other accused in the case but denied relief to Mr. Khalid and Mr. Imam on the ground that the roles attributed to them stood on a “qualitatively different footing”. It, however, permitted them to renew their bail pleas after a year or upon completion of the examination of protected witnesses, whichever was earlier. Mr. Sibal drew the court’s attention to the subsequent May 22 order of the Justice Kumar-headed Bench, which had granted interim bail to Tasleem Ahmed and Abdul Khalid Saifi, two other accused in the conspiracy case, while referring the question of bail under the UAPA to a larger Bench. He urged the court to extend similar interim relief to the two activists. The reference, the Division Bench had said, was necessary to ensure “parity, consistency and institutional fidelity” in the application of binding precedents by coordinate Benches. “Only the main matter on the legal issue is under reference. Let the issue of interim come up for hearing,” Mr. Sibal submitted, requesting an early hearing. The CJI, however, pointed to conflicting judicial interpretations of the court’s 2021 ruling in Union of India v. K.A. Najeeb. In Najeeb, the court had held that the stringent bail embargo under Section 43D(5) of the UAPA could “melt down” where prolonged incarceration and delay in trial infringed an accused’s fundamental rights. The provision precludes the grant of bail where there are reasonable grounds to believe that the accusations against a person are prima facie true.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “In the light of the conflict of observations, I have to apply my mind… One Bench says Najeeb means this, another Bench says it does not mean… We are aware of everything. We have done our homework and have gone through the January 5 judgment,” the CJI remarked.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #12 of 30 (25 NOV)

📰 SC defers Umar Khalid, Sharjeel Imam’s interim bail pleas pending larger Bench ruling on UAPA bail curbs

📌 Published: 25 Nov 2026, 05:11:59 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The two activists have challenged a September 30 ruling of the Delhi High Court rejecting their fresh bail pleas, contending that the case remains at the stage of framing of charges and that the trial is yet to commence

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Supreme Court on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) declined to entertain pleas for interim bail filed by former JNU scholar Umar Khalid and activist Sharjeel Imam , accused in the larger conspiracy case linked to the 2020 Delhi riots. The court indicated that any consideration of interim relief would have to await an authoritative ruling by a larger Bench of three judges on whether prolonged incarceration and delay in trial can override the stringent bail curbs under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 (UAPA). At the outset of the hearing, senior advocates Kapil Sibal and Siddharth Dave, appearing for Mr. Khalid and Mr. Imam, respectively, pressed for interim bail pending adjudication of the larger Bench reference, pointing out that both had been in custody for over six years. A Bench comprising Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana, however, declined the request. “We will not hear it today… We will have to constitute a larger Bench in light of the observations made in the order dated May 22, 2026 passed in Tasleem Ahmed v. State of NCT of Delhi,” the Bench said. In its January 5 verdict, a Division Bench headed by Justice Aravind Kumar had granted bail to five other accused in the case but denied relief to Mr. Khalid and Mr. Imam on the ground that the roles attributed to them stood on a “qualitatively different footing”. It, however, permitted them to renew their bail pleas after a year or upon completion of the examination of protected witnesses, whichever was earlier. Mr. Sibal drew the court’s attention to the subsequent May 22 order of the Justice Kumar-headed Bench, which had granted interim bail to Tasleem Ahmed and Abdul Khalid Saifi, two other accused in the conspiracy case, while referring the question of bail under the UAPA to a larger Bench. He urged the court to extend similar interim relief to the two activists. The reference, the Division Bench had said, was necessary to ensure “parity, consistency and institutional fidelity” in the application of binding precedents by coordinate Benches. “Only the main matter on the legal issue is under reference. Let the issue of interim come up for hearing,” Mr. Sibal submitted, requesting an early hearing. The CJI, however, pointed to conflicting judicial interpretations of the court’s 2021 ruling in Union of India v. K.A. Najeeb. In Najeeb, the court had held that the stringent bail embargo under Section 43D(5) of the UAPA could “melt down” where prolonged incarceration and delay in trial infringed an accused’s fundamental rights. The provision precludes the grant of bail where there are reasonable grounds to believe that the accusations against a person are prima facie true.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “In the light of the conflict of observations, I have to apply my mind… One Bench says Najeeb means this, another Bench says it does not mean… We are aware of everything. We have done our homework and have gone through the January 5 judgment,” the CJI remarked.

Institutional (Adjective)
संस्थागत — देश की संवैधानिक या सरकारी संस्थाओं के नियमों और ढांचे से जुड़ा हुआ।
✓ Syn: Systemic, Organizational, Constitutional  |  ✖ Ant: Individual, Informal, Unorganized
Constitutional (Adjective)
संवैधानिक — देश के संविधान (Constitution) के दायरे और मौलिक अधिकारों के अनुरूप।
✓ Syn: Statutory, Legitimate, Lawful  |  ✖ Ant: Unconstitutional, Illegal, Arbitrary
Consideration (Noun)
सोच-विचार — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Consideration' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Authoritative (Adjective)
आधिकारिक — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Authoritative' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile

articles.title: UK police charge two men over a break-in at Prince William and Princess Catherine’s country home
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Anmer Hall, a 10-bedroom house on the Sandringham estate, was a wedding present to the couple from the late Queen Elizabeth II

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Two men have been charged with burglary at the country home of Prince William and Princess Catherine, police said on Wednesday (November 25, 2026). The Norfolk Police force says Mirgen Doku, 34, and Arilen Ndoci, 32, were charged with entering a dwelling with intent to steal and trespassing on a protected site. They are due in court later on Wednesday. Police officers were called on Monday evening to reported “suspicious activity” at an address on the royal family's rural Sandringham estate in eastern England. After a search involving police dogs, drones and a helicopter, two men were arrested on suspicion of burglary and trespassing. William and Kate’s Kensington Palace office declined to comment on security matters. Anmer Hall, a 10-bedroom house on the Sandringham estate, was a wedding present to the couple from the late Queen Elizabeth II. William and Kate use the secluded red brick Georgian mansion about 110 miles (171 kilometres) north of London as a country residence on weekends. The couple and their three children spend most of their time at Forest Lodge in Windsor, west of London, which they have described as their “forever home.” Intruders have breached royal properties several times over the years. In October 2024, burglars broke into the Windsor Castle estate west of London and stole a pickup truck and a quad bike from a farm building. Charles and Queen Camilla weren’t at Windsor Castle at the time, but it was reported that William and Kate were in their nearby house. Three years earlier, a man armed with a crossbow was detained on the castle grounds. Jaswant Singh Chail was later sentenced to nine years in prison after admitting he had been encouraged by a chatbot to kill Elizabeth.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: In 1982, intruder Michael Fagan managed to sneak into the queen’s private chambers while she was in bed. The queen spent 10 minutes chatting with the burglar before raising the alarm when he asked for a cigarette.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #22 of 30 (25 NOV)

📰 UK police charge two men over a break-in at Prince William and Princess Catherine’s country home

📌 Published: 25 Nov 2026, 06:47:35 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Anmer Hall, a 10-bedroom house on the Sandringham estate, was a wedding present to the couple from the late Queen Elizabeth II

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Two men have been charged with burglary at the country home of Prince William and Princess Catherine, police said on Wednesday (November 25, 2026). The Norfolk Police force says Mirgen Doku, 34, and Arilen Ndoci, 32, were charged with entering a dwelling with intent to steal and trespassing on a protected site. They are due in court later on Wednesday. Police officers were called on Monday evening to reported “suspicious activity” at an address on the royal family's rural Sandringham estate in eastern England. After a search involving police dogs, drones and a helicopter, two men were arrested on suspicion of burglary and trespassing. William and Kate’s Kensington Palace office declined to comment on security matters. Anmer Hall, a 10-bedroom house on the Sandringham estate, was a wedding present to the couple from the late Queen Elizabeth II. William and Kate use the secluded red brick Georgian mansion about 110 miles (171 kilometres) north of London as a country residence on weekends. The couple and their three children spend most of their time at Forest Lodge in Windsor, west of London, which they have described as their “forever home.” Intruders have breached royal properties several times over the years. In October 2024, burglars broke into the Windsor Castle estate west of London and stole a pickup truck and a quad bike from a farm building. Charles and Queen Camilla weren’t at Windsor Castle at the time, but it was reported that William and Kate were in their nearby house. Three years earlier, a man armed with a crossbow was detained on the castle grounds. Jaswant Singh Chail was later sentenced to nine years in prison after admitting he had been encouraged by a chatbot to kill Elizabeth.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: In 1982, intruder Michael Fagan managed to sneak into the queen’s private chambers while she was in bed. The queen spent 10 minutes chatting with the burglar before raising the alarm when he asked for a cigarette.

articles.title: Meet the little stint: The tiny Siberian traveller visiting India’s wetlands
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The Little Stint travels thousands of kilometres between its Arctic breeding grounds and Indian wetlands. But as shrinking mudflats and changing landscapes threaten its feeding and resting habitats, this tiny shorebird tells an important story about conserving wetlands

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The little stint, a 25-gram shorebird, comes in lakhs from the Arctic to the shores of India, particularly to Point Calimere. “It’s an unforgettable sight,” says S Sivakumar, who has been involved in monitoring shorebirds in the Gulf of Mannar for over a decade. The birds remain through the winter months and depart between March and April, sometimes later in May. “In the 1980s, the little stint could be seen in several lakhs at any point of time. Even now, the numbers are still over a lakh as the Point Calimere Wetland Complex covers over 300 kilometres across coastal Tamil Nadu ,” says Sivakumar, assistant director at the Bombay Natural History Society’s Bird Migration Study Centre at Point Calimere, adding that such long-term observations help scientists understand how bird populations and their habitats are changing. The birds remain through the winter months and depart between March and April, sometimes later in May | Photo Credit: S Sivakumar The tiny bird’s annual migration journey, a feat of endurance, involves multiple stopovers across different landscapes, each of which must provide sufficient food and safe resting grounds. As shrinking mudflats and changing landscapes threaten its feeding and resting habitats, this tiny shorebird tells an important story about conserving wetlands. Ashvin Viswanathan, scientist at Bird Count India , places the little stints as the most visible representatives of a special group of shorebirds that breed in the Arctic. “ This group is declining rapidly due to climate change and loss of habitat. Little stints too are declining in India according to SoIB,” he says, referring to the State of India’s Birds assessment. Their widespread presence, he adds, indicates the health of wetland ecosystems in India as well as conditions in the Arctic. The fact that the little stint is still a fairly common bird does not mean that it is beyond risk. It’s numbers and distribution can help draw attention to changes taking place across the habitats it depends on. The numbers are still over a lakh at Point Calimere wetlands | Photo Credit: S Sivakumar The bird’s preparation for migration is as fascinating as the journey itself. “Before setting off, they enter a phase of intense feeding called hyperphagia. They feed voraciously to build up fat reserves that act as fuel during its journey. This can add 50 to 75 percent to the bird’s body weight. There are also physiological changes, some organs shrink in size as the bird prepares for the demands of sustained flight,” explains Sivakumar adding that India is an important destination along the Central Asian Flyway that connects the bird with wintering habitats further South. The birds can be found along several coastal wetlands, including Point Calimere, Pulicat, parts of Puducherry and Kanyakumari, the Sundarbans, and the mudflats of Gujarat and Maharashtra. Across Tamil Nadu, the species is familiar to birders. “You can spot them at wetlands such as Kurichi and Ukkadam in Coimbatore,” says birder K Selvaganesh adding that the flock plays an important part of the food chain as prey for raptors, including the Western marsh marrier and the brahminy kite. Goa-based Rakesh Dhareshwar, a wildlife photographer says Goa and the wider west coast are reliable places to find them each season. “This year, I was delighted to see them inland too, at Bhigwan in Maharashtra, during a mid-Novemeber trip. However, shorebirds worldwide are in decline. Loss of coastal and inland wetlands, reclamation of mudflats, and pollution threaten stopover and wintering sites these birds depend on. The good news is that we can fix this. Protecting wetlands, salt pans and estuaries, and sharing spaces thoughtfully with people can make a real difference.” Shorebirds worldwide are in decline | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: In his new book, Little Stint: A Migrant’s Tale (Neythal Pathipakam), author Byju H explores the bird’s remarkable journey through a blend of science and unconventional storytelling allowing the bird to narrate its own life, beginning with emerging from an egg in the Arctic tundra. “I wanted readers to travel with the bird,” he says adding that the book also highlights the fact that the bird’s ability to navigate vast distances depends on the availability of suitable wetlands along its migratory route.

Across Tamil Nadu, the species is familiar to birders. “You can spot them at wetlands such as Kurichi and Ukkadam in Coimbatore,” says birder K Selvaganesh adding that the flock plays an important part of the food chain as prey for raptors, including the Western marsh marrier and the brahminy kite. Goa-based Rakesh Dhareshwar, a wildlife photographer says Goa and the wider west coast are reliable places to find them each season. “This year, I was delighted to see them inland too, at Bhigwan in Maharashtra, during a mid-Novemeber trip. However, shorebirds worldwide are in decline. Loss of coastal and inland wetlands, reclamation of mudflats, and pollution threaten stopover and wintering sites these birds depend on. The good news is that we can fix this. Protecting wetlands, salt pans and estuaries, and sharing spaces thoughtfully with people can make a real difference.” Shorebirds worldwide are in decline | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: In his new book, Little Stint: A Migrant’s Tale (Neythal Pathipakam), author Byju H explores the bird’s remarkable journey through a blend of science and unconventional storytelling allowing the bird to narrate its own life, beginning with emerging from an egg in the Arctic tundra. “I wanted readers to travel with the bird,” he says adding that the book also highlights the fact that the bird’s ability to navigate vast distances depends on the availability of suitable wetlands along its migratory route.

hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — लिटिल स्टिंट अपने आर्कटिक प्रजनन मैदानों और भारतीय आर्द्रभूमियों के बीच हजारों किलोमीटर की यात्रा करता है।।

hinglishTracks.en: But as shrinking mudflats and changing landscapes threaten its feeding and resting habitats, this tiny shorebird tells an important story about conserving wetlands

hinglishTracks.en: The little stint, a 25-gram shorebird, comes in lakhs from the Arctic to the shores of India, particularly to Point Calimere.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — छोटा सा जीव, 25 ग्राम का समुद्री पक्षी, लाखों की संख्या में आर्कटिक से भारत के तटों तक, विशेष रूप से प्वाइंट कैलिमेरे तक आता है।।

hinglishTracks.en: “It’s an unforgettable sight,” says S Sivakumar, who has been involved in monitoring shorebirds in the Gulf of Mannar for over a decade.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — “यह एक अविस्मरणीय दृश्य है,” एस शिवकुमार कहते हैं, जो एक दशक से अधिक समय से मन्नार की खाड़ी में तटीय पक्षियों की निगरानी में शामिल हैं।।

hinglishTracks.en: The birds remain through the winter months and depart between March and April, sometimes later in May.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — पक्षी पूरे सर्दियों के महीनों में रहते हैं और मार्च और अप्रैल के बीच, कभी-कभी बाद में मई में प्रस्थान करते हैं।।

hinglishTracks.en: “In the 1980s, the little stint could be seen in several lakhs at any point of time.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — “1980 के दशक में, किसी भी समय छोटे से लक्षण को कई लाख लोगों में देखा जा सकता था।।

hinglishTracks.en: Even now, the numbers are still over a lakh as the Point Calimere Wetland Complex covers over 300 kilometres across coastal Tamil Nadu ,” says Sivakumar, assistant director at the Bombay Natural History Society’s Bird Migration Study Centre at Point Calimere, adding that such long-term observations help scientists understand how bird populations and their habitats are changing.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — प्वाइंट कैलिमेरे में बॉम्बे नेचुरल हिस्ट्री सोसाइटी के बर्ड माइग्रेशन स्टडी सेंटर के सहायक निदेशक शिवकुमार कहते हैं, “अभी भी संख्या एक लाख से अधिक है क्योंकि प्वाइंट कैलिमेरे वेटलैंड कॉम्प्लेक्स तटीय तमिलनाडु में 300 किलोमीटर से अधिक की दूरी तय करता है।” उन्होंने कहा कि इस तरह के दीर्घकालिक अवलोकन से वैज्ञानिकों को यह समझने में मदद मिलती है कि पक्षियों की आबादी और उनके आवास कैसे बदल रहे हैं।।

hinglishTracks.en: As shrinking mudflats and changing landscapes threaten its feeding and resting habitats, this tiny shorebird tells an important story about conserving wetlands.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — जैसे-जैसे सिकुड़ते कीचड़ और बदलते भू-दृश्यों से इसके भोजन और आराम करने वाले आवासों को खतरा होता है, यह छोटा समुद्री पक्षी आर्द्रभूमि के संरक्षण के बारे में एक महत्वपूर्ण कहानी बताता है।।

hinglishTracks.en: “ This group is declining rapidly due to climate change and loss of habitat.

hinglishTracks.en: Their widespread presence, he adds, indicates the health of wetland ecosystems in India as well as conditions in the Arctic.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — उनका कहना है कि उनकी व्यापक उपस्थिति भारत में आर्द्रभूमि पारिस्थितिकी प्रणालियों के स्वास्थ्य के साथ-साथ आर्कटिक की स्थितियों को भी दर्शाती है।।

hinglishTracks.en: The fact that the little stint is still a fairly common bird does not mean that it is beyond risk.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — तथ्य यह है कि छोटा कद अभी भी काफी सामान्य पक्षी है इसका मतलब यह नहीं है कि यह जोखिम से परे है।।

hinglishTracks.en: It’s numbers and distribution can help draw attention to changes taking place across the habitats it depends on.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — इसकी संख्या और वितरण उन आवासों में होने वाले परिवर्तनों पर ध्यान आकर्षित करने में मदद कर सकता है जिन पर यह निर्भर करता है।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Distribution' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: वितरण — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Distribution' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse और Antonyms हैं: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable।

hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — प्वाइंट कैलिमेरे वेटलैंड्स पर संख्या अभी भी एक लाख से अधिक है | फोटो साभार: एस शिवकुमार।

hinglishTracks.en: The bird’s preparation for migration is as fascinating as the journey itself.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — प्रवास के लिए पक्षी की तैयारी यात्रा जितनी ही आकर्षक है।।

hinglishTracks.en: “Before setting off, they enter a phase of intense feeding called hyperphagia.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — “जाने से पहले, वे हाइपरफैगिया नामक गहन भोजन के चरण में प्रवेश करते हैं।।

hinglishTracks.en: They feed voraciously to build up fat reserves that act as fuel during its journey.

hinglishTracks.en: This can add 50 to 75 percent to the bird’s body weight.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — इससे पक्षी के शरीर का वजन 50 से 75 प्रतिशत तक बढ़ सकता है।।

hinglishTracks.en: There are also physiological changes, some organs shrink in size as the bird prepares for the demands of sustained flight,” explains Sivakumar adding that India is an important destination along the Central Asian Flyway that connects the bird with wintering habitats further South.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — इसमें शारीरिक परिवर्तन भी होते हैं, जैसे-जैसे पक्षी निरंतर उड़ान की मांग के लिए तैयार होते हैं, कुछ अंग आकार में सिकुड़ते जाते हैं,'' शिवकुमार बताते हैं कि भारत मध्य एशियाई फ्लाईवे के साथ एक महत्वपूर्ण गंतव्य है जो पक्षी को दक्षिण में सर्दियों के आवासों से जोड़ता है।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Sustainability' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: सतत विकास — पर्यावरण और भविष्य की पीढ़ियों को नुकसान पहुँचाए बिना लंबे समय तक चलने वाला विकास। इसके Synonyms हैं: Viability, Eco-balance, Durability और Antonyms हैं: Depletion, Unsustainability, Destruction।

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #29 of 30 (25 NOV)

📰 Meet the little stint: The tiny Siberian traveller visiting India’s wetlands

📌 Published: 25 Nov 2026, 04:46:39 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The Little Stint travels thousands of kilometres between its Arctic breeding grounds and Indian wetlands. But as shrinking mudflats and changing landscapes threaten its feeding and resting habitats, this tiny shorebird tells an important story about conserving wetlands

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The little stint, a 25-gram shorebird, comes in lakhs from the Arctic to the shores of India, particularly to Point Calimere. “It’s an unforgettable sight,” says S Sivakumar, who has been involved in monitoring shorebirds in the Gulf of Mannar for over a decade. The birds remain through the winter months and depart between March and April, sometimes later in May. “In the 1980s, the little stint could be seen in several lakhs at any point of time. Even now, the numbers are still over a lakh as the Point Calimere Wetland Complex covers over 300 kilometres across coastal Tamil Nadu ,” says Sivakumar, assistant director at the Bombay Natural History Society’s Bird Migration Study Centre at Point Calimere, adding that such long-term observations help scientists understand how bird populations and their habitats are changing. The birds remain through the winter months and depart between March and April, sometimes later in May | Photo Credit: S Sivakumar The tiny bird’s annual migration journey, a feat of endurance, involves multiple stopovers across different landscapes, each of which must provide sufficient food and safe resting grounds. As shrinking mudflats and changing landscapes threaten its feeding and resting habitats, this tiny shorebird tells an important story about conserving wetlands. Ashvin Viswanathan, scientist at Bird Count India , places the little stints as the most visible representatives of a special group of shorebirds that breed in the Arctic. “ This group is declining rapidly due to climate change and loss of habitat. Little stints too are declining in India according to SoIB,” he says, referring to the State of India’s Birds assessment. Their widespread presence, he adds, indicates the health of wetland ecosystems in India as well as conditions in the Arctic. The fact that the little stint is still a fairly common bird does not mean that it is beyond risk. It’s numbers and distribution can help draw attention to changes taking place across the habitats it depends on. The numbers are still over a lakh at Point Calimere wetlands | Photo Credit: S Sivakumar The bird’s preparation for migration is as fascinating as the journey itself. “Before setting off, they enter a phase of intense feeding called hyperphagia. They feed voraciously to build up fat reserves that act as fuel during its journey. This can add 50 to 75 percent to the bird’s body weight. There are also physiological changes, some organs shrink in size as the bird prepares for the demands of sustained flight,” explains Sivakumar adding that India is an important destination along the Central Asian Flyway that connects the bird with wintering habitats further South. The birds can be found along several coastal wetlands, including Point Calimere, Pulicat, parts of Puducherry and Kanyakumari, the Sundarbans, and the mudflats of Gujarat and Maharashtra. Across Tamil Nadu, the species is familiar to birders. “You can spot them at wetlands such as Kurichi and Ukkadam in Coimbatore,” says birder K Selvaganesh adding that the flock plays an important part of the food chain as prey for raptors, including the Western marsh marrier and the brahminy kite. Goa-based Rakesh Dhareshwar, a wildlife photographer says Goa and the wider west coast are reliable places to find them each season. “This year, I was delighted to see them inland too, at Bhigwan in Maharashtra, during a mid-Novemeber trip. However, shorebirds worldwide are in decline. Loss of coastal and inland wetlands, reclamation of mudflats, and pollution threaten stopover and wintering sites these birds depend on. The good news is that we can fix this. Protecting wetlands, salt pans and estuaries, and sharing spaces thoughtfully with people can make a real difference.” Shorebirds worldwide are in decline | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: In his new book, Little Stint: A Migrant’s Tale (Neythal Pathipakam), author Byju H explores the bird’s remarkable journey through a blend of science and unconventional storytelling allowing the bird to narrate its own life, beginning with emerging from an egg in the Arctic tundra. “I wanted readers to travel with the bird,” he says adding that the book also highlights the fact that the bird’s ability to navigate vast distances depends on the availability of suitable wetlands along its migratory route.

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Sustainability (Noun)
सतत विकास — पर्यावरण और भविष्य की पीढ़ियों को नुकसान पहुँचाए बिना लंबे समय तक चलने वाला विकास।
✓ Syn: Viability, Eco-balance, Durability  |  ✖ Ant: Depletion, Unsustainability, Destruction
Unconventional (Adjective)
अपरंपरागत — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Unconventional' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Physiological (Adjective)
शारीरिक — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Physiological' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Distribution (Adjective / Verb)
वितरण — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Distribution' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse  |  ✖ Ant: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable

Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🚀 Science, Tech & Environment passage on "Meet the little stint: The tiny Siberian traveller visiting India’s wetlands", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. The Little Stint travels thousands of kilometres between its Arctic breeding grounds and Indian wetlands.

D. The author contends that 'Meet the little stint: The tiny Siberian trav' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "The Little Stint travels thousands of kilometres between its Arctic breeding grounds and Indian wetlands." Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Meet the little stint: The tiny Siberian traveller visiting India’s wetlands"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. “I wanted readers to travel with the bird,” he says adding that the book also highlights the fact that the bird’s ability to navigate vast distances...
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "“I wanted readers to travel with the bird,” he says adding that the book also highlights the fact that the bird’s ability to navigate vast distances..." (Hinglish Arth: “मैं चाहता था कि पाठक पक्षी के साथ यात्रा करें,” वह कहते हैं कि पुस्तक इस तथ्य पर भी प्रकाश डालती है कि पक्षी की विशाल दूरी तय करने की क्षमता उसके प्रवासी मार्गों के साथ उपयुक्त आर्द्रभूमि की उपलब्धता पर निर्भर करती है।)

articles.title: Tamil Nadu’s water dispute with Karnataka: Palaniswami, Dhinakaran criticise TVK government
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Taking a swipe at Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay, AIADMK chief Edappadi K. Palaniswami said the Karnataka government’s move reflected its perception that the Tamil Nadu administration was weak.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) strongly criticised the Congress government in Karnataka for reportedly moving the Supreme Court seeking a stay on several irrigation projects that will impact Tamil Nadu, including the ambitious Cauvery-Vaigai-Gundar river-linking project. Mr. Palaniswami accused the Congress of consistently acting against Tamil Nadu’s interests and questioned whether the TVK government, which is aligned with the Congress, would take a firm stand to protect the State’s water rights. He recalled that the Cauvery-Gundar river-linking project was formulated during his tenure as Chief Minister under the AIADMK government. Describing it as one of south India’s largest river-linking initiatives, he said its completion would significantly improve water availability for agriculture and help address water scarcity in several regions. Mr. Palaniswami also alleged that Karnataka had sought restrictions on several other Tamil Nadu irrigation projects. Taking a swipe at Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay , Mr. Palaniswami said the Karnataka government’s move reflected its perception that the Tamil Nadu administration was weak. He also criticised the government for not convening an all-party meeting despite his demand. He urged for initiating all possible legal measures to safeguard Tamil Nadu’s water resources. Meanwhile, AMMK general secretary T.T.V. Dhinakaran urged the Tamil Nadu government to legally challenge Karnataka’s move seeking a ban on several irrigation projects being implemented across the State along the Cauvery. Citing a report published in The Hindu in this regard, Mr. Dhinakaran said Karnataka has approached the Supreme Court seeking to stall projects, including the Cauvery-Vaigai-Gundar river-linking project and the Sarabanga lift irrigation scheme. Accusing the TVK government of failing to protect Tamil Nadu’s water rights, Mr. Dhinakaran sought transparency on the funds allocated and work completed under the river-linking project.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Tamil Nadu / All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam / Amma Makkal Munnetra Kazhagam / Karnataka / Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #7 of 30 (25 NOV)

📰 Tamil Nadu’s water dispute with Karnataka: Palaniswami, Dhinakaran criticise TVK government

📌 Published: 25 Nov 2026, 07:24:39 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Taking a swipe at Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay, AIADMK chief Edappadi K. Palaniswami said the Karnataka government’s move reflected its perception that the Tamil Nadu administration was weak.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) strongly criticised the Congress government in Karnataka for reportedly moving the Supreme Court seeking a stay on several irrigation projects that will impact Tamil Nadu, including the ambitious Cauvery-Vaigai-Gundar river-linking project. Mr. Palaniswami accused the Congress of consistently acting against Tamil Nadu’s interests and questioned whether the TVK government, which is aligned with the Congress, would take a firm stand to protect the State’s water rights. He recalled that the Cauvery-Gundar river-linking project was formulated during his tenure as Chief Minister under the AIADMK government. Describing it as one of south India’s largest river-linking initiatives, he said its completion would significantly improve water availability for agriculture and help address water scarcity in several regions. Mr. Palaniswami also alleged that Karnataka had sought restrictions on several other Tamil Nadu irrigation projects. Taking a swipe at Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay , Mr. Palaniswami said the Karnataka government’s move reflected its perception that the Tamil Nadu administration was weak. He also criticised the government for not convening an all-party meeting despite his demand. He urged for initiating all possible legal measures to safeguard Tamil Nadu’s water resources. Meanwhile, AMMK general secretary T.T.V. Dhinakaran urged the Tamil Nadu government to legally challenge Karnataka’s move seeking a ban on several irrigation projects being implemented across the State along the Cauvery. Citing a report published in The Hindu in this regard, Mr. Dhinakaran said Karnataka has approached the Supreme Court seeking to stall projects, including the Cauvery-Vaigai-Gundar river-linking project and the Sarabanga lift irrigation scheme. Accusing the TVK government of failing to protect Tamil Nadu’s water rights, Mr. Dhinakaran sought transparency on the funds allocated and work completed under the river-linking project.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Tamil Nadu / All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam / Amma Makkal Munnetra Kazhagam / Karnataka / Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam

Palaniswami on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) strongly criticised the Congress government in Karnataka for reportedly moving the Supreme Court seeking a stay on several irrigation projects that will impact Tamil Nadu, including the ambitious Cauvery-Vaigai-Gundar river-linking project. Mr. Palaniswami accused the Congress of consistently acting against Tamil Nadu’s interests and questioned whether the TVK government, which is aligned with the Congress, would take a firm stand to protect the State’s water rights. He recalled that the Cauvery-Gundar river-linking project was formulated during his tenure as Chief Minister under the AIADMK government. Describing it as one of south India’s largest river-linking initiatives, he said its completion would significantly improve water availability for agriculture and help address water scarcity in several regions. Mr. Palaniswami also alleged that Karnataka had sought restrictions on several other Tamil Nadu irrigation projects. Taking a swipe at Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay , Mr. Palaniswami said the Karnataka government’s move reflected its perception that the Tamil Nadu administration was weak. He also criticised the government for not convening an all-party meeting despite his demand. He urged for initiating all possible legal measures to safeguard Tamil Nadu’s water resources. Meanwhile, AMMK general secretary T.T.V. Dhinakaran urged the Tamil Nadu government to legally challenge Karnataka’s move seeking a ban on several irrigation projects being implemented across the State along the Cauvery. Citing a report published in The Hindu in this regard, Mr. Dhinakaran said Karnataka has approached the Supreme Court seeking to stall projects, including the Cauvery-Vaigai-Gundar river-linking project and the Sarabanga lift irrigation scheme. Accusing the TVK government of failing to protect Tamil Nadu’s water rights, Mr. Dhinakaran sought transparency on the funds allocated and work completed under the river-linking project.

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Devotees barred from Tirupparankundram hill for the second consecutive day and heavy security deployed

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A section of advocates on Wednesday (November 25) staged a protest outside the Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court, condemning the Tamil Nadu government and police for failing to light the Karthigai Deepam at the ‘Deepathoon’ atop Thirupparankundram hill despite a Supreme Court order permitting one-time lighting of the lamp on the stone pillar. Raising slogans against the state administration and police, the protesting lawyers accused the government of showing disrespect to the apex court and the Constitution. The demonstrators also questioned the authorities over the non-implementation of the court’s directive and protested the action taken against Hindu Munnani functionaries. The Tamil Nadu government on Wednesday (November 25) apologised to the Supreme Court over the non-lighting of the ceremonial lamp at the disputed Deepathoon (pillar) on the Thirupparankundram hill and blamed the Arulmigu Subramaniaswamy temple authorities for it, as contempt proceedings were sought against the State. The Supreme Court, while refusing to initiate suo motu contempt proceedings, said it will hear such a plea if filed. A bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi said the registry will verify the filing of applications for permission to light the lamp, including contempt petitions, and the court will see if they can be listed on Thursday (November 26) or Friday (November 27). The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) targeted the Tamil Nadu government over what it alleged was a defiance of the Supreme Court’s order on the Karthigai Deepam festival. BJP accuses INDIA alliance and Tamil Nadu government of contempt and anti-Hindu bias over Karthigai Deepam ruling and SC order. The Vishva Hindu Parishad (VHP) accused the TVK government in Tamil Nadu of defying the Supreme Court’s order on the traditional lighting of the Karthigai Deepam at ‘Deepathoon’ on Thiruparankundram hill near Madurai, saying its actions amount to an insult to the judiciary, the Constitution and Hindu religious sentiments. The RSS affiliate also warned that “anti-Hindu” politics and such a mindset are nearing extinction from the country’s political landscape and will soon disappear from Tamil Nadu as well. In a statement, VHP international president Alok Kumar said preventing a centuries-old religious tradition hurts the faith and sentiments of crores of devotees of Lord Murugan and reflects the state government’s “anti-Hindu obstinacy”.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “Preventing a centuries-old religious tradition despite the Supreme Court’s order is a grave insult to the Indian Constitution and the judiciary. It is also a serious affront to the faith and beliefs of crores of devotees of Lord Murugan,” Mr. Kumar said.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #8 of 30 (25 NOV)

📰 Thirupparankundram row updates: Supreme Court to examine if wilful disobedience occurred, as State and Hindu parties spar

📌 Published: 25 Nov 2026, 07:25:15 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Devotees barred from Tirupparankundram hill for the second consecutive day and heavy security deployed

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A section of advocates on Wednesday (November 25) staged a protest outside the Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court, condemning the Tamil Nadu government and police for failing to light the Karthigai Deepam at the ‘Deepathoon’ atop Thirupparankundram hill despite a Supreme Court order permitting one-time lighting of the lamp on the stone pillar. Raising slogans against the state administration and police, the protesting lawyers accused the government of showing disrespect to the apex court and the Constitution. The demonstrators also questioned the authorities over the non-implementation of the court’s directive and protested the action taken against Hindu Munnani functionaries. The Tamil Nadu government on Wednesday (November 25) apologised to the Supreme Court over the non-lighting of the ceremonial lamp at the disputed Deepathoon (pillar) on the Thirupparankundram hill and blamed the Arulmigu Subramaniaswamy temple authorities for it, as contempt proceedings were sought against the State. The Supreme Court, while refusing to initiate suo motu contempt proceedings, said it will hear such a plea if filed. A bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi said the registry will verify the filing of applications for permission to light the lamp, including contempt petitions, and the court will see if they can be listed on Thursday (November 26) or Friday (November 27). The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) targeted the Tamil Nadu government over what it alleged was a defiance of the Supreme Court’s order on the Karthigai Deepam festival. BJP accuses INDIA alliance and Tamil Nadu government of contempt and anti-Hindu bias over Karthigai Deepam ruling and SC order. The Vishva Hindu Parishad (VHP) accused the TVK government in Tamil Nadu of defying the Supreme Court’s order on the traditional lighting of the Karthigai Deepam at ‘Deepathoon’ on Thiruparankundram hill near Madurai, saying its actions amount to an insult to the judiciary, the Constitution and Hindu religious sentiments. The RSS affiliate also warned that “anti-Hindu” politics and such a mindset are nearing extinction from the country’s political landscape and will soon disappear from Tamil Nadu as well. In a statement, VHP international president Alok Kumar said preventing a centuries-old religious tradition hurts the faith and sentiments of crores of devotees of Lord Murugan and reflects the state government’s “anti-Hindu obstinacy”.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “Preventing a centuries-old religious tradition despite the Supreme Court’s order is a grave insult to the Indian Constitution and the judiciary. It is also a serious affront to the faith and beliefs of crores of devotees of Lord Murugan,” Mr. Kumar said.

कानूनी अनुमति या स्वीकार्यता — किसी कार्य को करने की वैध छूट।

क्रियान्वयन / ज़मीनी स्तर पर लागू करना — किसी योजना या फैसले को असलियत में पूरा करना।
✓ Syn: Execution, Enforcement, Fulfillment  |  ✖ Ant: Abandonment, Neglect, Cancellation
Constitutional (Adjective)
संवैधानिक — देश के संविधान (Constitution) के दायरे और मौलिक अधिकारों के अनुरूप।
✓ Syn: Statutory, Legitimate, Lawful  |  ✖ Ant: Unconstitutional, Illegal, Arbitrary
Administration (Noun)
प्रशासन — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Administration' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial

articles.title: The Hindu’s coffee table book on exploration of the Western Ghats released
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The book titled, ‘Mountains of Our Destiny: The Western Ghats, A Journey Through The Southern Monsoon Mountains by Vrinda Ramanan and J. Ramanan is a sequel to ‘Mountains of our Destiny: An Expedition to the Indian Himalaya’, also by the same authors.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Hindu launched a coffee table book titled, ‘Mountains of Our Destiny: The Western Ghats, A Journey Through The Southern Monsoon Mountains’, on Wednesday (November 25, 2026). Authored by Vrinda Ramanan and J. Ramanan, mountaineers, writers and photographers, the book was launched by Tamil Nadu Forests Minister R.V. Ranjith Kumar. The first copies were received by Rohit Ramesh, Director, Suresh Nambath, Editor, and L.V. Navaneeth, CEO, The Hindu . The book is a sequel to ‘Mountains of our Destiny: An Expedition to the Indian Himalaya’, also by the same authors. Speaking on the occasion, the Minister noted the importance of the forests, rivers and mountains to sustaining agriculture, livelihoods and ecological balance. He highlighted the need to ensure forest conservation, spoke of the measures taken by the government to improve upon work being done, such as AI technology to prevent elephant deaths on railway tracks and in the control of forest fires, and congratulated the authors on their work. Author J. Ramanan explained that the two mountain ranges: the Himalayas and the Western Ghats formed the bedrock of India’s existence. Without them, he said, we would not have had our rivers. The 1,500 km Western Ghats in particular, recognised as a biodiversity hotspot, was one of the richest ecological resources in the country, sustaining thousands of lives. The monsoon in India, Mr. Ramanan said, is shaped by the Western Ghats and the Himalayas. The book was an attempt to create awareness about, and educate people on the importance of maintaining ecological balance through their preservation. Through more than 400 photographs, field experiences and narratives, the book explores the geology, wildlife, plants, indigenous communities and the intricate web of life that sustains these mountains. It also examines the growing pressures of plantations, invasive species, tourism, dams and other human interventions, highlighting the urgent need for conservation.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The book is available at The Hindu ’s online bookstore: https://publications.thehindugroup.com/ . The cover price of the book is ₹2,999. At present, the book is available at a special launch offer price of ₹2,249 for a limited period of time. Those interested can also scan the QR code to buy a copy.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #9 of 30 (25 NOV)

📰 The Hindu’s coffee table book on exploration of the Western Ghats released

📌 Published: 25 Nov 2026, 07:22:40 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The book titled, ‘Mountains of Our Destiny: The Western Ghats, A Journey Through The Southern Monsoon Mountains by Vrinda Ramanan and J. Ramanan is a sequel to ‘Mountains of our Destiny: An Expedition to the Indian Himalaya’, also by the same authors.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Hindu launched a coffee table book titled, ‘Mountains of Our Destiny: The Western Ghats, A Journey Through The Southern Monsoon Mountains’, on Wednesday (November 25, 2026). Authored by Vrinda Ramanan and J. Ramanan, mountaineers, writers and photographers, the book was launched by Tamil Nadu Forests Minister R.V. Ranjith Kumar. The first copies were received by Rohit Ramesh, Director, Suresh Nambath, Editor, and L.V. Navaneeth, CEO, The Hindu . The book is a sequel to ‘Mountains of our Destiny: An Expedition to the Indian Himalaya’, also by the same authors. Speaking on the occasion, the Minister noted the importance of the forests, rivers and mountains to sustaining agriculture, livelihoods and ecological balance. He highlighted the need to ensure forest conservation, spoke of the measures taken by the government to improve upon work being done, such as AI technology to prevent elephant deaths on railway tracks and in the control of forest fires, and congratulated the authors on their work. Author J. Ramanan explained that the two mountain ranges: the Himalayas and the Western Ghats formed the bedrock of India’s existence. Without them, he said, we would not have had our rivers. The 1,500 km Western Ghats in particular, recognised as a biodiversity hotspot, was one of the richest ecological resources in the country, sustaining thousands of lives. The monsoon in India, Mr. Ramanan said, is shaped by the Western Ghats and the Himalayas. The book was an attempt to create awareness about, and educate people on the importance of maintaining ecological balance through their preservation. Through more than 400 photographs, field experiences and narratives, the book explores the geology, wildlife, plants, indigenous communities and the intricate web of life that sustains these mountains. It also examines the growing pressures of plantations, invasive species, tourism, dams and other human interventions, highlighting the urgent need for conservation.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The book is available at The Hindu ’s online bookstore: https://publications.thehindugroup.com/ . The cover price of the book is ₹2,999. At present, the book is available at a special launch offer price of ₹2,249 for a limited period of time. Those interested can also scan the QR code to buy a copy.

Indigenous (Adjective)
स्वदेशी — अपने ही देश (भारत) के वैज्ञानिकों और इंजीनियरों द्वारा देश में विकसित किया गया।
✓ Syn: Domestic, Home-grown, Native  |  ✖ Ant: Imported, Foreign, Exotic
Sustainability (Noun)
सतत विकास — पर्यावरण और भविष्य की पीढ़ियों को नुकसान पहुँचाए बिना लंबे समय तक चलने वाला विकास।
✓ Syn: Viability, Eco-balance, Durability  |  ✖ Ant: Depletion, Unsustainability, Destruction
Conservation (Noun)
संरक्षण — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Conservation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Biodiversity (Noun)
जैव विविधता — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Biodiversity' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial

A. The book titled, ‘Mountains of Our Destiny: The Western Ghats, A Journey Through The Southern Monsoon Mountains by Vrinda Ramanan and J.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'The Hindu’s coffee table book on exploration of ' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'The Hindu’s coffee table book on exploration ' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'The Hindu’s coffee table book on exploration ' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. The monsoon in India, Mr. Ramanan said, is shaped by the Western Ghats and the Himalayas. The book was an attempt to create awareness about, and educate people on the importance of maintaining ecological balance through their preservation. Through more than 400 photographs, field experiences and narratives, the book explores the geology, wildlife, plants, indigenous communities and the intricate web of life that sustains these mountains. It also examines the growing pressures of plantations, invasive species, tourism, dams and other human interventions, highlighting the urgent need for conservation.

articles.title: Drought affects groundnut cultivation in Karnataka; prices rise amid supply shortage
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: According to Agriculture Department data, groundnut sowing this year stood at 1.59 lakh hectares against the target of 2.54 lakh hectares. Of the area sown, crop failure has been recorded across 1.49 lakh hectares, accounting for 93.71% of the total sown area

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: As Bengaluru gears up for the historic Kadlekai Parishe, celebrated in Basavanagudi and Malleshwaram, the arrival of groundnuts in Karnataka’s markets has been delayed this year due to drought conditions, with farmers reporting reduced sowing and poor yields across major groundnut-growing districts. Groundnut farmers in Kolar, Chitradurga, Dharwad, Haveri, Mandya, Mysuru and Tumakuru districts said sowing had declined this year due to inadequate rainfall and drying borewells. Groundnut is predominantly cultivated during the kharif season in these districts, while Vijayapura, Yadgir, Kalaburagi and Raichur districts also cultivate the crop during the summer season. According to data from the Department of Agriculture, groundnut sowing this year stood at 1.59 lakh hectares against the target of 2.54 lakh hectares. Of the area sown, crop failure has been recorded across 1.49 lakh hectares, accounting for 93.71% of the total sown area. Agriculture Department officials attributed the extensive crop failure primarily to deficient rainfall, pointing out that groundnut cultivation in Karnataka is largely rain-dependent. Of the 2.54 lakh hectares targeted for cultivation, around 2.38 lakh hectares are rainfed, while only approximately 0.17 lakh hectares are under irrigation. Although groundnut is not widely cultivated during the rabi season, the department’s data showed that sowing had been completed across 0.58 lakh hectares as of November 13, against a target of 1.33 lakh hectares. Speaking to The Hindu , a senior Agriculture Department official said that the farmers who cultivate groundnut during the rabi season generally have access to better irrigation facilities. “Farmers who cultivate during the rabi season have good water facilities through borewells, or their fields are usually located in command areas,” the official said. Pointing to the delayed market arrivals, K.P. Bhoothaiah, senior vice-president of the Karnataka Rajya Raitha Sangha, Chitradurga, said even farmers who had managed to cultivate groundnut were reporting poor yields. “Even where farmers have cultivated groundnut, the yield is low and the seeds are smaller in size,” he said. Abhilash Reddy, a farmer from Kolar district, said that he had not cultivated groundnut this year due to drought, drying borewells and a shortage of agricultural labourers.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “Groundnut cultivation is labour-intensive. The crop has to be harvested, dried under the sun and shelled. With the borewells drying up and labour becoming difficult to find, I decided not to cultivate it this year,” he said.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #10 of 30 (25 NOV)

📰 Drought affects groundnut cultivation in Karnataka; prices rise amid supply shortage

📌 Published: 25 Nov 2026, 07:19:46 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: According to Agriculture Department data, groundnut sowing this year stood at 1.59 lakh hectares against the target of 2.54 lakh hectares. Of the area sown, crop failure has been recorded across 1.49 lakh hectares, accounting for 93.71% of the total sown area

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: As Bengaluru gears up for the historic Kadlekai Parishe, celebrated in Basavanagudi and Malleshwaram, the arrival of groundnuts in Karnataka’s markets has been delayed this year due to drought conditions, with farmers reporting reduced sowing and poor yields across major groundnut-growing districts. Groundnut farmers in Kolar, Chitradurga, Dharwad, Haveri, Mandya, Mysuru and Tumakuru districts said sowing had declined this year due to inadequate rainfall and drying borewells. Groundnut is predominantly cultivated during the kharif season in these districts, while Vijayapura, Yadgir, Kalaburagi and Raichur districts also cultivate the crop during the summer season. According to data from the Department of Agriculture, groundnut sowing this year stood at 1.59 lakh hectares against the target of 2.54 lakh hectares. Of the area sown, crop failure has been recorded across 1.49 lakh hectares, accounting for 93.71% of the total sown area. Agriculture Department officials attributed the extensive crop failure primarily to deficient rainfall, pointing out that groundnut cultivation in Karnataka is largely rain-dependent. Of the 2.54 lakh hectares targeted for cultivation, around 2.38 lakh hectares are rainfed, while only approximately 0.17 lakh hectares are under irrigation. Although groundnut is not widely cultivated during the rabi season, the department’s data showed that sowing had been completed across 0.58 lakh hectares as of November 13, against a target of 1.33 lakh hectares. Speaking to The Hindu , a senior Agriculture Department official said that the farmers who cultivate groundnut during the rabi season generally have access to better irrigation facilities. “Farmers who cultivate during the rabi season have good water facilities through borewells, or their fields are usually located in command areas,” the official said. Pointing to the delayed market arrivals, K.P. Bhoothaiah, senior vice-president of the Karnataka Rajya Raitha Sangha, Chitradurga, said even farmers who had managed to cultivate groundnut were reporting poor yields. “Even where farmers have cultivated groundnut, the yield is low and the seeds are smaller in size,” he said. Abhilash Reddy, a farmer from Kolar district, said that he had not cultivated groundnut this year due to drought, drying borewells and a shortage of agricultural labourers.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “Groundnut cultivation is labour-intensive. The crop has to be harvested, dried under the sun and shelled. With the borewells drying up and labour becoming difficult to find, I decided not to cultivate it this year,” he said.

Department (Adjective)

A. According to Agriculture Department data, groundnut sowing this year stood at 1.59 lakh hectares against the target of 2.54 lakh hectares.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Drought affects groundnut cultivation in Karnata' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Drought affects groundnut cultivation in Karn' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Drought affects groundnut cultivation in Karn' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "According to Agriculture Department data, groundnut sowing this year stood at 1.59 lakh hectares against the target of 2.54 lakh hectares." D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.

articles.title: Operation Gaja in Karnataka: People protest in Mudigere, observe bandh
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The Operation Gaja was launched after two people were killed in separate elephant attacks in Belur taluk. The department plans to relocate about 56 elephants.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The bandh called in Mudigere on Wednesday against Operation Gaja, the Forest Department’s drive to push wild elephants from Belur in Hassan district towards the Bhadra Wildlife Sanctuary, evoked an impressive response. The operation was launched after two people were killed in elephant attacks in Belur taluk. The bandh was called by various political parties and organisations, including farmers’ groups. Shops and hotels remained shut from 6 a.m. Autorickshaw associations backed the call, and auto stands stayed empty through the day. Most private schools and colleges had declared a holiday a day earlier. Government schools and colleges opened in the morning and were closed later, leaving students from rural areas inconvenienced. Lawyers stayed away from court and took out a march from the court premises to Lions Circle. KSRTC buses operated but ran almost empty, and several rural routes were cancelled. Heavy police deployment was seen in Mudigere town, Hand Post, Banakal, Kottigehara, Jannapura and Gonibeedu. Western Range IGP Shashikumar and Superintendent of Police Jitendra Kumar Dayama camped in the town. Protesters from across the taluk blocked the Kadur–Mangaluru National Highway for over an hour. They raised slogans against the government and Hassan district in-charge Minister K.M. Shivalinge Gowda, and burned his photograph. They placed coffee and arecanut plants damaged by elephants in Makonahalli, Gowthalli, Pura and Karabail on the road. They refused to move until the Deputy Conservator of Forests (DCF) met them. After police persuaded them to end the blockade, they marched to the Forest Department’s sub-division office, staged a dharna and raised slogans against the State government, the department and elected representatives. DCF K.T. Boraiah received a memorandum from the protesters. He said a meeting of Ministers, MLAs and senior officials would be held in Bengaluru. Former MLC M.K. Pranesh said the people of the taluk had shown patience and that it should not be tested. He said compensation was not what they wanted and demanded that the elephants be driven to Nagarahole or Bandipur. He accused Mudigere MLA Nayana Motamma of seeking sympathy through her offer to resign and said the ruling party’s legislators should have used their influence in government to find a lasting solution. Former town panchayat president P.G. Anukumar said farmers were leaving their land fallow because of wild animals. He demanded that the elephants be sent back to Belur and warned of a hunger strike from Thursday if this was not done.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The protesters took exception to Mudigere MLA Nayana Motamma for offering to resign. “The MLA should have joined the protest if she were genuinely concerned about the plight of farmers, instead of submitting the resignation," the proesters said.
