ultraAnalyticalQuestions2.question: Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Great Nicobar Island project: Final Calcutta High Court hearing deferred as Centre seeks to file affidavit, objections"?
options: Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
The petitioner’s counsel objected to this and clarified that these two petitions specifically deal with orders that reduce the buffer zones for two...
Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
ultraAnalyticalQuestions2.answerText: The petitioner’s counsel objected to this and clarified that these two petitions specifically deal with orders that reduce the buffer zones for two...
ultraAnalyticalQuestions2.hinglishExplanation: Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "The petitioner’s counsel objected to this and clarified that these two petitions specifically deal with orders that reduce the buffer zones for two..." (Hinglish Arth: याचिकाकर्ता के वकील ने इस पर आपत्ति जताई और स्पष्ट किया कि ये दोनों याचिकाएं विशेष रूप से उन आदेशों से संबंधित हैं जो ग्रेट निकोबार द्वीप पर दो विशिष्ट राष्ट्रीय उद्यानों के लिए बफर जोन को कम करते हैं।)

hinglishTracks.en: Centre argues that the FRA is not implemented in the A&NI, objects to some petitions claiming that they should be heard by the NGT or SC; next hearing posted for January 13, 2027; court to hear Attorney General of India on January 22
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — केंद्र का तर्क है कि एफआरए को ए एंड एनआई में लागू नहीं किया गया है, कुछ याचिकाओं पर आपत्ति जताते हुए दावा किया गया है कि उन्हें एनजीटी या एससी द्वारा सुना जाना चाहिए; अगली सुनवाई 13 जनवरी, 2027 को तय की गई; अदालत 22 जनवरी को भारत के अटॉर्नी जनरल की सुनवाई करेगी। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Implementation' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: क्रियान्वयन / ज़मीनी स्तर पर लागू करना — किसी योजना या फैसले को असलियत में पूरा करना। इसके Synonyms हैं: Execution, Enforcement, Fulfillment और Antonyms हैं: Abandonment, Neglect, Cancellation।

hinglishTracks.en: The Calcutta High Court’s final hearing in a batch of petitions alleging forest rights violations in diverting forest land for the Union government’s ₹92,000 crore Great Nicobar Island (GNI) project was deferred again on Wednesday (November 25, 2026), after the Centre sought time to file another affidavit and some documents on the question of tribal rights.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — केंद्र सरकार की ₹92,000 करोड़ की ग्रेट निकोबार द्वीप (जीएनआई) परियोजना के लिए वन भूमि को स्थानांतरित करने में वन अधिकारों के उल्लंघन का आरोप लगाने वाली याचिकाओं के एक समूह में कलकत्ता उच्च न्यायालय की अंतिम सुनवाई बुधवार (25 नवंबर, 2026) को फिर से स्थगित कर दी गई, क्योंकि केंद्र ने आदिवासी अधिकारों के सवाल पर एक और हलफनामा और कुछ दस्तावेज दाखिल करने के लिए समय मांगा था।।

hinglishTracks.en: The Centre argued that the Forest Rights Act (FRA), 2006, is not implemented in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands (A&NI), which the petitioners rebutted by noting that the Islands administration has already issued a certificate claiming that FRA rights have been settled, which is what is being challenged.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — केंद्र ने तर्क दिया कि वन अधिकार अधिनियम (एफआरए), 2006, अंडमान और निकोबार द्वीप समूह (ए एंड एनआई) में लागू नहीं किया गया है, जिसे याचिकाकर्ताओं ने यह कहते हुए खारिज कर दिया कि द्वीप प्रशासन ने पहले ही एक प्रमाण पत्र जारी किया है जिसमें दावा किया गया है कि एफआरए अधिकारों का निपटान कर दिया गया है, जिसे चुनौती दी जा रही है।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Implementation' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: क्रियान्वयन / ज़मीनी स्तर पर लागू करना — किसी योजना या फैसले को असलियत में पूरा करना। इसके Synonyms हैं: Execution, Enforcement, Fulfillment और Antonyms हैं: Abandonment, Neglect, Cancellation।

hinglishTracks.en: The High Court Bench, led by Chief Justice Ravindra Vithalrao Ghuge, has now posted the hearing for the batch of petitions on January 13, 2027, when the court is also expected to begin hearing a petition that specifically challenged the A&NI administration’s orders claiming that all provisions of the FRA had been complied with in diverting 121 sq.km.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — मुख्य न्यायाधीश रवींद्र विट्ठलराव घुगे की अगुवाई वाली उच्च न्यायालय की खंडपीठ ने अब याचिकाओं के बैच की सुनवाई 13 जनवरी, 2027 को तय की है, जब अदालत को एक याचिका पर सुनवाई शुरू करने की भी उम्मीद है, जिसमें विशेष रूप से ए एंड एनआई प्रशासन के आदेशों को चुनौती दी गई है, जिसमें दावा किया गया है कि 121 वर्ग किमी को डायवर्ट करने में एफआरए के सभी प्रावधानों का अनुपालन किया गया था।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Administration' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Administration' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Significant, Substantial, Strategic और Antonyms हैं: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial।

hinglishTracks.en: for the GNI project.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — जीएनआई परियोजना के लिए.।

hinglishTracks.en: This comes after the Centre told the Supreme Court in October this year that it would be best if the “High Court is requested to consider and decide all such cases at the earliest”.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — यह तब आया है जब केंद्र ने इस साल अक्टूबर में सुप्रीम कोर्ट को बताया था कि यह सबसे अच्छा होगा यदि "उच्च न्यायालय से ऐसे सभी मामलों पर जल्द से जल्द विचार करने और निर्णय लेने का अनुरोध किया जाए"।।

hinglishTracks.en: On Wednesday, when the Calcutta High Court was about to start the final hearing in these petitions as per the orders of the Supreme Court, Additional Solicitor General (ASG) of India Vikramjit Banerjee submitted that the Centre wished to once again raise preliminary objections on the maintainability of some of the petitions.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — बुधवार को, जब कलकत्ता उच्च न्यायालय सुप्रीम कोर्ट के आदेश के अनुसार इन याचिकाओं पर अंतिम सुनवाई शुरू करने वाला था, भारत के अतिरिक्त सॉलिसिटर जनरल (एएसजी) विक्रमजीत बनर्जी ने प्रस्तुत किया कि केंद्र एक बार फिर से कुछ याचिकाओं की विचारणीयता पर प्रारंभिक आपत्तियां उठाना चाहता है।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Maintainability' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Maintainability' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Significant, Substantial, Strategic और Antonyms हैं: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial।

hinglishTracks.en: Further, on the question of tribal rights, the ASG said the Centre wished to submit one more affidavit with some additional documents.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — इसके अलावा, आदिवासी अधिकारों के सवाल पर, एएसजी ने कहा कि केंद्र कुछ अतिरिक्त दस्तावेजों के साथ एक और हलफनामा दाखिल करना चाहता है।।

hinglishTracks.en: Attorney General for India, R.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — भारत के अटॉर्नी जनरल आर.।

hinglishTracks.en: Venkatramani, also appeared before the High Court on Wednesday.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — वेंकटरमानी भी बुधवार को हाई कोर्ट में पेश हुए।।

hinglishTracks.en: Profile: The Great Nicobar project | Between the sea and the state
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — प्रोफ़ाइल: ग्रेट निकोबार परियोजना | समुद्र और राज्य के बीच।

hinglishTracks.en: The Centre’s lawyers argued that on the question of the FRA, the law that is alleged to have been violated, it has been the historical stand of the Union government, across administrations, that the FRA need not be pursued in A&NI because the Protection of Aboriginal Tribes Regulations, 1956, was already operational there.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — केंद्र के वकीलों ने तर्क दिया कि एफआरए के सवाल पर, जिस कानून का कथित रूप से उल्लंघन किया गया है, यह केंद्र सरकार का सभी प्रशासनों का ऐतिहासिक रुख रहा है कि ए एंड एनआई में एफआरए को आगे बढ़ाने की आवश्यकता नहीं है क्योंकि आदिवासी जनजातियों का संरक्षण विनियम, 1956, पहले से ही वहां लागू था।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Administration' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Administration' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Significant, Substantial, Strategic और Antonyms हैं: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial।

hinglishTracks.en: In response, the petitioner’s counsel pointed out that the A&NI administration had explicitly issued a certificate saying that the rights of local tribespeople had been settled under the FRA and that this certificate is what has been challenged.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — जवाब में, याचिकाकर्ता के वकील ने बताया कि ए एंड एनआई प्रशासन ने स्पष्ट रूप से एक प्रमाण पत्र जारी किया था जिसमें कहा गया था कि स्थानीय जनजातियों के अधिकारों को एफआरए के तहत तय किया गया था और इस प्रमाण पत्र को चुनौती दी गई है।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Administration' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Administration' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Significant, Substantial, Strategic और Antonyms हैं: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial।

hinglishTracks.en: Further, the Centre submitted that it would like to continue arguing on the maintainability of two more petitions tagged as part of the same issue, noting that these two petitions dealt with matters that should be brought either before the National Green Tribunal or the Supreme Court.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — इसके अलावा, केंद्र ने प्रस्तुत किया कि वह इसी मुद्दे के हिस्से के रूप में टैग की गई दो और याचिकाओं की विचारणीयता पर बहस जारी रखना चाहेगा, यह देखते हुए कि ये दोनों याचिकाएं उन मामलों से संबंधित हैं जिन्हें या तो राष्ट्रीय हरित न्यायाधिकरण या सुप्रीम कोर्ट के समक्ष लाया जाना चाहिए।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Maintainability' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Maintainability' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Significant, Substantial, Strategic और Antonyms हैं: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial।

hinglishTracks.en: The petitioner’s counsel objected to this and clarified that these two petitions specifically deal with orders that reduce the buffer zones for two specific National Parks on Great Nicobar Island.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — याचिकाकर्ता के वकील ने इस पर आपत्ति जताई और स्पष्ट किया कि ये दोनों याचिकाएं विशेष रूप से उन आदेशों से संबंधित हैं जो ग्रेट निकोबार द्वीप पर दो विशिष्ट राष्ट्रीय उद्यानों के लिए बफर जोन को कम करते हैं।।

articles.newspaperPrintHtml:
🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #27 of 30 (25 NOV)

📰 Great Nicobar Island project: Final Calcutta High Court hearing deferred as Centre seeks to file affidavit, objections

Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Calcutta High Court’s final hearing in a batch of petitions alleging forest rights violations in diverting forest land for the Union government’s ₹92,000 crore Great Nicobar Island (GNI) project was deferred again on Wednesday (November 25, 2026), after the Centre sought time to file another affidavit and some documents on the question of tribal rights. The Centre argued that the Forest Rights Act (FRA), 2006, is not implemented in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands (A&NI), which the petitioners rebutted by noting that the Islands administration has already issued a certificate claiming that FRA rights have been settled, which is what is being challenged. The High Court Bench, led by Chief Justice Ravindra Vithalrao Ghuge, has now posted the hearing for the batch of petitions on January 13, 2027, when the court is also expected to begin hearing a petition that specifically challenged the A&NI administration’s orders claiming that all provisions of the FRA had been complied with in diverting 121 sq.km. for the GNI project. This comes after the Centre told the Supreme Court in October this year that it would be best if the “High Court is requested to consider and decide all such cases at the earliest”. On Wednesday, when the Calcutta High Court was about to start the final hearing in these petitions as per the orders of the Supreme Court, Additional Solicitor General (ASG) of India Vikramjit Banerjee submitted that the Centre wished to once again raise preliminary objections on the maintainability of some of the petitions. Further, on the question of tribal rights, the ASG said the Centre wished to submit one more affidavit with some additional documents. Attorney General for India, R. Venkatramani, also appeared before the High Court on Wednesday. Profile: The Great Nicobar project | Between the sea and the state The Centre’s lawyers argued that on the question of the FRA, the law that is alleged to have been violated, it has been the historical stand of the Union government, across administrations, that the FRA need not be pursued in A&NI because the Protection of Aboriginal Tribes Regulations, 1956, was already operational there. In response, the petitioner’s counsel pointed out that the A&NI administration had explicitly issued a certificate saying that the rights of local tribespeople had been settled under the FRA and that this certificate is what has been challenged. Further, the Centre submitted that it would like to continue arguing on the maintainability of two more petitions tagged as part of the same issue, noting that these two petitions dealt with matters that should be brought either before the National Green Tribunal or the Supreme Court.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The petitioner’s counsel objected to this and clarified that these two petitions specifically deal with orders that reduce the buffer zones for two specific National Parks on Great Nicobar Island.

articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: BJP and SAD(B) cannot count on their support bases adding up

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Few parties understand the arithmetic of the first-past-the-post (FPTP) system, and the necessity for alliances in States where they are minor players, better than the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) . The BJP has never shied away from partnerships with little ideological cohesion if they keep it electorally relevant. India’s FPTP system is unforgiving to smaller parties in a crowded polity if their support base is limited and dispersed. Votes translate into seats only if the support crosses a certain threshold. In Punjab , the BJP, despite its best efforts, has remained confined to sections of urban Hindu voters. Even after years of poaching leaders from the perennially fractious Congress , and after polling nearly a fifth of the vote in the 2024 general election without winning a seat, it realises that it cannot be relevant without a partner with a wider rural base. The Shiromani Akali Dal (Badal) walked out of the BJP -led National Democratic Alliance in 2020 over the Centre’s farm laws, which were later repealed, as the farmers’ agitation threatened its base in rural Punjab. But much water has flowed down the many rivers of the northern State since then. The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) has consolidated its hold in a crowded political space and is set to complete a full term. The Panthic vote, which used to be the SAD(B)’s core support base, has now fragmented. The SAD(B) appears to believe that it can regain ground only by expanding beyond its Panthic and rural constituencies, and that the farmers’ anger against the BJP is baggage from the past. It is this expedient calculation that now binds the two parties, despite six years of bitter attacks against each other. And it is also why the Union Home Minister, Amit Shah, has pointedly called the SAD(B) the “big brother” in Punjab after sealing the alliance. The SAD(B)’s calculation may not work out as well as it hopes it would. Farmers’ anger against the BJP-led Centre has not entirely dissipated in rural Punjab. In earlier alliances, the two parties transferred votes to each other effectively, partly because their voters had fewer alternatives. But a revived Congress and an entrenched AAP have shown that they can win over urban Hindu voters wary of the Akalis and rural voters who are not inclined to back parties allied with the BJP. That these two sections will simply add up for the alliance is not certain. At best, the alliance consolidates enough of the anti-AAP vote to make this a clear three-cornered contest. Punjab is a sensitive border State and one of India’s granaries. It is also among India’s most indebted States, with a stagnating agrarian economy and a government that has expanded welfare expenditure despite strained finances. It needs a serious competition of ideas on what welfare it can afford and how to revive growth. The SAD(B)-BJP alliance , with its Panthic appeal on one side and Hindu consolidation on the other, instead offers a rehash of familiar identity politics. With AAP failing to deliver on governance, and the Congress stuck in its old ways, Punjab’s voters will have to decide who they dislike the least.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: political parties / Bharatiya Janata Party / Punjab / voting / Indian National Congress / General Elections 2024 / Shiromani Akali Dal / Aam Aadmi Party / agriculture / economy / welfare

✍️ Editorial & Opinion Paragraph #4 of 30 (25 NOV)

📰 Transfer assumption: On the SAD(B)-BJP alliance in Punjab

📌 Published: 25 Nov 2026, 11:55:57 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: BJP and SAD(B) cannot count on their support bases adding up

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Few parties understand the arithmetic of the first-past-the-post (FPTP) system, and the necessity for alliances in States where they are minor players, better than the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) . The BJP has never shied away from partnerships with little ideological cohesion if they keep it electorally relevant. India’s FPTP system is unforgiving to smaller parties in a crowded polity if their support base is limited and dispersed. Votes translate into seats only if the support crosses a certain threshold. In Punjab , the BJP, despite its best efforts, has remained confined to sections of urban Hindu voters. Even after years of poaching leaders from the perennially fractious Congress , and after polling nearly a fifth of the vote in the 2024 general election without winning a seat, it realises that it cannot be relevant without a partner with a wider rural base. The Shiromani Akali Dal (Badal) walked out of the BJP -led National Democratic Alliance in 2020 over the Centre’s farm laws, which were later repealed, as the farmers’ agitation threatened its base in rural Punjab. But much water has flowed down the many rivers of the northern State since then. The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) has consolidated its hold in a crowded political space and is set to complete a full term. The Panthic vote, which used to be the SAD(B)’s core support base, has now fragmented. The SAD(B) appears to believe that it can regain ground only by expanding beyond its Panthic and rural constituencies, and that the farmers’ anger against the BJP is baggage from the past. It is this expedient calculation that now binds the two parties, despite six years of bitter attacks against each other. And it is also why the Union Home Minister, Amit Shah, has pointedly called the SAD(B) the “big brother” in Punjab after sealing the alliance. The SAD(B)’s calculation may not work out as well as it hopes it would. Farmers’ anger against the BJP-led Centre has not entirely dissipated in rural Punjab. In earlier alliances, the two parties transferred votes to each other effectively, partly because their voters had fewer alternatives. But a revived Congress and an entrenched AAP have shown that they can win over urban Hindu voters wary of the Akalis and rural voters who are not inclined to back parties allied with the BJP. That these two sections will simply add up for the alliance is not certain. At best, the alliance consolidates enough of the anti-AAP vote to make this a clear three-cornered contest. Punjab is a sensitive border State and one of India’s granaries. It is also among India’s most indebted States, with a stagnating agrarian economy and a government that has expanded welfare expenditure despite strained finances. It needs a serious competition of ideas on what welfare it can afford and how to revive growth. The SAD(B)-BJP alliance , with its Panthic appeal on one side and Hindu consolidation on the other, instead offers a rehash of familiar identity politics. With AAP failing to deliver on governance, and the Congress stuck in its old ways, Punjab’s voters will have to decide who they dislike the least.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: political parties / Bharatiya Janata Party / Punjab / voting / Indian National Congress / General Elections 2024 / Shiromani Akali Dal / Aam Aadmi Party / agriculture / economy / welfare

संवैधानिक — देश के संविधान (Constitution) के दायरे और मौलिक अधिकारों के अनुरूप।

समेकन — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Consolidation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Ideological (Adjective)
विचारधारा — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Ideological' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Calculation (Noun)
गणना — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Calculation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।

articles.title: Hostile architecture: the design choices keeping wildlife out of urban India
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: For animals and birds in India’s urban areas, hostile architecture takes many forms. ‘From spikes on ledges and nets over balconies to broken glass or spikes on compound walls that prevent animals from entering or perching,’ Shilpa Shirish, who specialises in culturally sensitive design at the Indian Institute of Human Settlements, Bengaluru, said

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: India’s cities and towns are seldom designed with their people in mind — and much less their animals. The green spaces within urban areas are also withdrawing as built area expands. And to deter animals from entering public spaces vouchsafed for humans, planners are turning to designs that increasingly have a collective name of their own: hostile architecture. New York-based architect James Petty defines hostile architecture as one where structures placed in public spaces are rendered “unusable in certain ways or by certain groups”. Slanting stone surfaces and barricades in 19th-century European cities to prevent public urination is one example. Another is anti-homeless architecture, visible as public benches with grooves and hand-rests in between to prevent people from lying down on them, and sloped seats at bus stops. For animals and birds in India’s urban areas, hostile architecture takes many other forms. “From spikes on ledges and nets over balconies to broken glass or spikes on compound walls that prevent animals from entering or perching,” Shilpa Shirish, who specialises in culturally sensitive design at the Indian Institute of Human Settlements, Bengaluru, said. “The issue extends beyond deliberately installed deterrents to changes in construction materials and landscape design.”
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Shilpa added that contemporary buildings are also built to not accommodate animals.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #30 of 30 (25 NOV)

📰 Hostile architecture: the design choices keeping wildlife out of urban India

📌 Published: 25 Nov 2026, 04:49:47 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: For animals and birds in India’s urban areas, hostile architecture takes many forms. ‘From spikes on ledges and nets over balconies to broken glass or spikes on compound walls that prevent animals from entering or perching,’ Shilpa Shirish, who specialises in culturally sensitive design at the Indian Institute of Human Settlements, Bengaluru, said

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: India’s cities and towns are seldom designed with their people in mind — and much less their animals. The green spaces within urban areas are also withdrawing as built area expands. And to deter animals from entering public spaces vouchsafed for humans, planners are turning to designs that increasingly have a collective name of their own: hostile architecture. New York-based architect James Petty defines hostile architecture as one where structures placed in public spaces are rendered “unusable in certain ways or by certain groups”. Slanting stone surfaces and barricades in 19th-century European cities to prevent public urination is one example. Another is anti-homeless architecture, visible as public benches with grooves and hand-rests in between to prevent people from lying down on them, and sloped seats at bus stops. For animals and birds in India’s urban areas, hostile architecture takes many other forms. “From spikes on ledges and nets over balconies to broken glass or spikes on compound walls that prevent animals from entering or perching,” Shilpa Shirish, who specialises in culturally sensitive design at the Indian Institute of Human Settlements, Bengaluru, said. “The issue extends beyond deliberately installed deterrents to changes in construction materials and landscape design.”

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Shilpa added that contemporary buildings are also built to not accommodate animals.

articles.title: A rare bird on stony rivers shows why Himalayan water needs its sediment
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The Himalayan rivers are home to several species that depend on rivers and their ecosystems, including fish, aquatic invertebrates like stonefly larvae and mayfly nymphs, and flora such as Himalayan alder and sea buckthorn along the banks and on the floodplains. When a river changes, all these environs, and their species, change as well

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: With its slate-grey plumage, curved bill, and black breast band, the ibisbill ( Ibidorhyncha struthersiii ) has adapted to life along the stony rivers of the Himalaya and the Tibetan Plateau. As seasons change, it migrates within the Greater, Middle, and Shivalik Himalaya, foraging among the pebbles and boulders for aquatic insects and larvae and nests on exposed gravel beds. Its survival depends not just on suitable climatic conditions but also on the river habitats where it can feed and breed. The ibisbill’s uncertain future echoes the growing threats to Himalayan rivers: protecting this rare bird also means preserving fragile ecosystems and vital water sources, and the biodiversity they sustain. Climate change is increasing glacier melt and early seasonal freezing, leading to more water in rivers, more sediments in those waters, and faster, more unstable flows. And for the ibisbill itself, the unsuitable climate causing these changes also means unsuitable habitats.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “We tend to picture rivers as fixed blue lines on a map, but Himalayan rivers are anything but static,” said Parv Kasana, a geologist and geoscientist at the Union Ministry of Earth Sciences. “They constantly move water and sediment, shift gravel bars, and split into braided streams.”

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #29 of 30 (25 NOV)

📰 A rare bird on stony rivers shows why Himalayan water needs its sediment

📌 Published: 25 Nov 2026, 06:49:36 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The Himalayan rivers are home to several species that depend on rivers and their ecosystems, including fish, aquatic invertebrates like stonefly larvae and mayfly nymphs, and flora such as Himalayan alder and sea buckthorn along the banks and on the floodplains. When a river changes, all these environs, and their species, change as well

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: With its slate-grey plumage, curved bill, and black breast band, the ibisbill ( Ibidorhyncha struthersiii ) has adapted to life along the stony rivers of the Himalaya and the Tibetan Plateau. As seasons change, it migrates within the Greater, Middle, and Shivalik Himalaya, foraging among the pebbles and boulders for aquatic insects and larvae and nests on exposed gravel beds. Its survival depends not just on suitable climatic conditions but also on the river habitats where it can feed and breed. The ibisbill’s uncertain future echoes the growing threats to Himalayan rivers: protecting this rare bird also means preserving fragile ecosystems and vital water sources, and the biodiversity they sustain. Climate change is increasing glacier melt and early seasonal freezing, leading to more water in rivers, more sediments in those waters, and faster, more unstable flows. And for the ibisbill itself, the unsuitable climate causing these changes also means unsuitable habitats.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “We tend to picture rivers as fixed blue lines on a map, but Himalayan rivers are anything but static,” said Parv Kasana, a geologist and geoscientist at the Union Ministry of Earth Sciences. “They constantly move water and sediment, shift gravel bars, and split into braided streams.”

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: The new U.S. tariffs must not erode India’s stand on a trade deal

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The latest U.S. tariffs on India are nothing more than a pressure tactic to push for the signing of a trade deal. The U.S. Trade Representative (USTR) has proposed to levy a tariff of 25% for India’s apparent use of strategic excess manufacturing capacity to the detriment of American industry. This is the second-highest tariff rate the USTR has applied across the 14 countries that it has taken action against. The pressure on India does not come from the 25% rate but from the 17% this could be reduced to if it signs a trade deal with the U.S. This latest action is yet another example of how, despite the frothiness of India-U.S. trade relations over the past year and a half, the actual substance has not changed. The 25% rate now proposed, which is net of existing tariffs, is nearly the same as the 26% rate that U.S. President Donald Trump had first announced when he unveiled his ‘Liberation Day’ reciprocal tariffs in April 2025. Indeed, it is exactly the same as the 25% tariff he finally imposed in July 2025, before he imposed an additional 25% for India’s Russian oil imports. The 17% rate is also only marginally lower than the 18% that the two countries had agreed on in their joint statement in February 2026. It is also just one percentage point lower than the tariffs on competitors such as Indonesia and Malaysia. The allegation of India having excess capacity does not hold water. Indeed, were India to have excess manufacturing capacity in any sector, it would be the Government of India that would be the first to announce it with great fanfare, instead of denying it as it did. After all, that has been its aim since 2014. Yet, even a basic assessment of India’s import dependence and the fact that manufacturing’s share in GDP is lower now than a decade ago shows that India is far from having excess manufacturing capacity in any sector. Further, higher tariffs are unlikely to reduce America’s imports of the goods from India that it does depend on. The USTR mentioned generic pharmaceuticals, telecommunication equipment, and renewable energy goods. The first two are items that India has developed expertise in, which is distinct from strategic excess capacity. A relatively small tariff disadvantage will not substantially erode the attractiveness of these Indian products. Renewable energy imports from India have swelled because the U.S. is reducing its purchases from China. Hanging over all of this are the 100% tariffs related to the purchase of Russian oil, which have only temporarily been paused. India has so far held off on signing a deal, and must go ahead with one only if it is convinced that the benefits at least equal the costs.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: USA / India / taxes and duties / manufacturing and engineering / industrial production / trade policy / Russia / oil and gas - upstream activities / Indonesia / Malaysia / imports / pharmaceutical / telecommunication equipment / renewable energy / China

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: Tamil Nadu should have followed Court order without backing Deepathoon claim

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: By defying the Supreme Court’s one-time direction to also light the ceremonial Karthigai Deepam at a stone pillar , claimed by Hindu groups to be a Deepathoon, atop the Thirupparankundram hills, the Tamil Nadu government has disregarded a constitutional body’s authority. Believed to be Lord Murugan’s first abode, the hills have, for centuries , witnessed an intersection of religious faiths, with occasional skirmishes leading to tense flare-ups and legal battles. They house the Arulmigu Subramaniya Swamy, Uchchi Pillaiyar and Kashi Viswanathar temples; Sultan Sikkandar Avulia Dargah; and also Jain beds. Historically, the lamp is lit near the Pillaiyar temple. In 1994-95, the Hindu Munnani precipitated matters, claiming that the moksha deepam (for departed souls) and Karthigai Deepam were being lit at the same place. It demanded the lamp be lit at a pillar, 50 metres from the Dargah. In multiple legal battles, successive governments, backed by hereditary priests (Sthaneeka Bhattars) , opposed the demand. Even in 1862 and 1912, courts had disallowed lamp lighting near the Dargah. The BJP and its affiliates have, since, aggressively weaponised the demand in the name of Hindu religious rights. Against this backdrop, last year, the Madras High Cour t’s Madurai Bench, relying on the 1931 Privy Council ruling on ownership of the hills, held that “for the sake of protecting its property, the [Subramania Swamy] temple management is obliged to light the festival lamp at the Deepathoon” . The DMK government defied the order. Later, a Division Bench upheld the verdict. While staying this order recently, the Supreme Court cited the festival’s proximity to permit the lamp to be lit at the Deepathoon this year alone , clarifying that this did not constitute “essential religious practice”. The State filed a review petition , arguing when no right is recognised prima facie, a direction altering the existing position lacks judicial foundation. On Karthigai Deepam day, November 24, with the review pending, the government walked a tightrope. The Collector assured the High Court of compliance. Yet, the lamp was lit only at the traditional spot . The Collector has now apologised to the Court, blaming the temple’s Board of Trustees for not authorising the proposed lighting team at the Deepathoon. The administration has thus attempted to distinguish its proclaimed intent to comply with judicial directions from customs governed by the trustees. But it remains exposed to the charge of colluding with the temple authorities to breach a judicial mandate. The Deepathoon may be a mischievous prop deployed by self-serving Hindu groups, but the pillar stands on temple property. The State could have permitted the limited lighting, leaving the onus on the Court, without endorsing the Deepathoon claim or compromising religious amity. A democracy can remain healthy only when its constitutional pillars do not collide with one another.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: court / Tamil Nadu / religion and belief / history / Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam / democracy / customs and tradition / constitution

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Few parties understand the arithmetic of the first-past-the-post (FPTP) system, and the necessity for alliances in States where they are minor players, better than the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) . The BJP has never shied away from partnerships with little ideological cohesion if they keep it electorally relevant. India’s FPTP system is unforgiving to smaller parties in a crowded polity if their support base is limited and dispersed. Votes translate into seats only if the support crosses a certain threshold. In Punjab , the BJP, despite its best efforts, has remained confined to sections of urban Hindu voters. Even after years of poaching leaders from the perennially fractious Congress , and after polling nearly a fifth of the vote in the 2024 general election without winning a seat, it realises that it cannot be relevant without a partner with a wider rural base. The Shiromani Akali Dal (Badal) walked out of the BJP -led National Democratic Alliance in 2020 over the Centre’s farm laws, which were later repealed, as the farmers’ agitation threatened its base in rural Punjab. But much water has flowed down the many rivers of the northern State since then. The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) has consolidated its hold in a crowded political space and is set to complete a full term. The Panthic vote, which used to be the SAD(B)’s core support base, has now fragmented. The SAD(B) appears to believe that it can regain ground only by expanding beyond its Panthic and rural constituencies, and that the farmers’ anger against the BJP is baggage from the past. It is this expedient calculation that now binds the two parties, despite six years of bitter attacks against each other. And it is also why the Union Home Minister, Amit Shah, has pointedly called the SAD(B) the “big brother” in Punjab after sealing the alliance. The SAD(B)’s calculation may not work out as well as it hopes it would. Farmers’ anger against the BJP-led Centre has not entirely dissipated in rural Punjab. In earlier alliances, the two parties transferred votes to each other effectively, partly because their voters had fewer alternatives. But a revived Congress and an entrenched AAP have shown that they can win over urban Hindu voters wary of the Akalis and rural voters who are not inclined to back parties allied with the BJP. That these two sections will simply add up for the alliance is not certain. At best, the alliance consolidates enough of the anti-AAP vote to make this a clear three-cornered contest. Punjab is a sensitive border State and one of India’s granaries. It is also among India’s most indebted States, with a stagnating agrarian economy and a government that has expanded welfare expenditure despite strained finances. It needs a serious competition of ideas on what welfare it can afford and how to revive growth. The SAD(B)-BJP alliance , with its Panthic appeal on one side and Hindu consolidation on the other, instead offers a rehash of familiar identity politics. With AAP failing to deliver on governance, and the Congress stuck in its old ways, Punjab’s voters will have to decide who they dislike the least.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: political parties / Bharatiya Janata Party / Punjab / voting / Indian National Congress / General Elections 2024 / Shiromani Akali Dal / Aam Aadmi Party / agriculture / economy / welfare

1. Core Context & Background: Karnataka needs a coherent policy on urban mobility

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: While Karnataka has spent years disputing motorcycle owners’ right to carry paying passengers, Bengaluru — with the dubious distinction of having one of the world’s highest travel times per unit distance — struggles with inadequate public transport capacity and lacklustre intermediate options. The Supreme Court ruling on November 20 to dismiss Karnataka’s appeal was thus straightforward, allowing motorcycles to be registered as transport vehicles. The State has often called bike taxis unsafe, yet has not improved the prospects of safer options. Earlier this year, the Centre for Science and Environment estimated the number of buses in urban centres nationwide to be 70% short of the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs benchmark and that 400 cities with populations between a lakh and 10 lakh altogether lacked organised bus services. In March, the BMTC reported a fleet of around 7,000 buses in Bengaluru, versus the 13,000 by 2025 envisaged by the Comprehensive Mobility Plan. Expanding the number of Metro stations also creates more demand for travel to and from stations, but the operating costs of the public transport corporation expected to serve that demand are not covered by the resulting increase in rail ridership. Overall, Karnataka has struggled to set up a consistent transport policy. An expert committee recommended against bike taxis in Bengaluru for first- and last-mile connectivity and in favour of better walking infrastructure and bicycle rentals in 2019, only for the State to launch the electric bike-taxi scheme in 2021, then rescind it in 2024 over safety concerns and drivers’ disputes. The market for short booked journeys is also dysfunctional. But while allowing bike taxis could temper autorickshaw fares, the State must investigate drivers’ operating costs, the difference between the paid and the received amounts, and prevent large platforms from exploiting the market. Finally, while the Union Road Transport Ministry has reported that 46.2% of all road deaths involved two-wheeler users, two-wheelers’ safety relative to autorickshaws and cabs, by the number and distance of journeys, is unclear. The State should require aggregators to report injuries and fatalities and investigate the consequences of drivers’ earnings being linked to the number of trips undertaken. The Union government’s 2025 Motor Vehicle Aggregator Guidelines already address passenger security, fares, and insurance while allowing States to authorise privately registered motorcycles through aggregators. Karnataka should exercise this additional power. A large national programme is required to address funding for public transport, which is necessary even when it is not immediately profitable.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Karnataka / scooters and motorbikes / public transport / court / population / urban planning / Bengaluru Metro / Electric vehicles / road accident / road transport / insurance

The proposed 50% increase in the number of seats in Parliament for different States, which was being discussed in various forums, did not necessarily ensure equity, he pointed out. Mr. Mishra said Odisha’s interests, or those of smaller States, should not be compromised. Until the details of the bill were made available, it would be difficult for the BJD to take a stand, the Rajya Sabha MP said.

Chief Minister V D Satheesan and Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala should clarify this,” he said. Mr. Jayarajan pointed out that even during the Emergency, newspapers, including Deshabhimani , were allowed in State prisons. At that time, certain news reports were blacked out due to press censorship to prevent inmates from accessing them, he said. There was no such situation now, and the present ban was a “primitive” move, he alleged. He also said prison rules stipulated that newspapers sent to inmates by their friends or relatives through sponsorships should be provided to them. The present restriction was against these rules, Jayarajan said, alleging that the Director General of Prisons would not have issued such a circular without the knowledge of the home minister. His criticism came a day after the Kerala Prisons and Correctional Services Department directed all jails in the state to stop purchasing and distributing newspapers and publications affiliated to political parties. In a circular issued on Thursday, Director General of Prisons S Sreejith said correctional institutions, which aim at the psychological and social rehabilitation of inmates, should ensure that the news and information made available to them were objective, truthful and free from political bias.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Publications serving as mouthpieces of political parties or organisations, or reflecting political interests, were not appropriate for distribution in prisons, the circular said.
